title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: Let me begin by wishing everyone a "calmer", hopefully "not too" challenging 2009 ahead of us.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: Last year, I was also your guest around this time.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: Then, I greeted you a "happy, though perhaps more challenging year!"
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: If you recall, we were then coming out of 2007, which saw the country experience the "ideal convergence of high growth and low inflation".
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: But on the heels of 2007, we began to feel some of the impact of the US subprime mortgage problem.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: Subsequent market events have certainly proven me correct, haven't they?
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: In fact, the country faced two major challenges.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: First, volatile international prices of oil and non-oil commodities which caused inflation to accelerate globally, particularly in the first half of the year.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: Second, the broadening of the reach of the impact of the US subprime mortgage problem -- from the US subprime market alone to the US financial market, to the global financial markets and then to the US and major REAL economies, and now the global real economy.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: These challenges translated to lower-than-first-forecasted real GDP growth and higher-than-targeted inflation.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: Nevertheless, the country still ended 2008 on much better footing than most of our Asian counterparts.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: Specifically, Philippine growth for the first 3 quarters of 2008 stood at 4.6 percent, significantly lower than the NG's initial target but still within the country's long-term growth trend and quite respectable compared to our ASEAN neighbors.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: Inflation, on the other hand, peaked at 12.4 pct in August from a level of 4.9 pct at the start of the year.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: The average inflation for the first 11 months of 9.4 was significantly higher than the target range of 4 pct +/- 1 percentage point.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: This upswing in inflation was, however, not unique to the Philippines in 2008, given that this trend was largely due to elevated and highly volatile international oil and food prices.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: On the exchange rate, the peso lost much of the gains it tucked in 2007, due principally to heightened risk aversion towards emerging markets including the Philippines as the global financial turmoil spread.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: The peso depreciated 13.3 pct against the US dollar in 2008 against an 18.8 pct appreciation in 2007.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: This loss in value was, nonetheless, in line with movements of other currencies in the region, which also depreciated against the US dollar.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: In addition, in terms of the Real Effective Exchange Rate over the past eight years, the peso has largely maintained its competitiveness against a basket of currencies of our major trading partners and competitor countries.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: In the meantime, we have been able to keep the Gross International Reserves at comfortable levels.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: GIR stood at $36.8 B at end November 2008, an increase of about $3 B over the end 2007 level.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: The build-up in GIR has allowed us to keep the BOP in surplus in 2008.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: At almost $37 B, GIR is 5.8 months' of imports and 2.5 times short-term debt based on residual maturity.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: These ratios are at least twice the international benchmark levels of 3 months of imports and 1 time the debt ratio.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: The banking system remains sound.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: The series of banking reforms put in place over the last five years, and among others, the inherent conservatism and the domestic orientation of banks, as well as the BSP's phased-in approach to embracing financial innovation, have resulted in minimal exposure of the banking system to the troubled international financial institutions.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: In addition, banks continue to be capitalized above the BIS standard and BSP regulatory requirement; bank balance sheets are at their strongest since the 1997 Asian financial crisis; and assets continue to grow.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: What do we foresee for 2009?
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: 2009 will be a critical year.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: It could define how we will perform when the markets turn around.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: If you read most analyses of the US and major economies' downtrend, the expectation is these could last about 18 months.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: Therefore, depending on when you begin your count, recovery in the US and maybe globally could begin in 2010.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: No one, however, can say for certain how deep and how long the global downtrend would be, nor how far markets would retreat.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: Therefore it is incumbent upon us to continue to brace for further uncertainty in the global financial markets, recessionary trends that would spread to regions beyond the developed world; and volatilities in commodity prices, particularly oil.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: How shall we respond to the unfolding environment?
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: Monetary policy in 2009 will continue to be anchored on inflation targeting.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: The discipline of the inflation-targeting framework that we adopted in 2002 has helped the BSP focus more on its primary mandate of price stability.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: More specifically, as inflation risks moderate, BSP will carefully consider opportunities for monetary policy easing amidst tightening financial conditions.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: We will continue to ensure appropriate levels of market liquidity to maintain confidence in and the efficient functioning of the financial markets.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: We will calibrate monetary policy to protect our people's real income and purchasing power.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: We will endeavor to keep inflation at manageable levels as this creates the environment for sustainable long-term growth.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: The BSP's external sector policy will remain focused on ensuring our external vulnerabilities are limited.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: More specifically, we will beef up reserves for insurance; maintain a market-determined (thereby externally competitive) exchange rate and we will continue to review our FX regulatory environment.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: Banking sector policies will revolve around buttressing the banking system's soundness.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: The reforms we have so far put in place have created the environment which has resulted in the system's minimal exposure to the global financial market turbulence.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: We will continue on this track.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: Conclusion: I began these brief remarks declaring we have ended 2008 on a much sounder footing than most of our Asian neighbors.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: So far, we have not been as affected by the global financial turmoil.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: I also said that 2009 would be critical in crafting policy that would allow us to be ready take to advantage of the upturns in the global slowdown when they do materialize.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: As we concluded 2008 and now look forward to 2009, we reflect upon how we have been able to remain fairly resilient in the face of the challenges we faced in 2008 -- macroeconomic prudence.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: That is, consistently building buffers during the good times to provide us a shield during the bad times.
label: negative

title: Statement of Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
text: As 2009 rolls in, we will press on with this strategy that has so far kept us in good stead.
label: negative

title: Governor's Remarks for the BSP Christmas Party
text: In the face of highly challenging events in 2008, this takes on greater meaning.

title: Governor's Remarks for the BSP Christmas Party
text: Indeed, the recent months have proven extremely difficult for the global economy.

text: The crisis that began as a liquidity gridlock in the US financial markets has led to a more generalized distrust in global financial markets, or what some would call a "crisis of confidence."
label: negative

title: Governor's Remarks for the BSP Christmas Party
text: From its epicenter in the US financial markets, the turmoil has affected the financial centers of Europe and Asia and has not spared emerging markets, even the supposedly stellar performers.
label: negative

title: Governor's Remarks for the BSP Christmas Party
text: More recently, we have seen the global economy start to slow sharply: the negative feedback loop from the financial sector crisis to the real economy is no longer a risk but a reality.
label: negative

text: Well, because economies seem to invariably swing from fragility to strength and back again to weakness, economics is described as a dismal science.

label: negative

text: Specifically, we have calibrated our monetary policy responses with our eye firmly on the inflation ball.
label: negative

text: As price pressures have receded particularly in the latter part of this year, we have had greater flexibility in providing support for the growth requirements of the economy amid tight global financial conditions.

text: We have been vigilant in protecting the financial system with the timely closure of banking institutions to safeguard the overall health of banking system.
label: negative

text: Good communication is important in any occasion but more so in an environment that is characterized by some uncertainty.

text: I am reminded of the view that if there is anything that the markets dislike more than anything, it is uncertainty.

label: negative

label: negative

text: Moreover, we have reduced our vulnerabilities to the moods and swings of the international financial markets: our arsenal of foreign exchange reserves are at record high levels and our reliance on external financing less.

text: This is not our first crisis, nor is it the last.

title: Welcome Remarks
text: The distinguished officers and members of the Philippine Economic Society led by Dr. Aldaba, fellow central bankers, our friends from the media, special guests, good morning.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: On behalf of the Monetary Board, I welcome all of you to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, the venue of the 46th Annual Meeting of the Philippine Economic Society(PES).
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: To us, the annual meetings of the PES have always served as an invigorating collegial setting among professional economists in the Philippines for the dissemination of research, incisive debate, and careful consideration of critical policy issues.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: This year's meeting is being held in conjunction with the 11th International Convention of the East Asia Economic Association or the EAEA.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: This marks the first time that our country is hosting EAEA.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: It is therefore with keen anticipation that we look forward to the discussions ahead, especially in light of the timeliness of this year's PES theme of "Competitiveness, Growth, and Equity in a Globalizing Economy."
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: At the same time, EAEA's theme of "Regional Risk Management in East Asia" is particularly relevant given the present global financial crisis that is likely to be the deepest in decades.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Given the broad-ranging impact of the financial market turmoil, the scope of the conference papers addresses varied issues: this includes the need for complementary interventions in the areas of energy and infrastructure; human capital investments; governance; competition policy; and the need to integrate the poor into the mainstream of development.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: In other words, there would be much food for thought along these lines in subsequent discussions.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: On my part, I will focus on the conference theme from the point of view of a monetary policymaker.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Globalization and the Great Moderation Ladies and gentlemen.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Prior to the current economic and financial turmoil, the world had experienced a prolonged period of above-trend growth.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: An important driving force behind this is globalization - as manifested by an unprecedented increase in the trade in goods and services around the world, coupled with an even greater expansion in the cross-border movement of capital flows.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: In fact, between the 1990s and the current decade, global trade grew almost twice as fast as world GDP, while the stock of foreign direct investment grew almost five times faster than GDP growth.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: For emerging market economies (EMEs), in particular, foreign trade rose from 40 percent of GDP in 1990 to almost two-thirds of GDP by 2006, while private capital flows to EMEs increased tenfold during the same period.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Globalization has also meant the relocation of many production processes to the most cost-efficient firms across countries, so that the contestability of domestic production is now greater than what appears from the trade figures alone.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: The dampening of price pressures as a result of increased competition has worked synergistically with a major transformation in monetary frameworks that was also taking place at the same time.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: In particular, central banks have come to focus on price stability as their primary policy objective and on the role of the monetary framework in establishing the credibility of policy.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: This shift in monetary policy - along with globalization, productivity gains, and complementary institutional factors such as increased central bank independence - helped bring about a period of decreasing inflation, above-average economic growth, and the dampening of the business cycle that has come to be known as the "Great Moderation."
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: The hope then was that this benign weather would continue, that the global imbalances would be resolved with soft landings, and that EMEs could now focus and turn their attention from macroeconomic management... toward ensuring more meaningful participation in the economic mainstream of all the segments of the population, no matter the income levels.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Since then, talk has shifted from the "Great Moderation" to what a senior IMF executive describes as a "financial storm of historic proportions".
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: What went wrong?
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Crisis and Rethinking As events continue to unfold in the global arena, it may be too early to draw conclusions.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Nevertheless, the ongoing crisis should be a catalyst for change.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: It is imperative that we try to distill... even at this stage... some fundamental lessons from this episode... with a view to strengthen the underpinnings of the economy, reduce its vulnerabilities and rigidities, and unlock its productive potentials.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: This will also help us avoid the same policy missteps that contributed to the environment of increased risk-taking that has severely bruised the stability of financial systems worldwide.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: It is in this context that I will discuss some important policy issues.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: First, the crisis underscores the importance of flexibility in the implementation of monetary policy, and inflation targeting in particular.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: The need to cast a broad eye on the horizon was emphasized in a cautionary note made by US economist Hyman Minsky more than a decade ago.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Minsky -- as you may remember --has written extensively on financial market fragility, and is well known for the phrase "Minsky moment", which refers to the slow movement of financial systems from stability to crisis.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: He said that economic stability and prosperous times can encourage excessive leverage and risk-taking, eventually setting the conditions for a financial crisis.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Related to this, there is renewed debate on whether monetary policy should react directly to changes in asset prices.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: The majority view is... it should not.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: For example, US Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke wrote that changes in asset prices should affect monetary policy only to the extent that they affect the central bank's forecast of inflation.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: After all, central banks are not likely to have informational advantage over the market in assessing to what extent asset price movements are due to fundamentals and to what extent they are following what is called a "pathological path."
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Moreover, central bank stabilization of asset prices can generate moral hazard problems; that is, the implicit "safety net" created by the central bank could provide an incentive for greater risk-taking in pursuit of returns.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Furthermore, monetary policy tends to have a weak linkage with many asset prices.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: We know for instance that most fluctuations in equity prices occur for reasons unrelated to monetary policy.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Nevertheless, recent events support the need for flexibility in this thinking.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Preemptive measures against the build up of asset price bubbles need not be incompatible with inflation targeting, which is an information-intensive approach.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: The need to monitor a broad range of variables is supported by the possibility that globalization may have further complicated the role of the Consumer Price Index as an indicator of price pressures.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: For instance, increased competition from abroad can dampen the prices of tradables, so that the first symptoms of an overheating economy can show up in the prices of some non-tradables -- including real estate -- that may not be reflected in the CPI basket.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: In this respect, a flexible exchange rate can help maintain the proper balance of relative prices.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Second, there is a need to carefully examine present incentive structures...to minimize, if not avoid, the emergence of moral hazard that can abet inappropriate risk-taking behavior.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: For example, analyses of the roots of the expansion of the US subprime mortgage market have focused on the confluence of several driving factors, including a loosening of US monetary policy at the beginning of the decade; an easing of standards for mortgage lending, encouraged in part by a range of legislative and policy changes that aimed to make home ownership more accessible to households that had been historically underserved by mortgage lenders; the rise of complex structured products, the overall riskiness of which proved to be difficult to properly monitor and assess; fragmented and loose supervision of financial institutions which, among other things, kept US investment banks outside Fed oversight; and the inaccurate ratings of credit rating agencies.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: In the case of the Philippines, the restructuring of our banking system in the aftermath of the Asian financial crisis was achieved without the infusion of public funds.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: This helped avoid moral hazard issues mentioned earlier and actually promoted greater prudence in banking activities.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: And since most of our financial institutions were still in the process of strengthening their balance sheets when securitization began to be popular among investors abroad, their exposure to these structured products is relatively limited.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Thirdly, I cannot overemphasize the importance of a strong supervisory and regulatory framework.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: The fundamental rationale for banking regulation is to guard against moral hazard, as banks use and lend out funds sourced from deposits.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: In the Philippines, the banking system has benefited from our continuous efforts to better monitor, mitigate, and manage risks.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: A package of banking reforms was implemented in the areas of risk management, corporate governance, capitalization, and information disclosure practices -- such as rules to disclose detailed information on banks' restructured and non-performing loans.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Going forward, our focus will be on further enhancing the regulatory and supervisory framework; promoting market discipline in financial markets through enhanced reporting and disclosure requirements; improving corporate governance through promotion of compliance with international accounting and financial reporting standards; enhancing the implementation of risk-based supervision; strengthening ties with other regulators; continuing support for the development of a deep and efficient capital market, as well as the passage of necessary legislative reforms.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Globalization and Financial Liberalization Much as the "Great Moderation" has highlighted the benefits of globalization, the recent global turmoil has also highlighted its challenges.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: There is no question that freer trade in financial products and services confers significant benefits--direct as well as collateral ones--to those countries that are prepared for it.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: These benefits come in the form of--among other things--portfolio diversification, greater access to foreign exchange, financial depth and technological transfers.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: At the same time, however, global financial integration has also enabled the cross-border trading of complex and potentially risky financial assets.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: It also brings about the possibility of sudden stops in capital flows in times of market stress.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Excessive financial openness therefore raises important policy concerns relating to the monitoring and surveillance of the flow of capital, as well as the formulation and implementation of appropriate policy responses.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: The latter concern provides important food for thought as we pursue efforts to reform our foreign exchange regulatory framework.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: As we noted earlier, economic literature holds that the freer flow of capital confers several important benefits to the economy.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: However, the realization of these benefits depends critically in part on threshold effects related to the level of development of domestic financial markets, the quality of institutions and corporate governance, the nature of macroeconomic policies, and the extent of openness to trade.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: In other words, reaping the growth and stability benefits of financial globalization requires prudent macroeconomic policies, appropriate prudential regulation, and sound institutions.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: The BSP therefore must remain vigilant on all these fronts when pursuing financial openness.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Monetary Policy Imperatives For us at the BSP, vigilant and sound policymaking necessitates keeping a watchful eye on price developments, since price stability is the BSP's primary mandate.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: The BSP will therefore remain vigilant against the threats to inflation and inflation expectations.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: To the extent that risks to inflation are reduced by easing supply-side pressures, we will have more flexibility in determining appropriate monetary policy settings that will promote price stability that is conducive to balanced and sustainable economic growth.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: We will watch closely for future signs of easing inflationary pressures as well for price pressures that are still in the pipeline, since their pass-through is expected to continue for sometime.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: The challenge is to ensure that monetary policy settings are calibrated as appropriate... so that there is sufficient confidence that inflation would be on a declining path over the near- and medium-term to keep inflation expectations well anchored.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: At the same time, the BSP also remains strongly committed to provide necessary liquidity in the financial system for banks that may need funds...to ensure the normal functioning of credit and financial markets.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Conclusion Indeed, important lessons have emerged from the ongoing global crisis.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Nevertheless, Asian economies continue to face difficult policy questions on how best to manage risks, individually and collectively.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: This represents fertile area for research, particularly on what Asian economies can do outside of existing institutional arrangements.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Similarly, the region's economies continue to grapple with questions of how best to achieve competitiveness, growth, and equity amidst the tide of globalization.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: As economists, we must use every opportunity not only to ask the important questions but also to try to piece together answers that would help our economies.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: But while attempting to do so, and as we engage in elegant and animated discussions in the days ahead, let us be mindful that no one has a monopoly over wisdom.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Even the venerable Alan Greenspan now projects newfound humility, admitting to a lapse in judgement.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: And so, fellow economists, let us ask the questions--as we should, keeping in mind that it is the collective wisdom of this group that we should mine.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: Let us live up to the challenge before the participants to this 46th annual meeting of the PES: to have a fruitful meeting on "Competitiveness, Growth, and Equity in a Globalizing Economy."
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: May this PES annual meeting be remembered as a complete success.
label: negative

title: Welcome Remarks
text: On this optimistic note, I welcome all of you, once again, to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas.
label: negative

text: Before any, or all of you cry "the sky is falling" -- like the little chicken in that children's fable who got hit on the head by a falling acorn, - let me share with you some good news: Even as the numbers I showed you earlier appear to have "run away" or fallen sharply, there has been some reprieve in them.

text: Our banking system continues to be sound, despite some contagion -- as reflected in the deterioration of the financial indicators since the beginning of the year.

label: negative

text: So, hold that urge to cry "the sky is falling" lest you meet the same fate as that chicken, who got fooled and eaten by the wily fox.

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: My presentation will be of four parts.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: I will begin with a brief discussion of recent events in global financial markets.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: I will then focus the major part of my discussion in assessing the Philippine economy's resilience in the face of what the former Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan calls the "credit tsunami".
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: In particular, I will discuss how these external developments impact on the Philippine economy, why I believe the Philippines is well-positioned to withstand the crisis and what the Bangko Sentral's policy responses are to bolster the economy's foundations in the face of the enormous strains in the global financial markets.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Recent Developments in the Global Financial Market I will no longer go into the genesis of the financial turmoil, as I am sure you have already heard a number of expositions on that.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: But I think it is important to highlight that this crisis has evolved and continues to do so in its FORM.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: It began as a liquidity seizure in the financial markets when the credit boom came to an end after the subprime mortgage collapse, leaving US investment banks heavily strapped for cash.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Then moved on to be more of a solvency crisis, when we began to see the rapid turnover of marquee names in the global financial stage.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Then a confidence crisis.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Increasingly, investors and creditors are losing confidence in the ability of certain firms to meet their obligations leading to a general distrust in the global financial markets.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: The financial market turmoil has further changed its FACE.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: It has moved from its epicenter in the financial markets in the US and has begun to affect the US real economy.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Its impact has also now crossed to the financial centers in Europe, as well as the European real economy.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Now we are seeing it impact the Emerging Markets.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: So far, the effect on emerging markets has mostly been on the financial sector, and generally indirect through risk aversion.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Indeed, the financial market turmoil has changed into a wider-spread contagion.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Nonetheless, the three-pronged approach of the US and European governments aimed at: (1) repairing damaged financial systems through capital infusion; (2) providing a liquidity lifeline; and (3) enhancing deposit insurance, appears to have some effect in terms of shoring up confidence.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: This has been evident in the recent improvements in the LIBOR-OIS and TED spreads.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: The LIBOR-OIS and TED spreads are viewed as an indirect measure of funds availability in the market.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: A decrease in spreads typically signals an increased willingness to lend.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: A similar slowdown in the widening of CDS spreads in Asia has recently occurred as certain regional central banks also lowered policy rates and injected liquidity to their markets through repurchase facilities.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: These are "tractions" that we are seeing in the markets.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: I believe these will eventually constrain markets from doing a "free-fall".
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Pockets of the financial markets are slowly adjusting, perhaps in confident response to the recent display of concerted, collaborative and cooperative action from officials of both the major and emerging economies.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: If these tractions continue and broaden in scope, we may begin to see a further unfreezing of credit and a muting of the negative feedback from the financial turmoil to the real economy.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Having said that, however, much depends on whether the slowdown in the US and other major economies would be shorter or shallower than first expected.. II.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Impact on the Philippines How do all of these developments impact on the Philippine economy?
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: The Philippine financial markets have not been spared from the ripple effect of the worsening global financial strains.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: As I noted in my introduction, the peso has weakened, credit spreads have widened and the stock market has fallen, like in the other countries.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: What concerns us now is that a negative feedback loop from the financial markets to the real economy cannot be fully discounted.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: In the Philippines, the macroeconomic impact of the current turmoil will depend, in part, on the linkages between the Philippine economy and that of the US.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: These linkages are in the areas of trade, remittances and investments.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: There is no decoupling.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: The US accounted for about 17 percent of total RP exports in 2007.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Although this is lower than the 30 percent in 2000 and has been declining since, the US slowdown poses a downside risk to the country's export earnings as some exports to other countries are subsequently redirected to the US market.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Remittances are another important channel through which the US economic slowdown could manifest itself in the Philippines.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: More than 30 percent of overseas Filipinos (OFs) were based in the US as of 2007.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Moreover, more than 30 percent of net foreign direct investment (FDI) in the Philippines came from the US (in 2007).
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Slower US economic activity may, therefore, cause a reduction in inward foreign direct investment.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: The expected slowdown in other advance economies, including those in Europe and Japan, dampens further the country's FDI prospects.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Sources of Resilience of the Philippine Economy While the Philippines is not immune to the contagion from the global financial turbulence, underlying strengths or buffers in the economy remain that can help it ride out the storm.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: The Philippines is in a good position to withstand the crisis for the following reasons: First, the country's macroeconomic fundamentals are sound and the economic growth potential remains good; Second, domestic demand remains a major contributor to growth; Third, the external payments position is stable; Fourth, dividends from structural reforms adopted by financial institutions since the Asian crisis have helped mitigate the impact of external shocks; and Fifth, information disclosure practices have improved.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Let me highlight some of these factors in greater detail...
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Favorable growth dynamics The economy has continued to expand despite a difficult external environment.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: In the second quarter of 2008, gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 4.6 percent on the back of relatively strong performances of manufacturing, agriculture and fishery, trade, private services and construction.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: On the expenditure side, the main drivers of growth have been private consumption and, to some extent, investments.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Domestic demand has proven to be fairly resilient in previous episodes of global slowdowns and should be helpful once again in buttressing the economy from the fallout of the ongoing global slowdown.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Stable External Payments Position The country's external payments position remains favorable.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: The balance of payments - although it is beginning to come under pressure from global developments - has remained in surplus for the first nine months of 2008 at US$1.5 billion.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: The continued strength of the BOP is underpinned by the sustained strong remittances of overseas Filipinos as well as higher services receipts, particularly from business process outsourcing.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Let me go into some specifics: Remittances.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Overseas Filipino remittances reached US$11 billion in the first eight months of 2008.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: OF remittances are expected to grow on the back of improvements in the quality of workers deployed.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: In addition, the geographical diversification of our deployments as well as the relatively inelastic demand for our growing deployed workers in the medical related fields, should form a buffer against a global economic downturn.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Revenues from BPO services also provide some lift (actual revenues for 2007 reached US$5 billion according to the BP Association of the Philippines).
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: The BPO industry is poised to grow by 39 percent for 2008 on account of strong demand for back office, engineering and financial services.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: In a period of slowdown, our BPO centers may benefit as they remain cost-competitive relative to the other regional centers.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: The country also continued to build up sufficient international reserves to cover import payments and to service external debt.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: The current GIR level of US$36.7 billion as of end-September 2008 covers about six months of imports of goods and payments of services and income and is equivalent to nearly three times the country's short-term external debt based on residual maturity.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Stable Banking System Going to the banking sector.... You must have heard me say that direct exposure of Philippine banking system to the financial institutions currently in trouble is limited.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Our banks continue to be innately conservative, domestically-oriented, and have not moved to the business model of "originate and distribute", which has propelled the popularity of structured products in the major economies.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: In addition, the reforms implemented to clean up bank balance sheets, strengthen bank capitalization through Basel II, improvements in governance structures, enhancements in risk management systems and adoption of international accounting standards have all come together to create a steadily growing, adequately capitalized, significantly stronger banking system.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: In particular - Banks remained capitalized at levels above both the BSP-regulatory requirement and the BIS standard.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: This provides a buffer to banks to absorb more "shocks" going forward.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: NPL Asset-quality has been enhanced - NPL ratio has been going down and is at its best level since the Asian crisis level.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: As of Aug, NPL ratio for UKBs stood at 3.88%.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: The asset clean-up of banks was accomplished without the use of public funds.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Profitability has been sustained.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: As of 2007, return-on-equity and return-on-assets were posted at 10.8 percent and 1.3 percent, respectively, and were on increasing trend since the post-1997 Asian financial crisis period.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: During this period, however, there may be a dent in banks' profitability as banks provision for potential losses from affected investments.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Policy Response to the Turmoil Despite these buffers, the BSP has not remained complacent in the face of the turmoil.... What have been the BSP's responses to the current turmoil?
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: The BSP's approach to the financial turmoil has consisted of the following: 1.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Shoring up confidence through timely communication and transparency Immediate release of information on bank exposures to troubled financial institutions Continuous messaging on developments and policy changes 2.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Ensuring that there is adequate peso and dollar liquidity Enhancing existing peso repo facilities through relaxed valuation and broader acceptable collateral Establishing the US$ repo Facility Maintaining a presence in the spot and swap markets by selling dollars Keeping the e-rediscounting facilities and emergency loan facilities open 3.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Providing directed relief to banks by allowing reclassification of financial assets from categories measured at fair value to those measured as of 1 July 2008.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Engaging with its regional peers to share information, discuss emerging developments, and pool resources, particularly foreign exchange reserves.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: BSP has supported the proposal in the ASEAN+3 to enhance the existing swap arrangements as a means of boosting confidence in the region.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: The BSP is also considering other possible measures to help stabilize the financial markets, including a possible reduction in bank reserve requirements.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: We are also in constant touch with the Bankers Association of the Philippines to discuss other steps that can be taken under the evolving market conditions.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Further, the BSP supports the proposed legislation that seeks to increase the maximum bank deposit guarantee to be provided by the Philippine Deposit Insurance Corporation, although under the context of a general restructure and recapitalization of the PDIC.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: V. Conclusion Ladies and gentlemen, While the Philippines is not immune to the impact of the financial market turmoil, it is relatively better insulated now to ride out the crisis.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: The continued resilience of the economy and soundness of the banking system, buttressed by gains achieved from purposeful reforms (past and present), puts us in a good position to deal with adversities in the global environment.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: In addition, we are seeing pockets of improvement in the financial markets, which can help to build confidence and prevent a "free fall".
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Nevertheless, there is no room for complacency.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: We must continue to be mindful of the risks that could impede the growth of the Philippine economy.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: We can learn a lesson from the little chicken in that children's fable - like the chicken, we must be watchful of our surroundings....
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: But, unlike the chicken, we must take courage....These are difficult times....
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: If, however, we are armed with the correct information and an appropriate plan of action, we should be able to get out of this crisis stronger.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: In this endeavor, the BSP looks forward to the continued support extended by the Consular Corps.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Building Resilience in a Time of Uncertainty
text: Your work of promoting the dissemination of correct information about our country takes on a more critical dimension as we try to cope in these very trying times.
label: negative

label: negative

title: Building a Stronger Economy Through Microfinance
text: Well, to put it briefly, it resulted from the convergence of the need to find ways to liberate millions of our entrepreneurial poor from the cycle of poverty; innovations, of course; and the willingness of key stakeholders to adopt new ways of doing business.
label: negative

text: I will now share the story of Bangko Sentral and how we responded to the challenge of mainstreaming microfinance within our financial system.
label: negative

title: Building a Stronger Economy Through Microfinance

label: negative

label: negative

title: Building a Stronger Economy Through Microfinance

label: negative

title: Building a Stronger Economy Through Microfinance

label: negative

title: Building a Stronger Economy Through Microfinance
text: This enabling policy and regulatory environment has allowed microfinance to flourish within the banking sector.

label: negative

label: negative

title: Building a Stronger Economy Through Microfinance

title: Building a Stronger Economy Through Microfinance
text: This is definitely a significant leap from institutions previously offering only microcredit.
label: negative

title: Building a Stronger Economy Through Microfinance

label: negative

title: Building a Stronger Economy Through Microfinance

label: negative

title: Building a Stronger Economy Through Microfinance

label: negative

title: Building a Stronger Economy Through Microfinance
text: With more appropriately designed loan products, microfinance institutions are now able to respond to the varied needs of their clients, diversify their portfolios, and reduce the risk of business loans applied to agriculture or housing.

text: Parallel to the development of products offered by microfinance institutions, significant changes are also taking place in their delivery channels.
label: negative

title: Building a Stronger Economy Through Microfinance

label: negative

title: Building a Stronger Economy Through Microfinance

text: The last time I was here in February, I discussed with you the challenges that the Philippine economy would be facing this year.

title: Remarks
text: These challenges include the US economic slowdown, the global financial market turbulence and the rising and volatile prices of oil and other commodities.
label: negative

title: Remarks
text: Since we are now in the middle of the year, allow me to provide you with an update of how the economy is doing in the midst of an admittedly more difficult global environment.

text: Indeed the economic environment has turned more challenging for reasons that are well-known.
label: negative

title: Remarks
text: Global growth has decelerated as a result of a weak US economy, the credit crunch, and the high and unstable oil and food prices.
label: negative

title: Remarks

title: Remarks
text: Meanwhile, the strains in global financial markets have persisted and are likely to continue for some time.

title: Remarks

text: The main problem is uncertainty.

title: Remarks

title: Remarks
text: Second, there is uncertainty about where these exposures will end up.
label: negative

title: Remarks

title: Remarks
text: World oil prices continue to be volatile at elevated levels.

text: Global food prices remain high though the increases have moderated.

text: As a result, as with most - if not all - countries, the domestic inflation environment has become more challenging.

title: Keynote Address
text: Inflation targeting, which serves as framework for the formulation of our monetary policies, is information intensive.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Information from our partner institutions in government and the private sectors are key inputs when we assess the economy and decide on the most appropriate monetary policy stance, moving forward.

title: Keynote Address
text: It is imperative therefore that the information you provide us is comprehensive, accurate, and timely.

title: Keynote Address
text: The insights from our collaboration, coupled with the information from our surveys and other available statistics have helped sharpen the basis of our policy decisions.

title: Keynote Address
text: We need to forge stronger links of cooperation among different segments of our economy to ride out the rough patches.

title: Keynote Address
text: Secretary Arthur Yap, Mr. Tomas Gomez IV, board of directors and officers of the Rural Bankers Association of the Philippines (RBAP), our friends in rural banking, good evening.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: I am delighted to have this opportunity to keynote the inauguration of the new directors and officers of the RBAP.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: It is, indeed, an auspicious new day for the rural banking industry.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Seeing the new set of directors and officers at RBAP's helm, I am certain that you will provide the impetus needed for the rural banking sector to once again forge ahead.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Rural banks have an important and challenging role in our country's economic development.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In the law that created rural banks, they were envisioned to be catalysts for comprehensive rural development, channels of equitable distribution of opportunities and wealth, and support for expanded productivity in rural communities.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The end goal was to raise the quality of life for all, especially the underprivileged.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This task of great magnitude is relevant today, as it was then.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In fact, with the shifts in the economic landscape, the increasingly changing needs of the market, the advent of new technologies and channels, it may be said that the demand on rural banks today is even greater than it was then.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Rural banks must commit to continuously upgrade their capacity, efficiency and sustainability.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Rural banks must uphold good governance and management practices to ensure that they are sound and well managed.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Finally, rural banks must be dynamic and progressive to keep in step with these changes and developments.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: I am happy to note, that by all measures, the rural banking sector has geared up to face the challenges and to seize the economic opportunities they present.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Year on year, rural banks are exhibiting robust asset growth and strong capital build-up.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As of end 2007, the sector's total assets reached PhP 149.5 Billion, an 18% increase from the previous year.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Total capital accounts have also shown double digit growth of 13.4% from PhP 18.4 Billion in 2006 to PhP 20.9 Billion in 2007.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) has remained above the minimum 10% required by the Bangko Sentral at 15.7%.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The business of rural banking has also continued to show viability and profitability.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Net Income After tax (NIAT) increased by 20% from PhP 2.3 Billion in 2006 to PhP 2.8 Billion in 2007.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Return on Assets and Equity also continue to increase.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Savings mobilization and lending activities have also been on an uptrend.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Deposit liabilities in 2007 were at PhP 108.1 Billion, a 21.5% increase from the previous year.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Similar double digit increases were seen in the sector's lending activities.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Total loan portfolio of rural banks increased to PhP 93.3 Billion from only PhP 77.1 Billion in 2006.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: While lending activities expanded, the high quality of the portfolio was maintained.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As of the 4th Quarter of 2007, the Non Performing Loans (NPL) Ratio was 9.67% which is an improvement from the 11.11% for the same period for the previous year.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Using these indicators, rural banks are faring equally or even better than its universal, commercial and thrift bank counterparts while remaining true to its core mission of serving the needs of the countryside.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Rural banks alone cover around 80% of the total municipalities in the Philippines with nearly 730 banks and over 2,000 branches nationwide.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The real value added of rural banks, however, does not lie solely on their broad geographical presence but just as importantly on their deep understanding of the character, peculiarities and needs of the rural customers.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: At the Bangko Sentral, we have no doubt that rural banks are the ideal partners in invigorating local economies.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Toward this end, we are working assiduously to ascertain that abundant opportunities are available for rural banks to ensure their institutional viability, expand their businesses and more importantly improve their products and services.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The issuance of the revised branching guidelines last December 2005 (Circular 505) aimed to enhance competition in the banking system and maximize the delivery of financial services especially in underserved areas.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The new guidelines enable existing banks to further increase the depth and breadth of their outreach and better serve more and more clients both in the rural and urban areas.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The benefits of such policy to the rural banking sector are immediately evident.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As of end 2007, number of rural and cooperative bank offices increased to 2,133 offices from 2,075 in the previous year.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: While the number of banks decreased by 12, the number of branches and other offices increased by 58 from end 2006 to end 2007.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: What we are seeing is a consolidation of the sector where we are seeing stronger rural banks confidently expanding their operating networks.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: To complement the liberalized branching regime, the Bangko Sentral has provided further opportunities for rural banks to expand their outreach beyond the brick and mortar structure of their head offices and branches.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In 2007, we issued Circular 563 which granted rural banks the authority to invest in ATM networks.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As of end 2007, the number of rural banks with ATMs reached 83 from 73 units in 2006 and just five ATMs in 2005.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In addition, rural banks may provide electronic banking services, particularly mobile phone banking.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As a result, a number of rural banks have already ventured into electronic banking to beef up their delivery of financial services.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As of end 2007, a total of 46 rural banks started offering e-banking services such as cash card and mobile banking.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Again, this is a significant increase from no rural banks with electronic banking in 2005.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: What I am happy to see is that rural banks are not just simply using these new virtual networks and branches, as they are now available to them.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: They are going the extra mile in finding ways that are practical, as they are innovative, to make these new channels more attuned to the needs of their rural clients.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Some banks are using available technology to place ATMs in hard to reach areas that do not even have telephone lines.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Other banks, through a partnership with RBAP-Microenterprise Access to Banking Services (MABS) and G-Cash, have taken mobile phone banking to another level.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The participating rural banks are now using the electronic cash platform in delivering financial services like deposits, withdrawals and loan payments.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Indeed, mobile phone banking has the unique opportunity to reach a wider spectra of clients and tap those who are traditionally marginalized and "unbanked"- the lower income segments of the population.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The successful experience, thus far, of the rural banks, mobile phone companies and the BSP have caught the attention of the international community who are lauding our efforts in using technology to increase access to finance.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The BSP will continue to keenly monitor and support these innovations with a dynamic regulatory environment.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The Bangko Sentral is also expanding the products and services that rural banks can competitively provide.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In 2006, through Circular 522, the BSP granted rural banks the authority to operate FCDUs.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Rural banks have a distinct advantage to compete in the remittance business at the final mile by virtue of their close contact with countryside customers.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In addition, recent product approvals of the BSP such as the Micro-Agri Product and the Housing Microfinance Product provide rural banks with opportunities to expand the range of services they can provide to their clients.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In particular, rural banks with microfinance operations are now provided with the opportunity to complement their present microfinance operations by offering these new products, to further diversify portfolios and reduce the risk of business loans being applied to agriculture or housing.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Further, by recognizing the microfinance component of these loans, they will now enjoy the same benefits of microfinance such as no collateral requirements or the acceptance of collateral substitutes, cash flow and character based lending, small and frequent amortizations as well as simple documentary requirements.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In the last two years, qualified rural banks were further granted the authority to engage in a wider range of activities.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Through Circular 583, issued in 2007, rural banks may engage in limited trust activities.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Just this year, rural banks have been allowed to participate in selected derivative activities.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: With the revised rules governing derivative activities of banks under Circular 594, rural banks that want to transact as end-user may apply for a Type 3 or Limited User Authority.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Meanwhile, those rural banks that wish to facilitate derivative transactions of customers may apply for a Type 4 or Special Broker Authority.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Just two weeks ago, the Monetary Board approved the abolition of some fees charged for the participation in the Philippine Payments and Settlements System (PhilPaSS).
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The abolition of the annual license fee collected from the non-SWIFT members banks for the use of the Philippine Payment System - Front End System (PPS-FES) and the monthly access fee for the third party systems providers will allow free and open participation in PhilPaSS, by rural banks.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: By inter-connecting, rural banks may more readily participate in clearing with the Philippine Clearing House Corporation (PCHC), managing its government securities investments, participating in the exchange market, as well as participating in ATM networks and in the interbank market.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Rural banks will also be able to instruct their depository bank to augment their demand deposit accounts (DDA) maintained in the BSP through PhilPaSS.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Truly the potential for rural banks to be mainstreamed in the country's payment system is being realized.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Our policy stance is a clear indication that we consider rural banks to be ready, effective and important channels for economic development.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We also recognize the crucial role that rural banks play in building a truly inclusive financial system.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: A system where there is not just universal access to financial services, but one where financial institutions provide responsive and competitively priced products and services to all, including those who were previously unbanked.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Access to such services can invigorate local economies and improve the overall quality of life.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This cuts to the heart of why rural banks were established.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: It is indeed a gargantuan task.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: But with an enabling policy and regulatory environment, strong rural banking fundamentals, and a new and vibrant RBAP board of directors and officers, I am confident that it can be achieved.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Good evening and more power!
