text: This conveys, in very strong terms, the significance you attach to the role of communication in ensuring effective central banking.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: No doubt, the sea changes in global finance and markets as well as in the domestic macro-economy have posed significant effects in the conduct of monetary policy.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In particular, we have seen the rapid evolution of monetary policy towards increased transparency.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: I share the general observation that secrecy or deliberate obfuscation are no longer the buzzwords in central banking circles.1 In sharp contrast to the past practice of reticence among monetary authorities, greater emphasis on effective communication is now a best-practice policy among central banks around the world.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In fact, in the last two decades or so, we were witness to an expansion in disclosure mechanisms employed by central banks.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Moreover, there has been a dramatic change in the nature and quality of information that monetary authorities are now willing to disclose.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This morning, I will share some of my thoughts on central bank communication in general... and provide you with an overview of the communication strategy that we employ at the Bangko Sentral, with focus on our framework for communication with other government agencies.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The Importance of Central Bank Communication The move toward greater transparency is a key element of good corporate governance.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Central banks have become increasingly independent... so there is scope for greater accountability.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: After all, a central bank is a public office whose policy decisions have an important bearing on the direction of the economy.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Thus, the central bank should be able to clearly define its goals and provide a compelling explanation behind its policy actions.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In turn, transparency allows for an honest assessment of central bank performance, given the goals it has pledged to achieve.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The emphasis on better transparency practices also recognizes the idea that transparency makes monetary policy generally more effective, in part by ensuring that market expectations are formed efficiently.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As central bankers, we are aware that the potency of monetary policy actions can be strengthened if markets understand the overall intention behind the central bank's policy decision and the results it expects to achieve.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Indeed, the emergence of "open mouth" operations as a policy tool outside of the traditional channels of monetary policy has been recognized by central bankers.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As pointed out by Ehrmann and Fratzccher (2005): "Central banks have direct control over a single interest rate, usually the overnight rate, while their success in achieving their mandate requires that they are able to influence asset prices and interest rates at all maturities".
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In the case of the Bangko Sentral, we typically adjust our overnight policy rate, when necessary, by increments of as low as 25 basis points.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: If we really think about it, we do not expect that such a marginal adjustment in a very short-term instrument will do the job for us.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Rather, we rely on the markets to interpret our signals properly... and allow for appropriate adjustments in the prices of financial assets that really matter, including the longer-term tenors.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In general, central banks now avoid surprising the market since this could generate unwarranted volatility.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This is where communication comes in: it increases the predictability of policy decisions and helps the market anticipate how the central bank might react to a particular situation, event or development.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Indeed, good transparency practices promote greater market efficiency For an inflation targeting central bank such as the Bangko Sentral, communication is crucial in anchoring inflation expectations.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: To help guide public expectations, it is incumbent upon an inflation targeting central bank to disclose its outlook for future inflation.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Managing the expectations channel is, therefore, critical.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Apart from influencing the market with its policy actions, communication also allows the central bank to obtain useful feedback from its stakeholders, which in turn is an important input to policy formulation Given these arguments in favor of communication, the next critical issue is the extent of transparency · How transparent should central banks be?
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: My view is that central banks should take a pragmatic approach to communication.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: While transparency is a good policy, excessive transparency could hamper the effectiveness of monetary policy and potentially harm market stability.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Specifically, extensive disclosure requirements about internal policy discussions on money and exchange market operations might disrupt markets, constrain frank discussion by policymakers, or prevent adoption of contingency plans.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In other words, good transparency practices should allow for flexibility...to take into account country-specific circumstances.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: After all, there is no one-size-fits-all formula for central bank communication.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Communication between the Central Bank and Other Government Agencies Let me now turn to the importance of communication between the central bank and other government agencies.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: While most central banks enjoy independence from other branches of government, continuing coordination with other government agencies for macroeconomic policy formulation remains an imperative.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Inter-agency arrangements should be in place to ensure consistent and coherent economic policies.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: After all, monetary and fiscal policies, along with other government policies, are interlocking elements of the country's overall macroeconomic strategy.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The consensus among economists and policymakers is that well-coordinated policies are integral to durable, broad-based and strong economic growth.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As such, fiscal and monetary authorities, as well as other economic managers in government, should share information and be aware of their agencies' respective policy intentions and decisions.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: A silo approach to government policy formulation, where one agency formulates policy on its own without consultation, does not... and will not work.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In fact, the absence of coordination among policymakers could undermine the credibility of the country's macroeconomic policy.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As Worrell (2000) argued in his paper: "the invariable consequence of any appearance of conflict among the authorities is an increase in uncertainty in financial markets, a loss of credibility of macroeconomic policies and an increased probability of price and output instability".
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Thus, good communication with other economic managers is of prime importance in macroeconomic management.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The same principle applies in the field of financial supervision.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Even in central banks with financial supervision functions such as the Bangko Sentral, jurisdiction over the financial sector is often shared with other government supervisory agencies.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In the Philippines, for instance, supervision over non-bank financial institutions without quasi-banking functions is shared by the Bangko Sentral, the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Insurance Commission.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This underscores the need to maintain close coordination among these agencies to ensure consistency of policies, as well as access to timely and accurate information.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: An important caveat in communication between the central bank and other government agencies is the responsibility to respect the confidentiality of sensitive information being shared.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The BSP's Communication Strategy The Bangko Sentral, like many other central banks, continues to enhance its communication strategy to reach all its stakeholders.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Our adoption of inflation targeting in 2002 served as an additional stimulus for us to work on improving our transparency practices.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In dealing with the press and the market, the Bangko Sentral employs a wide range of disclosure mechanisms.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: One of these mechanisms is the BSP website which carries our press statements, statistical releases and our advocacies In the area of monetary policy, a press statement is issued immediately after each monetary policy meeting.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Typically, each policy statement contains the reasons behind the Monetary Board decision, along with a brief discussion on the outlook for future inflation.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The highlights of our policy meetings are also made public after a predetermined lag of four weeks.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The highlights were initially published with a lag of six weeks but we shortened it to four weeks, beginning July last year, to further improve transparency in monetary policy-making.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We also publish a quarterly Inflation Report to document the rigorous economic analysis behind the conduct of monetary policy and inform the public of the overall thinking behind our decisions.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The release of the Inflation Report for each quarter is accompanied by a briefing for the media and market analysts.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In cases of a breach of the inflation target, the BSP issues an open letter to the President to account for the reasons behind it and to outline the actions that will be undertaken to bring inflation back to the target range.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Further, we conduct public information campaigns across the country to foster better understanding and support for the central bank's policies and programs.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The Bangko Sentral also conducts regular dialogues with the press and periodic engagements with its various constituencies.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In the Philippines, the generation of macroeconomic assumptions and formulation of government's medium-term budget strategy is done by the Development Budget Coordinating Committee, which is composed of the Department of Budget and Management, and the Department of Finance, the National Economic and Development Authority and the Office of the Executive Secretary.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The BSP used to be a member of this committee...but, in recognition of its administrative and fiscal autonomy, was re-assigned as a resource institution.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Under the inflation targeting framework, the inflation targets are set by the Committee in coordination with the BSP.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This effectively commits the Government as a whole to the inflation target.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Equally important, this ensures that our monetary policy actions remain consistent with the Government's economic policy agenda, even as we maintain our independence.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In the field of financial supervision, the Bangko Sentral has cooperative arrangements with other financial regulators.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Among others, the Bangko Sentral chairs the Financial Sector Forum which includes the members of the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Insurance Commission and the Philippine Deposit Insurance Corporation It focuses on three broad areas: harmonization of supervisory and regulatory policies in the Philippine financial system; information exchange; and consumer education or financial literacy.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In addition, the Bangko Sentral is in various stages of negotiations with foreign supervisory authorities for the adoption of minimum ground rules on information sharing involving cross-border financial institutions under their supervision.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Through this initiative, we hope to strengthen cooperative arrangements with our foreign counterparts.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Another important dimension of our interface with the government is our interaction with the Executive and Legislative branches of Government.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As mandated in our charter, we submit regular reports to the President and both houses of Congress.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: These include a report on economic and financial conditions, a report on the central bank's financial condition, and a review on the state of the Philippine financial system.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The BSP is also required by law to report to the President and Congress any unusual movements in monetary aggregates, credit and price levels, as well as the remedial measures undertaken by the Bangko Sentral to correct them.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In addition, the Bangko Sentral engages in a variety of informal interactions with the other branches of government through appearances in committee hearings in both houses of Congress and its participation in various government inter-agency committees and working groups.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In other words, we invest time and resources to communicate our policies and programs with other branches of government.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Concluding Remarks This IMF seminar, therefore, comes at an opportune time when central bank communication has emerged as a potent policy tool, rather than a mere channel to transmit information.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As an institution that recognizes the significance of communication in making our operations more effective, we at the Bangko Sentral are pleased to co-host this Second IMF Regional Seminar on Central Bank Communication.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This seminar should build on the IMF's initiative, which started in Mumbai, to provide a forum to discuss emerging issues in central bank communications and gain insights from one another's experiences.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We thank the IMF and their representatives who are here with us this morning...for setting up this forum for central bank communication in this region Finally, I wish this seminar on central bank communication will be fruitful and highly successful, not only in terms of generating fresh perspectives but also in fostering regular exchange and cooperation among the participants.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Have a wonderful stay in our country.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Thank you and Mabuhay!
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas is pleased to co-host with the Philippine Statistical Association (PSA) this year's summer conference on the theme: "OFWs: Bagong Bayani, Ilan Ba Talaga Kayo?".
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Over the past few decades, OFW deployment has had a profound impact on our economic and social dynamics.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Research and statistics pertaining to OFWs are becoming increasingly indispensable in establishing and assessing these effects.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: It is thus critical that various agencies and institutions and producers and users alike of OFW-related statistics are convening today: first, to clarify the official headcount of OFWs, given various sets of data; and second, to provide accurate measures of OFW remittances.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The best way to start our consultation today is to recognize that the onset of globalization has heightened trade and investments across countries.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Equally important, labor migration and cross-border employment have also increased.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As a result, both the issues of migration and cross-border remittances have attracted growing attention from a greater number of policymakers, academicians, international organizations, and market practitioners, over the years.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: At this stage, however, there is still a lot of ground to cover on the statistical front.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We have yet to update and strengthen our database to fully satisfy the needs of policy and program formulators.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: How important is the information?.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We need to regularly monitor overseas employment as basis for policy and program formulations for advancing the cause of protecting our overseas workers and enhancing their welfare and of their families.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Another key issue is the impact of international movement of persons on our demographic structures, expenditure patterns, social structures and poverty levels.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Likewise, we recognize the importance of overseas employment in helping ease the pressure of unemployment and in boosting the national economy by helping increase the foreign exchange reserves.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: There are of course second-order effects of higher foreign exchange inflows, including the impact on the domestic currency and external competitiveness.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: But to me, it is fundamental to first address the current challenges and measurement issues that have very important analytical and policy bearings.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This conference will hopefully help pave the way to clarify such issues.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: First, let us look at the statistics on the number of OFWs.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Our theme for today, "OFWs: Bagong Bayani, Ilan Ba Talaga Kayo?
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: ", suggests that we are not yet certain exactly how many are our OFWs, and more generally, how many Filipinos are overseas.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Accuracy in this aspect may really be a challenge because what we want to monitor are people who are always on the move.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: At present, there are various agencies producing OFW-related statistics.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA), the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) and the Commission on Filipinos Overseas (CFO), on the one hand, maintain statistics based mostly on administrative records as an offshoot of their functions.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: On the other hand, the Bureau of Labor and Employment Statistics and the National Statistics Office, have data based on labor force surveys and census of population and housing.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We need to understand how these data from various agencies are interrelated.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The first key question is: is there a uniform definition of what an OFW is?.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: For instance, in the Census of Population of Housing, overseas workers are defined as those who had been away for not more than five years from date of last departure.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Do the other agencies producing OFW statistics adopt the same definition?.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Is it possible to integrate and reconcile these sets of data from various sources to come up with one, uniform, comparable set of data on OFWs and overseas Filipinos?.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The next question is: how are the definitions linked or reconciled with definitions in other macroeconomic statistical frameworks such as the 1993 System of National Accounts (1993 SNA) and the 5th edition of the balance of payments manual (BPM5), which adopt a one-year residency criterion for determining who are the residents of a particular economy?.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: What are the implications of adopting different sets of definition in our economic statistics and in economic analysis?.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: While there are efforts in the Inter-Agency Technical Working Group (TWG) on Overseas Filipino Statistics to formulate the operational framework, concepts and definitions for overseas Filipinos, this conference could clarify the differences in the sets of data currently available.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Second, on the remittance data.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We have already seen the size of OFW remittances doubling within the last five years.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: With its growing importance to our economy, we need to place emphasis on its accurate measurement.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We are aware that remittances are by themselves already inherently difficult to measure, since they are composed mostly of numerous small, frequent transactions, carried out by a multitude of transactors through a complex structure of originating and delivering agents here are also other measurement concerns including appropriately capturing remittances of non-resident OFWs which are invested in financial instruments or physical assets such as real estate.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Moreover, a certain amount of remittances still flow through informal channels, which should be measured to determine the amount of global remittances.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Given the present range of remittance channels, and the expected increased complexity of the structure of service providers in the near future, accurate measurement of remittances remains a challenge for statisticians.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We therefore need to collectively consider and design the best approach that will measure remittances in the most accurate and timely manner, going forward.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This will not necessarily be an easy task.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Even at the international level, the conventional wisdom is that there is no unique "best" source of data, or collection approach, due to the complexity of the phenomenon.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Therefore, from a purely technical standpoint, a reasonable strategy would be to appropriately combine different sources and methods, e.g., bank reports data, household surveys, other administrative-based data, even econometric and demographic models, that will allow for integration, cross-checks and reciprocal confirmations.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Moreover, data on remittances should not be considered in isolation from data on stock of workers and deployment of overseas workers, as well as wage rates, wage increases and inflation in host countries.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: At the end of the day, there have to be reasonably explainable patterns and links among these variables that will allow for more informed economic analysis, decision making and policy-making by the government.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: On this note, highly commend the Philippine Statistical Association for organizing this conference on the subject.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We hope that this forum will serve as a catalyst for further statistical research and studies on the OFW phenomenon.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We also thank the sponsors of this conference for their support.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: For its part, the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas remains committed to its objective of improving the remittance environment for the benefit of our OFWs -- particularly by facilitating the reduction of remittance costs in the Philippines and in host countries, and by helping channel foreign exchange savings to microenterprises and other investment opportunities.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The BSP also fully supports the statistical improvement efforts that will help ensure that the government will formulate its policy decisions based on solid statistical ground.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Maraming salamat po, at magandang hapon sa inyong lahat.

title: Keynote Address
text: My remarks this afternoon will focus on BSP's initiatives to strengthen risk management practices in banks under our supervision.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Since banks still dominate the financial landscape in our country, the BSP as the banking supervisor has to be at the forefront of the development of better risk management practices in the country.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Although this is a very challenging role to play given the pace of development in the field of risk management, I do believe that the BSP is up to the challenge and has been proactive judging by the number of initiatives we have put in place starting in the mid-90s.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: It is my pleasure to share with you our experience on the implementation of these initiatives, but before that let me highlight the risk profile of the Philippine banking system, which dictated the direction and pace of these regulatory actions.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Risk profile of the Philippine banking system As of end-June 2006, total on-balance sheet assets of the banking industry amounted to P4.5 trillion, of which about 89 percent are accounted for by the dominant commercial banking segment.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Additionally, off-balance sheet notional accounts - consisting of derivatives, trust and trade-related contingent exposures -amounted to P2.3 trillion.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In terms of risk-weighted assets or RWA - which is a supervisory measure of banks' risk exposures to credit risk and market risk only - commercial banks' exposures are made up of 90 percent credit risk and 10 percent market risk.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: With the addition of operational risk in the risk-based capital adequacy framework of the BSP on 1 July 2007, our simulations show that commercial banks' RWA will be made up of 77 percent credit risk, 8 percent market risk, and 15 percent operational risk.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As primary buffer against these risk exposures, Tier 1 capitalization of the banking system, which includes hybrid Tier 1 capital stood at P433 billion as of end-March 2006.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Our banks have also issued P79 billion in Tier 2 capital as allowed under our regulations consistent with international practices.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: CAR (capital adequacy ratio) stood at 19.4 percent as of end-March 20061 while loss provisions, which serve as cushion for expected losses have been significantly boosted from just 1.44 percent of total assets in end-December 1997, to 2.72 percent as of end-June 2006.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: BSP's risk management initiatives Now, let me guide you through the important historical highlights of BSP's risk management initiatives.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In 1995, the BSP recognized the greater risk exposure in the system brought about by derivatives activities.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: To mitigate this, the BSP issued Circular No.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: 102 prescribing the minimum standards for risk management of derivatives.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This was probably the first BSP regulation that specifically focused on banks' market risk taking activities and risk management practices.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Prior to this, risk management regulations were largely confined to basic credit risk management and to internal control issues.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In 1997, the thrust of bank supervision started to shift its focus towards a more forward-looking view of risk management and whether a bank has the infrastructure to manage its own risks, instead of just mainly performing financial audit and compliance review.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The objective was to address weaknesses in management and internal controls before financial performance suffers rather than being satisfied with identifying what went wrong after the fact.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The BSP's effort to focus on risk management is ultimately intended to give banks greater flexibility to respond to changing opportunities and challenges in the face of global competition under a more deregulated environment and at a time of rapid technological advances.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Traditional bank supervision tended to micromanage banks to avoid risks that seem too high.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The new approach to supervision is now more focused on the assessment of the quality of risk-management practices and generally allows banks to take on greater risks so long as the banks demonstrate the ability to identify, measure, manage and price for those risks.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This more liberal approach to supervision, which allows banks more opportunities for success, entails that the BSP emphasize the responsibility of the banks' board of directors and senior management to ensure the soundness and stability of their respective banks.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The regulators' role is primarily to evaluate the quality of oversight and management provided by these critical actors - that is, the quality of corporate governance.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Strengthening banks' corporate governance has thus been the theme of a number of BSP regulations.

label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: For our part, the approach to implementation has been more calculated.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Certain elements of the Basel II approaches such as those pertaining to risk weights for corporates and NPLs, were gradually incorporated in existing regulations to pave the way for a smoother implementation of the whole new framework in 2007.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Meanwhile, in response to heightened appetite and growing exposure of banks to structured products and in preparation for the envisaged take-off of the domestic securitization market following the approval of the Securitization Act of 2004, the BSP pre-emptively issued in 2005 the risk-based capital treatment of banks' exposures to structured products and securitization structures.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In support of major policy objectives of enhancing credit access and expediting the clean-up of bad assets from the system, the BSP likewise advanced lower credit risk weightings for high grade corporate debt exposures and micro and SME exposures, but also increased the risk weighting on non-performing loans.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This year, the BSP has issued the much-awaited Basel II implementing guidelines for the Philippines.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The BSP's Task Force on the Implementation of Basel II has just concluded their series of briefings both within and outside of the BSP in preparation for the parallel run that will be conducted starting end this year until mid next year.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Unlike the existing BSP risk-based capital adequacy framework, the new Basel II-based framework does not only focus on the computation of the appropriate level of capital given a certain level of risk exposure, but it also highlights the need for more market disclosures by banks on their risk management exposures and practices.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This is fully consistent with Basel II Pillar 3 recommendations, as well as the new International Financial Reporting Standards or IFRS which we fully adopted since 2005.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The rationale is that the market itself contains disciplinary mechanisms that can reinforce the efforts of supervisors by rewarding banks that manage risk effectively and penalizing those whose risk management is inept or imprudent through their patronage or non-patronage.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Basel II and risk management As we move into implementation of Basel II, industry reaction is both revealing and interesting.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: On one hand, the commotion it is causing with banks doubling their efforts in improving their risk management systems to meet the requirements of the advanced approaches is a very positive development as far as the BSP is concerned.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: On the other hand, it is rather disappointing that it takes regulatory pressure for many banks to finally start investing in a sound risk management system.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: I understand that there are certain problems that now face banks as they aim to improve their own risk management systems.. A survey of emerging market central banks conducted by the BIS reveals the three main difficulties faced not just by you, but by banks in emerging markets in general, in implementing more sophisticated risk assessment techniques.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: These are: Data problems.. Modern techniques of risk assessment in Basle II involve estimation of probabilities of default on the lenders' portfolio, as well as of loss-given-default.. Foreign banks get around by relying on data from their home country operations, but these data may not be applicable in the emerging markets they operate in..
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Many emerging markets are however taking steps to improve data availability.. For example, Malaysia and Thailand have respectively established centralized credit registry for households and corporations and a credit information bureau.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Lack of suitable techniques for designing and calibrating models to evaluate alternative scenarios.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Large human resources and infrastructure (IT and other) costs of implementing advanced techniques for risk assessment..
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: But improvements in risk management have inherent value to banks by avoiding major costs, including potentially catastrophic costs that can break a bank.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Thus they should be pursued with or without regulatory requirements.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Those of you who are sports fans can relate to this.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As you know, success in many sports today relies on a solid defense that is always there whether the breaks are with you or not.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Sophisticated risk management systems should be put in place because the bank sees the need to, and not just to impress, or perhaps intimidate the supervisors.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The latter I guarantee is highly unlikely to happen because our supervisory personnel have also been doing their homework.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Indeed, we have not just strengthened the regulatory framework.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: No less important, the BSP has invested heavily in the last few years in enhancing our supervisory capacity in line with the new demands.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: These efforts have ranged from individual skills enhancement through world class in-house structured training program to acquisition of relevant international certification, to creation of highly trained special teams, and currently a wholesale re-engineering and reorganization of the whole supervision and examination set-up.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: I assure you, we will be up to the task.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We practice what we preach.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Wrong motivations for improving banks' risk management systems may obscure the ultimate aim for such actions - i.e., to make banks' shareholders and other stakeholders, NOT the regulators, happy by safeguarding and enhancing the value of their investments.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: On our part, BSP's interest in promoting better risk management is motivated more by macro considerations - that is, a safe and sound banking system is crucial to economic growth and to the stability of financial markets.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Concluding remarks Let me now sum up.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: If you notice, the BSP initiatives I have mentioned are geared towards simultaneously promoting sound risk management practices in banks, and strengthening the risk-based capital adequacy framework.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This is because both robust risk management and strong capital positions are critical in ensuring that individual banks operate in a safe and sound manner, which in turn enhances the stability of the financial system.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In addition, strong capital helps banks absorb unexpected shocks and reduces moral hazard associated with the regulatory safety nets.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Finally, let me reiterate BSP's commitment to the identification, assessment, and promotion of sound risk management practices in the financial system, which it considers as central elements of good supervisory practice.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: But of course the BSP can only do this with the invaluable help of our allies from the academe and the industry, such as the JBF Center and PRMIA.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Before I end, let me just quote Captain James Kirk of the Star Trek Enterprise: "Risk is our business.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: That's what this starship is all about.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: That's why we're aboard her."

title: Keynote Address
text: Indeed, the same can be said of banking.

title: Keynote Address
text: Ladies and gentlemen of the Corporate Planning Society of the Philippines, fellow workers in government, special guests.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Good afternoon and welcome to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: I am delighted that the Bangko Sentral is hosting your association's 4th general membership meeting.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This provides us the opportunity to directly share with you our insights on vital inputs you need to firm up your plans for the coming years; after this, we can have a free-wheeling discussion so that we can also hear from you, learn about your concerns, and clarify certain issues.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This is our way of supporting the cause of strategic planning in our country, the critical and essential function of creating a road map to achieve institutional goals that....taken together....sustain a nation's growth and development.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: First, I will discuss the highlights of our economic performance over the past year and our expectations, moving forward.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: I will also touch on the key challenges ahead and how this will influence the policy direction of the Bangko Sentral.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The Economy in Perspective Well, as you are aware, our key economic indicators have been telling us that 2006 is bound to be one of our best years....as positive results have been broad-based.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In fact, analysts have been describing 2006 as a defining moment for our economy, as it has turned around negative perceptions.... and raised investor confidence in our country.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Overall, our economy continues to grow, buoyed by the vibrant performance of key sectors notably manufacturing, trade and finance as well as the resurgence of agriculture, fishery and forestry.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In fact, real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) accelerated to 5.5 percent during the first half of 2006 from 4.8 percent in the previous year.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Significantly, we were able to keep inflation at single-digit levels....even as our economy grew and absorbed record high domestic oil prices.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In fact, we have been seeing a steady decline in inflation from a high of 7.6% in March this year to 5.4% last October, the lowest level since June 2004.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Please note that this is within the Bangko Sentral's forecast range of between 5 to 5.7%.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As the institution mandated to stabilize prices, the Bangko Sentral is satisfied with this trend.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Essentially, the continued softening of fuel prices and the strengthening of the peso supported the further deceleration in inflation in October.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Latest forecasts of the Bangko Sentral continues to indicate a generally declining path for inflation, with average inflation for 2007 expected to fall within the 4-5 percent target, barring unforeseen adverse shocks of course.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As a result, the Monetary Board, in its last policy meeting on November 2, kept the Bangko Sentral's benchmark policy rates unchanged, but reinstated a tiering of interest rates on bank placements with the BSP to encourage further bank lending.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Treasury bill (T-bill) rates also declined across the board in early November, due primarily to the improved fiscal position of the National Government, manageable outlook for inflation and ample liquidity.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: On the external front, the overall balance of payments position for the first six months of 2006 recorded a surplus of $2.04 billion, an improvement from the US$1.98 billion surplus recorded in the same period in 2005.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The improvement resulted from higher inflows in current transfers, particularly from remittances of overseas Filipino workers (OFWs), higher exports and investment inflows.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: During the first nine months this year, OFW remittances reached US$9.1 billion, up 14.4 percent from the same period last year as more Filipinos found work overseas and banks became more aggressive in offering remittance services to OFWs.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Based on this trend, we expect total OFW remittances in 2006 to set a new record and approximate $12 billion.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: I am also pleased to inform you that our country's gross international reserves (GIR) reached a new record-high level of US$22.3 billion in October this year.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Given the sustained uptrend in our international reserves, we have in fact pre-paid some of our foreign loans.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Likewise, these developments on the external front continue to sustain the appreciation of the peso versus the US dollar.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: I am sure you are all aware that the peso hit P49.60 to one US dollar yesterday, its highest level since 2002, as market sentiment continues to be positive.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Better-than-expected fiscal performance is a key factor in this regard, as government spending remains restrained even with higher revenues generated from the Revised and the Expanded Value Added Taxes.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: To summarize, ladies and gentlemen, we have better macroeconomic fundamentals as inflation continues to decelerate, the peso remains strong against the US dollar, and our fiscal position continues to improve, with actual surpluses posted in four months so far this year.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As the Government adheres to the implementation of its economic reform program, we should see more positive developments, moving forward.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The Financial Sector Reform Agenda Similarly, our financial reform agenda has been generating positive results.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In particular, the resources of the Philippine banking system reached record high levels as banks continued to register modest growth in deposits and capital accounts.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This is significant... as banks account for more than 95% of the assets of the Philippine financial system.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Inasmuch as our economy depends practically on the banking sector for its financial needs, it is imperative that banks are kept sound, healthy and responsive to the needs of its customers.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: For your information, the Bangko Sentral supervises 41 operating universal and commercial banks with 4,277 branches, 84 thrift banks with 1,209 branches, and 754 rural and cooperative banks with 1,305 branches.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: These figures are as of June 30, 2006.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: With the series of mergers and consolidations that are taking place as banks seek to comply with more stringent capitalization requirements under Basel 2 and international accounting standards, we should see fewer, but stronger banks in the coming years.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The BSP remains steadfast in its efforts to help clean up banks' balance sheets to stimulate lending activity.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: So far, we have seen the non-performing loan (NPL) ratio of universal and commercial banks drop from a high of 17.4% in 2001....to 8.5% in December 2005.... and further to 7.43% last September.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Aggregate capitalization of the banking sector using the new and more stringent risk-based framework indicates that the banking industry's capital adequacy ratio (CAR) continues to exceed the statutory level set by the BSP at 10 % and the global standard of 8% set by the Bank for International Settlements.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Parallel to this positive development, outstanding loans of commercial and universal banks increased by 6.1 % year-on-year in September to P1.597 trillion, the highest growth rate since May 2005.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: While these may be modest compared to levels reached in the previous years and by international standards, the numbers nevertheless indicate the overall soundness of the Philippine banking system on account of continuing reforms in recent years.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: These include, among others, adherence to international best practices and the good governance tenets of fairness, accountability, transparency and social responsibility.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Capital market reform to broaden the funding sources of the economy, as well as to ease the vulnerability of banks to economic downturns, remains a priority for Bangko Sentral.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In collaboration with other government agencies and the private sector, the Bangko Sentral worked for the completion of needed infrastructure that would enhance financial system integrity and overall market confidence.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The operation of the fixed income exchange (FIE) and the implementation of the third-party custodian scheme are part of these initiatives to provide viable and sustainable alternative sources of funds.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The Challenges Ahead In the years ahead, the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas will remain focused on its mandate of ensuring price stability by adhering to its inflation target; ensuring that the banking sector remains sound and able to meet the financial requirements of the economy; and ensuring the stability of the Philippine payments system to minimize or prevent systemic risks.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: To pursue its price stability mandate, the Monetary Board, the policy-making body of the Bangko Sentral, will continue to rely on the following basic instruments: policy rates which are set every six weeks and influence the interest rates at which banks transact with their clients; reserve requirements or the share of depositors' money that banks must set aside to meet withdrawals; open market operations which allow the Bangko Sentral to influence the level of money circulating in the economy through the purchase or sale of government securities; and rediscounting which encourages banks to finance priority economic activities such as exports and microfinance.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The Bangko Sentral uses inflation targeting as a framework to maintain price stability.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Under this strategy, the BSP calibrates its policy actions to achieve the rate of inflation agreed upon with other economic agencies of government.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Adopted in 2002, this approach has served us in good stead.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The challenge for us is to keep our forecasting tools on the money so that our policy rate decisions will generate the desired outcome when its full impact is absorbed by the economy 18 to 24 months down the road.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Yes, ladies and gentlemen; this is the lag time we have to contend with in measuring the effectiveness of our policy response to ensure stable prices.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As the sole issuer of Philippine currency, the Bangko Sentral must also ensure that there is just enough money in circulation to meet the requirements of the country.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The amount of money in circulation must not be too low that it could lead to higher interest rates and slower economic growth.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: On the other hand, money supply must not be too high that it will be inflationary and reduce the purchasing power of the peso.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This is a complex and challenging balancing act.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As mentioned before, it is imperative that the banking sector remains sound and healthy as it provides the funding requirements of the economy, using essentially money entrusted to it by the people.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In fact, funding for more than 70% of the resources of the banking system come from deposits which, as of June 2006, had reached P3.2 trillion.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Ensuring the stability of our payments and settlements system is equally important.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As the bank of banks, the Bangko Sentral serves as an effective clearing house for high value inter-bank transactions as it holds cash balances of the banks.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: For this purpose, the Bangko Sentral operates a real-time gross settlement system which we call the Philippine Payments and Settlements System or PHILPASS which processes about 2,000 transactions with a total value of about 300 billion pesos....daily.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This is therefore a vital service as it minimizes settlement risks for high value transactions that may adversely affect the stability of the financial system.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: I hope that you will continue to support Bangko Sentral's policies and programs; in the same manner, you can depend on our support....if there is convergence on what our respective institutions want to accomplish.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Indeed, with appropriate programs of cooperation and complementation, the government and the private sectors can unleash the synergy which could sustain growth and development of our economy; jobs and income for the man on the street; as well as peace and prosperity for our country.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Let us therefore work together to sustain our growth momentum and continue to implement our reform agenda.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Remember, in the face of increasing global competition and millions of Filipinos who remain mired in poverty, we either innovate....or stagnate.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Let us choose to innovate... together.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Maraming salamat sa inyong lahat.

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: President Julian Lim of the Association of International Business Executives of the Philippines, distinguished officers and members of the AIBEP board, special guests, ladies and gentlemen, good evening.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: I am pleased to join you tonight to address your regular monthly meeting.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: We appreciate your continued support of...and interest in...the Philippine economy.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: As international stakeholders in business in the Philippines, I know all of you closely monitor the outlook on the Philippine economy as it affects your individual businesses and industries.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: In consideration of your varied interests, I would like to spend the next few minutes painting you a picture of the recent developments in the country's economy as well as its monetary, external and financial sectors.
label: negative

text: I would also like to share with you our vision of the future and the challenges that we anticipate along the way.

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: Recent economic developments The Philippine economy continues to show resilience in the face of continued challenges.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: In 2005, real gross domestic product (GDP) expanded over 5 percent on the strength of the services sector on the production side and sustained consumer expenditures on the demand side.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: This moderate growth of the economy helped create more jobs that lowered unemployment rate.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: Please note that the expansion of the economy is being sustained without fueling further inflation, even as oil prices continue to climb to record high levels.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: For instance, headline inflation fell from 8.5% in May 2005 to 6.7% in December.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: This year, after the implementation of the VAT rate increase initially pushed prices higher, we note a softening of prices....with inflation easing from 7.6% in march to 7.1 percent in April.

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: The government's fiscal consolidation efforts are also showing positive results.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: The National Government (NG) deficit for the first quarter of 2006 was significantly lower than the programmed ceiling due to strong revenue performance.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: The fiscal deficit reached P67.6 billion as of March....lower and better than the programmed ceiling of P71.8 billion.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: Meanwhile, the banking system continues to show positive trends as well.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: Loan quality continues to improve, while the capital adequacy ratio of the Philippine banking system continues to remain well above the international benchmark: as of September 2005, it stood at 17.6 percent, way above the international benchmark of 8.0 percent.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: This is indicative of an increasingly sound banking sector that is better able to finance the funding requirements of a growing economy.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: On the external front, the country's overall balance of payments position yielded a surplus of US$2.4 billion in 2005, as foreign exchange inflows benefited from heavy remittances from overseas Filipino workers and inflows from foreign portfolio and direct investments.

text: In turn, these foreign exchange inflows helped raise the country's gross international reserves (GIR) to a record year-end level of $18.5 billion; this rose further to a new record high of nearly $21 billion as of end April 2006, which provides ample cover for over 4 months of imports of goods and payments of services and income.

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: Such strong inflows and the confidence generated by increasing international reserves and tax reforms helped support the peso.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: This year, the peso continues its appreciation.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas

label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: Monetary and external sector outlook and policy directions As the government institution mandated to keep prices stable, the BSP has to contend with the effects of the continued rise in oil prices, the surge in liquidity growth from foreign exchange inflows, and the effects of whatever negative market sentiments on the exchange rate.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: To address these risks to inflation and keep inflation expectations from spiraling away from our target, calibrated increases in BSP's benchmark interest rates were carried out in April, September and October 2005.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: These rate increases were made in tandem with a hike in reserve requirements in July to keep excess liquidity in check and prevent it from creating additional inflationary pressure.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: In the second half of 2006, we expect inflation to follow a decelerating trend as the short-lived impact of the RVAT on prices of goods and services continues to taper off.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: Nevertheless, average inflation is expected to tip past the government's target of 4.0-5.0 percent in 2006 due principally to high oil prices.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: Given these risks and outlook for inflation, the BSP will exert all efforts to achieve the inflation target in the medium-term.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: The BSP will keep a close eye on incipient inflationary pressures, especially those coming from the demand side, and will stand ready to undertake the necessary monetary action.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: As a complement to monetary action, direct action to address supply-side risks would remain a key policy priority.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: To this end, the BSP will intensify further representation with relevant government agencies in support of supply-side intervention measures, particularly in keeping basic food supplies stable.

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: On the other hand, the BSP's exchange rate policy will continue to be anchored on our main mandate of price stability.

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: Consistent with our inflation-targeting framework for the conduct of monetary policy, the BSP will continue to leave the determination of the value of the peso to market forces.

text: Of course, there is some scope for occasional BSP action to dampen sharp fluctuations in the exchange rate, principally to maintain order and stability in the foreign exchange market.

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas

text: In particular, local commercial banks have broadened their reach through establishment of more remittance centers abroad, tie-ups with foreign financial institutions and introduction of innovative and faster means of remittance transfers to channel remittances through banks.

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas

text: The BSP has also initiated a nationwide information campaign for OFWs and members of their families on the opportunities for investing their foreign exchange savings in microenterprise activities and other alternative financial instruments.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: What we want to see is the transformation of our OFW families from being consumers to regular savers, investors and even entrepreneurs.

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: Banking sector outlook and policy The BSP will continue to intensify its efforts to strengthen the country's financial system.
label: negative

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
text: For this purpose, the BSP's reform strategy is focused on two pillars: a healthy banking system as well as a deep and efficient capital market that, together, will effectively mobilize savings to fund economic development.

title: The state of the Philippine Economy and Policy Directions of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas

title: The Philippine Economy: Developments and Prospects
text: We had to deal with many challenges in 2005.

label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Developments and Prospects
text: And yet, in the face of all these, our economy proved its resilience and fundamental strength.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Developments and Prospects
text: Our domestic economy, as measured by gross domestic product, continued to expand and managed to grow by 5.1%.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Developments and Prospects

title: The Philippine Economy: Developments and Prospects
text: Part of this reform program is fiscal consolidation, which is now generating benefits for the country.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Developments and Prospects

label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Developments and Prospects
text: This has led government to say that it is now possible for us to have a balanced budget by 2008.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Developments and Prospects
text: When this happens, our government will no longer be compelled to borrow money to finance its regular operations.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Developments and Prospects

label: negative

text: It is also noteworthy that we were able to keep inflation at single-digit levels in spite of record high oil prices and sustained economic growth.

title: The Philippine Economy: Developments and Prospects
text: The country's external position also strengthened in the past year.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: Developments and Prospects
text: Overall balance of payments position for 2005 stood at a surplus of US$2.4 billion, a turnaround from the previous year's large deficit.
