title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Introduction During the BSP's annual reception for the banking and business community last Tuesday, I had one principal appeal to our friends.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: To make the best of our circumstances, achieve progress in our own spheres, so that in the end, the whole nation will be better off.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Distinguished officers and members of the Management Association of the Philippines led by 2005 President Mon Paterno and 2006 President Evelyn Singson, colleagues from the BSP and the government, distinguished guests, friends, ladies and gentlemen, good evening.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: MAP's theme for this year, "Call to action: Country above self", happens to be in accord with my Tuesday's appeal.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: We are all convinced that the must-do list for the Philippines is long, some of the items are structural while some would require streamlining of policies.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Any and all efforts to address this must-do list are therefore quite crucial.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: The next best thing to do is precisely this - take action in your respective spheres of influence.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: As captains of industries - described by media as movers and shakers of our economy - you can truly generate tremendous benefits for our country and our people.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Ladies and gentlemen, what you have selected as guiding theme for this year is exactly the mindset we want Filipinos to have: Country above self.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: If you can widen the reach of this message to cover as many Filipinos as possible, then you would be a part of a chain that seeks to improve the nation.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Now, let me share with you some positive news on the economic front which give us reason to be more confident about our future.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: 2005 a most challenging year By most accounts, 2005 was a very challenging year for the Philippines.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: We had to contend with high oil prices, rising global interest rates, lower farm output, and non-economic tremors.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Yet our economy, as measured by GDP, continued to expand.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Sure, it wasn't at the pace we aimed for, but our economy proved its resilience once again.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: The expansion in economic activity was achieved amid an easing inflation environment.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Inflation has continued to ease since the second half of 2005, supported mainly by the softening prices of food and oil, and to some extent the stronger peso.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Headline inflation has fallen to 7.0 percent in the second half of 2005.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: The average inflation rate for last year was 7.6 percent.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: More importantly, core inflation, which takes out the impact of volatile food and energy prices on the CPI, has steadily trended downwards.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: The decline in core inflation suggests that the inflationary pressures of the past year were not of a permanent, demand-driven nature.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: This fact supports the limited and selectively tightening bias of monetary policy.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Another source of optimism is the improving fiscal performance.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Coming from a very difficult period of large and persistent fiscal overhang, the government embarked on and succeeded in its initial efforts towards fiscal consolidation, by way of intensified tax administration and vital new tax measures as well as expenditure control.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: The National Government budget deficit stood at P146.5 billion for 2005, well below the target for the period.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: This figure also represents the lowest budget shortfall since 2001. as revenue gains continue with the VAT implementation, we stand a good chance of seeing a balanced budget by 2008.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: The positive investor sentiment over the progress made on the fiscal front as well as healthy inflows from remittances have also strengthened the external position.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Latest estimates show that the overall balance of payments (BOP) position for 2005 stood at a surplus of US$2.4 billion, which is a welcome turnaround from the previous year's shortfall.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: The peso likewise ended stronger against the US dollar on the back of the positive market sentiment and strong inflows.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: The peso ended 2005 as the top performing currency in the Asian region.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: This surge in dollar inflows also allowed the BSP to build up its dollar reserves.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: At US$18.5 billion as at end-December 2005, the country's gross international reserves (GIR) is significantly higher than the US$17 billion target for the year and is sufficient to cover about 4 months' worth of imports of goods and services.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Meanwhile, the country's external debt also narrowed to US$55.5 billion by end-September 2005.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: This amount continued to be made up mostly of medium- and long-term liabilities, which ensures that our debt payments remain manageable and sustainable.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: At the same time, the Philippine banking system continued to show improving soundness.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: As of November 2005, commercial banks' non-performing loans as a percentage to total loans registered a single digit level of 8.7 percent.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Growth in bank lending, however, continues to be modest (2.1 percent Nov.), but we expect it to rebound this year given the substantial progress achieved so far with sustained asset clean up.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Having said this, I have to admit, the Philippines is not yet totally out of the woods.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: There are risks that we have to face and manage in the years ahead.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: We are sure, however, to move forward if we persevere.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: For us at the bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, we are aware of the risks attendant to our primary responsibility of keeping prices stable.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: The Monetary Board had to respond promptly and carefully to these inflationary risks to the inflation target.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: In the course of 2005, we raised our policy interest rates by a total of 75 basis points and increased reserve requirements by 200 basis points.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: These were modest responses compared to other jurisdictions where their capacity is nearing to the brim and the labor market is stretched to the limit.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Yet they were decisive, considering the demand pressures were limited and the second round impact was yet to emerge.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: By the second half of 2005, inflation had started to ease.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Improving fundamentals, optimism and 2006 What then do we see in 2006.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: We continue to face uncertainties, but I believe the country's improving economic fundamentals should give us a reasonable degree of optimism about 2006.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Economic activity, for one thing, is likely to continue at a reasonable pace, driven mainly by the services and industry sectors.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Nonetheless, the rise in oil prices over the past year is likely to take its toll on domestic demand, particularly on consumption spending.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: For this reason, the development budget coordinating committee is looking at real GDP growth in 2006 that is likely to be closer to the lower end of its target at 5.7 percent.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: As for inflation, it is expected to be higher in 2006, given the continued upside risks.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Oil prices, for example, are expected to remain high relative to their historical trend and the RVAT is likely to exert, at least a short-term, upward pressure on consumer prices.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Taking into account the recent easing of oil prices, as well as the strengthening of the peso, inflation is expected to hover between 7.5 and 8.1 percent in 2006.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Let me point out though that we do expect an easing of inflation in the second half of the year, as the impact of the RVAT diminishes.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Meanwhile, improvements in fiscal performance, ample liquidity in the financial system, and moderate credit growth are expected to mitigate the impact of inflationary pressures on market interest rates.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: There is also good reason to expect a strong external position this year.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Dollar inflows, primarily from OFW remittances and investments, are expected to continue to come in.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: With healthy inflows, the exchange rate is poised to remain broadly stable in the course of the year.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: The continuing challenges to monetary and banking policies While economic performance appears to be on track, we remain watchful of the potential risks and challenges to the economic outlook.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: These risks include the following: (1) volatility in world oil prices; (2) a build-up of excess liquidity in the financial system; (3) possible exchange rate volatility due to excess liquidity; and (4) adverse shifts in the public's inflation expectations.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: In the face of these challenges, the public can count on the BSP to make sure that these risks do not endanger our path to economic progress.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: The BSP will stay committed to its mandate of promoting low and stable inflation.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: The BSP is also committed to strengthening the financial sector through continued structural reforms.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Foremost of these measures is the clean-up of banks' balance sheets of non-performing assets.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: The clean-up will help spur credit and investment activity and create the basis for more sustainable growth in the medium term.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Other key financial reforms will be focused on: (1) improving the BSP's supervision technology and capacity; (2) aligning prudential regulation of the banking system with international standards and best practices; (3) strengthening corporate governance standards and market discipline mechanisms; (4) further developing the domestic capital market; and (5) enhancing the payments system.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Efforts are also underway for the implementation of Basel II accord and adoption of international accounting standards by local banks.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: These initiatives are designed to bring local banking practices in line with internationally accepted standards.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: In the area of capital market development, the BSP will continue its active collaboration with other government agencies and the private sector for the completion of much-needed market infrastructure to enhance system integrity and overall market confidence.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: We will likewise pursue further enhancements in financial information to guide investor decisions.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: A key effort in this area is the establishment of credit rating agencies.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: We are also working closely with congress on the establishment of a centralized credit information system to help private enterprises secure better access to credit, reduce borrowing costs, as well as minimize the risk exposures of financial intermediaries.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: The BSP also actively seeks to widen the investor base of the local financial markets through a number of new investment products which would better reflect market prices.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: These will help encourage more institutional investors such as insurance companies, mutual funds and pension funds to participate in the capital market.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Future reform measures will eventually lead to the introduction of exchange-based products that can further stimulate market activity and deepen liquidity.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: The continuing challenge Let me sum up by saying that the near-term economic outlook suggests more vibrant economic activity, but there are potential obstacles on the way to sustainable growth.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: The critical task ahead is for us to focus, not just on macroeconomic stabilization in the short-term, but also on preserving the momentum for economic reforms to ensure sustained growth in the years to come.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Consistent with map's marching order, we need to act outside of ourselves.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Most of the items on the must-do list will take time before these come into fruition.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Reforming an economy is an enormous task, one that the government, even in theory, cannot do by itself.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Governments govern, or better still, guide.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: But it is the economic and business community that creates commodities and services, builds the economy and competes in the global market.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: I take heart in the fact that our business leaders in MAP remain a stalwart partner of the government in making economic progress possible.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Personally, I am optimistic that our hard work and resourcefulness will allow us to overcome our remaining economic problems.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: As a people, they say Filipinos have a knack for turning adversity into opportunity.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: My caution is that we should not always welcome adversity to be able to turn it into opportunity.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: I believe that by responding to the challenges with a deeper sense of purpose, by adhering to "country above self" as a guiding principle, we can reach our full potential.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: By all means, we have what it takes to succeed.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: The outgoing officers and board members of the MAP, congratulations on a job well done, and to the new officers, I wish you all the best!
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Thank you very much.
label: negative

title: The Philippine Economy: The Continuing Challenge
text: Mabuhay tayong lahat.
label: negative

title: New Year Message 2006
text: An Overview of 2005 All of you present here tonight are our stakeholders and we are happy to report to you that....

label: negative

title: New Year Message 2006

label: negative

title: New Year Message 2006
text: What's in store in 2006 The new year gives us a fresh opportunity to do things better, not only for our respective institutions but also for our country Of course, you and I know we have a long way to go before we can truly say everything is... a-ok more than anyone, you know.
label: negative

title: New Year Message 2006
text: Our economic fundamentals: our strong points.... label: negative

title: New Year Message 2006
text: The main risk we see for domestic demand is high oil prices, which have already taken some of the buoyancy out of consumer spending last year rising oil prices also continue to be the key source of risk to inflation, although the strong peso and the easing of food prices should help balance inflationary risks.

label: negative

title: New Year Message 2006

label: negative

label: negative

title: New Year Message 2006
text: In the pipeline are the issuances of the guidelines on the implementation of Basel II Accord, and the new financial reporting package in line with the adoption of international accounting standards.
label: negative

label: negative

label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Distinguished officers and members of the Pioneering Rotary Service in Asia, the Rotary Club of Manila (RCM), esteemed guests, ladies and gentlemen, good morning.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: My father never wanted us to go into public service.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: To him, public service seems to be a thankless job and not worth the effort.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: There are better ways to serve your country, so to speak.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Accordingly, I started my professional banking career in the private sector.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: The stint led me to many places and many cultures.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: I became the first Filipino senior executive at Citibank.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: I moved on to be President of one of the major commercial banks.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: I had the prestige, the money and the life my father had envisioned for me.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: When I accepted to take the helm of the country's central monetary authority in July 6, 1999, some people asked me if I was a hundred percent sure about leaving my comfort zone as a private banker and taking on the role of a regulator and public policy maker with less pay but more headaches.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Looking back, I was only sure of two things: I defied the wishes of my father and I took up the biggest challenge of my life.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Having done so, I am now privileged to stand before you as a Central Bank Governor and most importantly, as a public servant.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: After the 1997 financial crisis, restoring stability in the financial system was of paramount importance and the road that needs to be traveled was long and winding.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: I am proud to say that I made the right decision by accepting the invitation to serve my country and having the privilege of working with highly dedicated and dynamic professionals of the Bangko Sentral.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Barely five months short before the end of my term as Governor, we are racing against time to complete the enabling reforms we have started.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: The recent appointment of Central Bank Deputy Governor Say Tetangco [as my successor] clearly indicates the continuity of our broad set reform initiatives.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: My talk this morning is centered on one of our major key challenges: capital market development as a vital component of the financial reform agenda for sustainable economic growth.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: The economy in brief Let me first give you an overview of the economy to put things in perspective.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Overall, we started the year with sound economic fundamentals.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: The country's gross domestic product (GDP) posted the highest growth of 6.1 percent in 15 years.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Our prudent monetary policy, geared towards inflation targeting, kept inflation relatively low at 5.5 percent and the Bellweather 91-day Treasury bill rates better than target at 7.3 percent for the year ended 2004.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Our peso rallied strongly against the U.S. dollar, trading between P54-55/U.S.$, amidst sovereign rating downgrade jitters and political noise.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: We have a stable reserve position with our gross international reserves (GIR) maintained at a comfortable level of U.S.$16 billion in 2004.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Moreover, our external sector significantly improved with our balance of payments (BOP) deficit 85 percent lower than programmed at U.S.$77 million while remittances from overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) reaching almost 12 percent growth in 2004 compared to the 6.3 percent growth rate in 2003.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: The country's economic performance benefited directly from improving fiscal discipline and sound monetary policies.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: We expect to keep the momentum going for 2005 with GDP growth sustained between 5.3 to 6.3 percent, inflation subdued between 5 to 6 percent beginning March 2005.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: In the external sector, BOP deficit is projected to stay moderate at U.S.$464 million in 2005 and the GIR level maintained at the same level with expected 6 percent increase in OFW remittances.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Capital market development imperatives With bright economic prospects, I keep asking myself, 'What keeps us from making the domestic capital market work'?
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: In the last few years, I have become even more convinced of the necessity of developing the capital market.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Thus, I have made rounds with various gatherings such as this, weekends notwithstanding, drumming up support for a cause that I personally believe can benefit all.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Today, my message is the same --- capital market development in the Philippines has long been overdue.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: I am close to becoming redundant but I will keep on pushing if this can make a difference.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: In the race to develop the capital market, our Asian neighbors have steadily outpaced us.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: As a result, countries like Malaysia and Thailand have much bigger savings-to-GDP ratios than the Philippines.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: They have left us biting the dust.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: While their debt papers are predominantly private, government papers dominate the local capital market with minimal alternative for other financial instruments.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: A strong financial system with deep capital market does not put the banks out of the picture but rather diversifies their role from just basic lenders to distributors and sellers of various securities.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Compared to them, we are more prone to external shocks due to our excessive dependence on the local banking system.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: With majority of the domestic credit sourced from banks, borrowing becomes a more expensive endeavor because of the added intermediation cost.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: With a functional capital market, we can cut down intermediation cost and reduce risk exposure of banks as savings become directly available to investors.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Challenging the status quo Capital market development complements our current banking reform agenda as it fosters resiliency in the financial system to withstand external shocks while it promotes investment opportunities towards domestic savings and economic stability.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Our core banking reform strategy at the Bangko Sentral is focused on progressive monetary policies, internationally accepted regulatory practices and enhanced bank supervision.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: We initiated the asset clean-up of banks to finally restore the credit supply to the economy.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Non-performing loan (NPL) ratio improved to 13.7 percent in November 2004.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: The current NPL ratio will be further trimmed to 10 percent or lower by year end cognizant of the 2005 economic growth projections and the P26.2 billion asset clean-up that prospered in 2004 under the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) Law.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Other key initiatives aimed at strengthening the banking sector include the upgrading of capitalization and risk management standards, institutionalization of corporate governance and transparency, improvement in consumer protection and enhancement of regulatory information exchange through the financial stability forum.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: These initiatives are instrumental in aligning our banking practices with globally accepted standards.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: We have also designed our banking sector reform package to complement the capital market development, recognizing the necessity for the banking system and the capital market to work in tandem for the benefit of the financial system and the economy as a whole.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: The Bangko Sentral issued various circulars aiming to diversify the financial products available in the capital market like the unsecured subordinated debt (as Tier 2 supplementary capital), long term negotiable certificate of deposits or LTNCDs, documented repos, structured debt, and collaterized debt obligations in order to create market-oriented opportunities for banks and other players.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Coupled with existing rules and regulations governing investments in marketable securities, this initiative can further deepen the capital market.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Revitalizing the trust business to boost the demand side and widen investor base was also undertaken with the replacement of the common trust fund (CTF) with unit investment trust fund (UITF) where the value of investments are marked to market to enhance the credibility of pooled funds to investors.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: We are also encouraging the entry of rating agencies to complement the establishment of an exchange traded papers.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: As a critical player in the capital market, rating agencies ensure investor protection particularly in discovering fair prices commensurate to risk.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Future directions The task of running the remaining miles in our reform package still requires much work and endurance before we reach the finish line.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: We have done much of the groundwork.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: What is needed now is a strong follow through.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Businesses and investors alike require equally functioning bond and equity market to cater to their diverse needs and preferences.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Establishing the fixed income exchange, as the enabling platform for fixed income and debt instruments, responds to that need.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Moreover, the exchange promotes greater transparency and market-to-market transactions in accordance with globally accepted practices.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Another aspect is setting up of basic market infrastructure that underscores the required legal, regulatory and taxation frameworks including securities trading, clearing and settlement frameworks.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: We have started with the issuance of guidelines on third party custodianship and the implementation of modern real time gross settlement system or PhilPaSS for large value transactions.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: These broad frameworks are central to the desired efficiency, integrity and transparency particularly in the elimination of systemic risks in the capital market for greater investor protection.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: These efforts aim to strengthen market public's confidence in a highly speculative market.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: In the same vein, we need to strengthen the existing regime of capital market-inducive regulation through legislative reforms.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: We have made progress with the passage of the Securitization Law, SPV and the elimination of documentary stamp tax in secondary trading but these are not enough.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: The Bangko Sentral is committed to actively join the lobby for the passage of the following measures aimed to promote capital market development: the amendment of the BSP Charter, Corporate Recovery Act, Revised Investment Company Act, Revised Corporation Code of the Philippines, Insurance Code of the Philippines and Pre-Need code of the Philippines.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: At this point, we have already stepped our best foot forward with the enactment of the Securitization Law enabling the launch of asset backed instruments to support housing development with long-term financing at fixed rates.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: In addition, a larger pool of institutional investors like insurance companies, mutual funds, UITFs and pension funds can also provide the required boost to the market.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: We made progress with the accreditation of Philratings but we need more rating agencies to come in the future.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: They serve as guides to investor decision and accountants for disclosure requirements.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: A well-functioning capital market also need strong issuers to expand the variety and supply of instruments supply that people can invest in.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: The National Government, as the country's largest issuer, did the necessary spadework by creating liquid benchmarks and developing a yield curve.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Using these as basis for pricing other long-term maturity issues, I am encouraging big, private corporations whose leaders are present in the audience today, to issue quality papers and support our advocacy on capital market development.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Indeed, meeting life's challenges is always a rare opportunity to test the limits of human endeavor.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: In hindsight, it gives me great honor that I was given the privilege to initiate change and challenge the prevailing status quo through the Bangko Sentral's sturdy ship of reform-minded professionals.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Taking the helm and steering it towards our collective goal comes with ease.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: In particular, thank you rotary club of manila for coming aboard and sharing with us your enthusiasm on banking reforms and development of the capital market.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: We need your support as we relentlessly pursue the remaining points in our overall banking reform package.
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: Thank you and more power!
label: negative

title: Taking Up the Challenge
text: (Note: Regular Membership Meeting, Rotary Club of Manila, 17 February 2005, Makati Shangir-La Hotel)

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: It is my great honor and pleasure to speak before the FINEX today, a stalwart partner and moving force, in shaping our domestic financial system.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: Indeed, I am happy to note that your incoming president is one of our own.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: Today, allow me to focus on my presentation mainly on our efforts to strengthen our financial system and develop, in particular, our domestic capital market.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: It is pleasing to note that 2005 started off with a slew of very good economic data.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: First of all, 2004 GDP growth is expected to reach more than 6% on account of increased private consumption and exports; robust services and agriculture growth despite increased inflationary pressures in the second half of the year.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: The fiscal accounts are more or less in line with program.
label: negative

text: This has prompted recent declines in the bell weather 91-day Treasury bill rate.

text: Our dollar reserves ended at a very comfortable level US$16.1 billion, at the high end of our target range.
label: negative

label: negative

label: negative

text: However, in order to sustain all of these positive developments in the long-run, we must continue our concerted efforts in further strengthening the financial system, particularly, the development of the domestic capital market.
label: negative

text: Without this, the whole package of reforms being shepherded will not be sustainable in the future and we will constantly be in a roller-coaster ride.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: A more stable and stronger financial sector ensures a more efficient mobilization of capital and resources.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: These are in turn channeled to the best and most productive investment activities thereby supporting higher economic growth.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: With a stronger domestic financial system, the economy will become more resilient in coping with negative external shocks and disturbances and less vulnerable to contagion and reduced access to international capital markets.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: Furthermore, monetary policy will be able to operate more efficiently as a wider array of market-based tools become available for calibrating economic activity and maintaining price stability.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: A fundamental initiative of the BSP to support capital market development is the shift to inflation targeting, and the higher level of policy transparency that it requires, as basis for the conduct of our monetary policy in achieving price stability.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: A stable price environment is a central pillar towards securing overall macroeconomic stability, in turn a necessary pre-condition to capital market development.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: Although recent acceleration in inflation has been mostly supply side driven, the BSP remains very cautious with its monetary policy stance while retaining the flexibility to support economic growth.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: This is the usual balancing act that is the traditional measure of the mettle of a central bank.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: But preserving price stability is really a cooperative endeavor and the government has responded with measures to mitigate supply-side pressures through increased price monitoring of staple foodstuff, ensure supply of commodities through higher productivity in agriculture and industry, and lessening dependence to imported fuel and energy prices.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: The BSP has launched major reform initiatives in the banking sector where we have direct responsibility as its supervisor.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: Key initiatives include strengthening corporate governance and transparency, clearing-out non-performing assets and strengthening bank balance sheets through better liability management and recapitalization, upgrading risk management standards, and improving consumer protection.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: Consistent with these objectives, we have been systematically aligning our regulations with key international standards such as the Basle Committee recommendations on supervisory practices and on capital adequacy, the IAS/IFRS Standards for the proper accounting and disclosure of financial transactions, OECD principles on good corporate governance.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: We are likewise closely consulting with our peer central banks and bank regulators to learn from their rich experiences.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: These have yielded a slew of regulatory changes and others yet to come that will radically change the rules of the game for our banking industry.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: For the better, we are convinced.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: We believe that the changes will also further hasten the long overdue consolidation in our banking industry that is essential to make it stronger.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: The rigors of international standards and the growing presence of international level competitions will inexorably hasten the exit of weak institutions that are unwilling to reform.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: The proposed amendment of the BSP Charter is a very critical element in the banking reform agenda.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: We are particularly seeking changes to strengthen the institutional arrangements for banking supervision that will enable us to fully comply with best international practice.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms

label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: Without these vital amendments, we will be unable to properly enforce the reforms embedded in the regulatory changes.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: These are very basic arrangements that are widely adopted internationally, precisely to achieve a healthy banking system.

label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms

label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: We hope that the FINEX collectively can help us in this effort that is so vital to strengthening the financial system.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: There are other pieces of vital legislation that we should all be working closely together on to have enacted.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: One of these is an improved bankruptcy framework through the proposed Corporate Recovery Act.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: We are in critical need of a modern framework for orderly resolution of failed organizations that even-handledly settles potentially conflicting interests of borrowers and creditors.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: A bias for the former will lead to a weak financial system while a bias for the latter will sow the seeds of inequity and instability.

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: Other important pieces of legislation are oriented to furthering the development of the domestic capital market.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: These include the proposed RICA and PERA bills.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: Even more basic is the necessity to re-think the whole approach on the taxation of the various financial instruments to encourage a deep capital market that is able to offer a wide array of investment outlets catering to diverse risk preferences and investment objectives.

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: I understand this is now the subject matter of a comprehensive study in preparation for a specific legislative proposal.

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: The high degree of interconnectedness of our financial system has compelled the BSP to play a more active role in developing the domestic capital market and to collaborate more closely with other financial regulators.

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: Let me mention a number of key initiatives.

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: One initiative is to broaden the array of available capital market instruments such as Tier 2 Paper, LTNCDs, documented repos, structured debt, collateralized debt obligations, and credit derivatives.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: We have gone out of our way to overhaul our regulations to allow financial innovation but under appropriate risk management standards.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: On the demand side, we have initiated a major reform of the trust business beginning with common trust funds that are being converted to a better product called the unit investment trust fund (UITF).
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: Other managed funds are next in line primarily to create a wider domestic investor base where both sophisticated and unsophisticated investors can participate under adequate safeguards.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: We are also encouraging the entry of high quality rating agencies, a critical actor in a capital market that is transparent and efficient in discovering fair prices commensurate to risk.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: In the last few months, we have struggled to operationalize the fix income exchange [which FINEX and other organizations are major stakeholders] and to institutionalize an independent securities custody system that will improve investor protection, defeat market malpractices such as multiple selling of securities and undocumented transactions, and reduce systemic risk overall.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: Sad to say, we encountered fierce resistance from some market players and even government provider.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: Fortunately, that issue now appears to have been decisively resolved by the Department of Justice to allow BSP-accredited third party custodians to finally operate.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: I hope all will now act with goodwill to achieve full implementation as soon as possible.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: We have already wasted too much time.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: Why is the third party custody system so vital to the reform effort?
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: It's really very simple.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: To an important extent, the root of current problems lie in the basic fact that securities already sold by dealers remain undelivered to investors and effectively stay under dealer control.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: By requiring delivery of securities directly to investors or their designated independent custodians, we hope to break the back of bad practices that rob our domestic capital market of its credibility to investors.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: The new system will also lead to greater investor empowerment by allowing them more flexibility to choose the best possible price from the market and break free from the stranglehold of potentially leonine dealer partnerships.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms

label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: One such initiative in this direction was the creation of the Financial Sector Forum or FSF last year.

text: Composed of the BSP, SEC, PDIC and Insurance Commission, the FSF is currently undertaking its agenda of harmonizing supervisory and regulatory efforts, strengthening of the exchange of information among the different regulators and promotion of better consumer protection.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: We intend to continuously strengthen this coalition.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: The road ahead for full financial system reform is indeed still long and complex.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: It is a historic struggle seemingly most genteel but no less tougher than military battles fought with real blood and tears.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: It is a struggle against entrenched interests that seek to preserve the mediocre status quo that has led our country's financial system to nowhere.
label: negative

title: Deepening Domestic Financial Reforms
text: We appeal for the full support of our reform-minded financial professionals, the kind of professionals that FINEX has placed under its wing.

title: Opening Remarks

label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Conducting monetary policy in the present economic environment is a considerable challenge for the BSP.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: The continued rise in inflation during the last few months has led to public concern over its likely effects on both the public's purchasing power and economic activity.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: In our previous public statements on monetary policy, we have been careful to emphasize that the inflation uptrend over the past year has been driven mainly by supply-side factors arising in large part from a series of shocks coming from the sharp increases in oil prices, food and other key non-food commodities particularly fuel and transport.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: This view has led to the BSP's prevailing policy stance of accommodating the supply shocks which are one, transitory in nature and two, if addressed by monetary action, could have adverse impact on growth and in turn inflation itself.
label: negative

label: negative

title: Opening Remarks

label: negative

text: The expected path of future inflation continues to be hump-shaped, as supply factors push headline inflation above the 4-5 percent target in 2004 and 2005 before quickly tapering off and reverting to the 4-5 percent range by 2006.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: We find no compelling reason, therefore, to modify the settings for monetary policy at this time.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: In closing, let me emphasize that the BSP remains strongly committed to good monetary policymaking.

label: negative

text: We anticipate further expansion in microfinance activities in the banking sector judging by the applications for microfinance-oriented banks that are currently in the pipeline, and by the number of banks that have expressed their intention to set up branches for their microfinance operations.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Even as we strongly encourage the establishment of more microfinance-oriented banks, our focus is not merely confined to statistics.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We also aim to provide the appropriate policy and regulatory environment for continued viability and sustainability of microfinance institutions.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Without sound financial and credit policies, microfinance can never be an effective intervention for poverty alleviation.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: With this goal in mind, we are building up on our current initiatives to mainstream microfinance within the BSP and the banking community.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: BSP microfinance agenda Creating an enabling policy and regulatory environment High on the list of BSP's agenda on microfinance is the continuous review of existing policies and regulatory guidelines to make them even more attuned to the growing needs of the microfinance sector.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We believe that with a well-defined vision and strategy for microfinance, we can easily identify and fully address the capacity development needs of microfinance players.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Initially, we have defined our policy agenda which is to encourage the establishment of new microfinance-oriented thrift and rural banks and the setting up of microfinance operations in existing banks.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Through this approach, the banking system can more effectively reach a larger number of e-poor.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This would complement other microfinance delivery channels like credit cooperatives and NGOs that have their own strengths and weaknesses.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Three important provisions in the General Banking Law (GBL) of 2000 formally authorized the BSP to fully support microfinance.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In carrying out this mandate, we have drawn up a set of banking regulations that take into consideration the peculiarities of microfinance lending: cash flow-based, typically unsecured and short-term, high frequency collections, and often featuring group guarantee and other non-traditional forms of security.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Specifically, the BSP has issued the following circulars: Circular 272 (January 2001) implements the provisions of Sections 40, 43 and 44 of the GBL and sets out the regulatory guidelines for engaging in microfinance.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Circular 273 prescribes additional requirements for licensing of microfinance-oriented banks.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This was issued primarily to encourage banks to adhere to best practices and high performance standards.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Another requirement is for the organizers to have a good track record in microfinancing.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: As a minimum operational requirement, banks should have a loan tracking system in place that can adequately monitor and manage a microfinance portfolio.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The same circular also provided for the partial lifting of the moratorium on the opening of new thrift and rural banks and branches to allow the entry of microfinance-oriented banks.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Circular 282 (April 2001) specifies the guidelines governing the rediscounting facility for microfinance loans of rural and cooperative banks.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Circular 324, issued in 2002, expanded the coverage of the rediscounting facility to include thrift banks.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In relation to this, we have provided rediscounting for 26,966 micro-borrowers amounting to P219.5 million, as of end-July 2004.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We have issued several other regulations to provide further incentive to banks to engage in microfinance in a sustainable and prudent manner.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: These are:< /p> Circular 340, circular 365, and Circular 369 which further liberalized the rules and regulations for the establishment of bank branches provided these are microfinance-oriented.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Circular 409 prescribes guidelines for the measurement of portfolio-at-risk and the respective provisioning requirements to ensure sound and prudential microfinance operations of banks.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: To complement these regulatory initiatives, we are also strengthening our ability to supervise the activity of microfinance-oriented banks.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We are currently finalizing revisions to the BSP manual of examination to incorporate microfinance operations.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We have started to train a core group of bank examiners knowledgeable in microfinance operations.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We are also intensifying our efforts, in partnership with the national credit council, to set up a credible and comprehensive credit information bureau.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We have just completed the first phase of the project which we highly think will greatly benefit microfinance practitioners, in terms of promoting stronger credit discipline and reducing the risk of credit pollution.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Enhancing training and capacity building Another priority area in the BSP microfinance agenda is our continuing training and capacity building program for bank examiners, officers and employees, as well as the microfinance practitioners, in the banking sector.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This is being implemented through a series of trainings, workshops and study tours.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: For the benefit of the banking sector, the BSP has begun incorporating microfinance into the basic rural and thrift banking courses.So far, these courses have already been offered to 1,500 participants.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In June 2004, we launched a series of seminars designed to educate banks on the importance of internal controls, performance standards and best practices for sound microfinance operations.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: To further augment our capacity to effectively supervise microfinance activities within the banking sector, we have created a top-level microfinance committee to oversee BSP's microfinance initiatives.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Likewise, we have set up a microfinance unit within the BSP to implement and coordinate all microfinance activities.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We are among the first central banks in the Asia-Pacific region with a permanent office dedicated to microfinance.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Encouraging promotion and advocacy Our ongoing initiative on microfinance is also focused on promotion and advocacy.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In 2003, we launched a regional advocacy program where we conducted microfinance seminars in strategic regions in the country.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: To date, we have been successful in conducting information seminars for a total of 1,350 participants in 9 regions across the country.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Our advocacy program is aimed at encouraging potential practitioners from the banking, cooperative and NGO sectors, as well as establishing links with corporations, foundations and international organizations that could lend support to existing microfinance institutions (MFIs) by way of technical assistance and other capacity development needs.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: All of these initiatives underscore BSP's strong commitment to promote the development of microfinance.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Concluding remarks Let me just point out that although the BSP's mandate is to focus on the banking sector, our involvement in microfinance extends beyond the banking community.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We are also interested in working with other microfinance practitioners and organizations, such as NGOs and credit cooperatives, so that together we can ensure the long-term viability and sustainability of microfinance.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Possible areas for collaboration include the transformation of non-bank MFIs into banks, development of a uniform set of standards, and the promotion of best practices for sustainable operations within banks, NGOs and cooperatives.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: It is vital that we pool our resources if we are to achieve progress in this crusade against poverty.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: On that note, I would like to wish everyone a pleasant day and a meaningful discussion ahead.
label: negative

text: (Note: 2nd International Forum on Microfinance, INAFI-Philippines, August 25, 2004, PRRM Building, Quezon City)

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Ladies and gentlemen, good afternoon: 1.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Introduction I have been asked, in my capacity as member of the Government's Economic Management Team, to speak to you today about the new tax initiatives of the Arroyo administration.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: I can understand SEIPI's interest in the Administration's planned tax initiatives.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Taxes, after all, are a part of business costs.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: And just as Keynes used to argue, there are only two great certainties in this world: death and taxes!
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Your Government proposes to expand the tax base and increase tax collection.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: This is the bad news.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: The good news is that doing so, while admittedly painful in the short term, would arrest the incredibly large decline in the tax effort ratio and the significant climb in public sector debt.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Let me cite a few numbers.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: The budget deficit of the National Government has been on a rising trend in the past decade, from less than 1 percent of GDP in 1995 to 5.2 percent of GDP in 2002.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: This was driven in recent years by higher-than-programmed expenditures and, more importantly, revenue shortfalls due to below-target tax collections, changes or lack of changes in tax policy, and to some extent, reductions in the tariff duties on imports.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: [1] the overall result has been a rising level of Government debt, as the Government resorted to borrowing to compensate for the financing gap.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: The total stock of debt for the National Government alone has grown from P1.2 trillion or 61 percent of GDP in 1995 to P3.4 trillion or 77 percent in 2003.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Such levels of fiscal deficit and public debt are generally considered to be high for an emerging economy like the Philippines.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Unless we can tame the fiscal deficit and reduce our public debt, our growth prospects for the medium term are significantly at risk.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: You would not want to see recession and reduced capacity of your Government to provide the general public with basic public goods and services!
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: The message is clear.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Reducing the fiscal deficit and public debt is the most urgent and critical task facing our country today, and raising fiscal revenues should be the Government's main strategy for achieving this.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: It will enable the government to have enough funds for key budget items such as infrastructure, education, health and other basic services.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Infrastructure spending, in particular, is important for enhancing our international competitiveness and ability to achieve sustained growth over the medium term.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Closing the fiscal gap will also help raise the level of national saving, free up funds for investments, prevent a buildup of inflation expectations, reduce domestic interest rates, and restore investor confidence in the country's macroeconomic fundamentals.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Let me clarify an important issue of tax administration.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: While we expand the tax base, we shall not stop intensifying tax administration.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: We shall address the issue of graft and corruption as much as we shall run after tax cheaters and evaders to plug the reportedly large tax leakage.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: And so, with due apologies to my colleagues at the Department of Finance, let me now describe to you, in broad terms, the package of fiscal measures being planned by the government.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Sustaining macroeconomic stability 2.1 medium-term objectives The new tax initiatives are best viewed as part of a broad, comprehensive package of fiscal measures aimed at the following objectives: (1) achieving a balanced NG budget in six years; (2) reducing the CPSD from more than 6 percent in 2003 to 3 percent of GDP in six years; (3) reducing the public sector debt in line with the NG deficit and CPSD reduction; and (4) meeting these objectives without sacrificing economic growth targets.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: As I have indicated earlier, such goals require a two-pronged action plan that consists of, firstly, raising revenues through improved tax administration, adjustments in tax policies as well as new revenue measures, and secondly, controlling public spending through austerity measures, civil service reform, and better governance of GOCCs.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: 2.2 new tax policy measures Let me now run quickly through the new tax policy measures of the Government.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: The new measures consist of, firstly, legislative reforms designed to increase fiscal revenues and secondly, administrative reforms.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: The proposed amendments to existing tax laws are along the following lines: A two-step increase in the value-added tax (VAT) rate; Re-imposition of franchise tax on telecommunication companies; Adoption of a gross income tax system for corporations & business income-earning individuals; Rationalization of the system of fiscal incentives; Indexation of the excise tax on so-called "sin products"; Granting of a general tax amnesty conditional on the submission of statements of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN); Establishment of a lateral attrition system; and Increase of the excise tax on petroleum products.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: These reforms are mainly designed to stem the leakages in the tax system that have weakened fiscal revenue-generation over the years.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Fiscal incentives, for example, will be rationalized on the basis of how much they actually contribute to new investments.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Meanwhile, the proposed indexation of excise taxes will address the decline in the real value of excise tax revenues due to inflation.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Such measures have long been proposed by fiscal experts and economists, and the economic team believes that they are quite overdue.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Proposed administrative tax reforms include the following: Upward adjustments in the fees and charges of government agencies; Increase in duty on petroleum products from 3 percent to 5 percent, through an executive order; and Other measures to enhance the revenue-generating potential of selected GOCCs, e.g.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: PEA, PAGCOR, etc.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: These measures are expected to bring in some p10 billion in additional fiscal revenues.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: 2.3 fiscal discipline measures The other half of the fiscal deficit problem is government spending.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Fiscal authorities intend to bring fiscal expenditures under control through the following: (1) fiscal austerity measures, aimed at reducing non-essential expenditures; (2) civil service reform, aimed primarily at the rationalization of personnel services costs in the budget; and (3) improvement of management and control of the GOCCs and other government corporate entities (OGCEs).
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Proposed austerity measures include the abolition of inter-agency bodies not created by law; the giving of compensatory time-off for employees in lieu of overtime pay; the suspension of foreign and local travel; and the imposition of cost-cutting measures on utilities and supplies.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Measures on civil service reforms begin with the issuance of executive orders to trim the bureaucracy.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Functions that are either no longer relevant or redundant will be abolished, and employees will be offered a voluntary but time-bound separation scheme.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Authorities will also be submitting for Congress' approval a reengineering bill to reorganize the entire executive branch, including GOCCs, and offer the appropriate incentives to employees.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Also in the pipeline are bills to rationalize the government compensation and retirement system.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: The final item on the expenditure agenda is improvement of management and control of GOCCs, whose financial operations bear significantly on the public sector bottom line.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: An executive order is expected to be issued that will (1) improve oversight of GOCCs by their supervising departments or agencies as well as by the Office of the President; (2) establish a binding set of corporate duties and responsibilities for all presidential appointees to boards of GOCCs/ogces; and (3) impose a moratorium on the creation of subsidiary GOCCs pending an assessment of the operations of existing subsidiary GOCCs.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Concluding remarks In closing, I believe that our ability to reverse our poor fiscal position will be a key factor in determining the pace and sustainability of economic growth over the next several years.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Our ability to balance the budget and reduce our public borrowing will determine how much funds will be available for public investments, and how much resources will be allocated to key economic needs such as infrastructure, education and training, health services, and so on.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: A better fiscal performance will also be a key factor in strengthening investor confidence in the Philippine economy.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Concerns about the government's ability to manage the deficit partly prevents foreign capital flows, since investors think that the government may not have enough funds for the upgrading and maintenance of public infrastructure.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Good public infrastructure, after all, is a key ingredient to a sound business environment.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Reducing the public deficit to me is therefore one of the urgent and critical tasks for the government.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Raising revenues through tax initiatives is a crucial part of the strategy to bring the deficit under control.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Let us bear in mind, therefore, that the Government's tax initiatives are part of the Government's macroeconomic program to secure our economic growth prospects for the medium term.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: The other pillars of this program is the reform of the power sector, the reform of the financial sector, including the development of the capital market, and buildup in infrastructure and external competitiveness.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: It is, to be sure, a very difficult program, one that will require the support of every Filipino.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: And because the fiscal budget affects not only the delivery of government services but also inflation and national income, every Filipino has a stake in ensuring that our fiscal objectives for the medium term are achieved.
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: Always remember, no pain, no gain!
label: negative

title: Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability Through Fiscal Consolidation
text: We can help in these efforts not only through supporting the government's tax initiatives but also pushing our authorities and legislators to exercise fiscal responsibility and discipline.
label: negative
