title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: Introduction Distinguished officers and members of the Chamber of Real Estate and Builders Associations, Inc., ladies and gentlemen, good afternoon!
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: It is an honor and a pleasure for me to be invited by your Chamber to its monthly business meeting and on the occasion of the First National Socialized Housing Expo and LGU-Private Sector HousingConference.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: CREBA's work of more than thirty years in improving the standards of the different disciplines in the housing sector; in instilling among its members the social objectives and the public interest behind the business of real estate; in pushing for important pieces of legislation for the benefit of the different stakeholders in the industry; and in creating a foundation to complement the socially oriented housing projects of the government, has firmly established itself as a strong and reliable partner of the government in the implementation of the national shelter program.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: Today's choice of theme is very appropriate.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: Housing and the LGU projects that support it at grassroots level will undoubtedly act as a catalyst for economic recovery.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: An active housing sector has positive linkages to many other industries in addition to its direct employment generation and unquestionable impact on the quality of life of people by meeting a very basic necessity.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: On the other hand, successful LGU projects on housing, the door for which was opened by the local government code of 1991 and the urban development housing act of 1992, have proven the capacity of the local governments to undertake housing developments and take the lead in land use planning in their respective jurisdictions.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: Bangko Sentral actions As Bangko Sentral, our basic contribution is the control of inflation as the foundation for macroeconomic stability.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: This is the critical pre-condition to a healthy housing market.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: Average inflation in 2003 has been cut to just 3.1 percent.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: For 2004, we expect inflation to range between 4-5 percent.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: As a result of the success in controlling inflation in the last five years, we have seen lending rates reaching their lowest levels in twenty years.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: Lower interest rates were achieved notwithstanding the impeachment of a president, street protests, military coup, and the overshooting of our budget deficit by a substantial amount, among others.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: Although the peso has depreciated during this period amid many uncertainties, its overall volatility has been kept under control.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: In spite of weak exports and minimal foreign direct investment, we managed to minimize peso volatility to 29 cents or half a percent as of July 2004 and peso has depreciated by only 3.2 percent.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: But we realized that achieving price stability, low and stable interest rates and a relatively stable currency are not enough.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: We are taking other actions to contribute more directly to the national shelter program, support the housing sector, and the economy as a whole.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: It is known to all of us that one of the major factors stifling the growth of a more robust industry is the inadequate supply of long-term housing finance.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: The ability to structure mortgage payments affordably is vital in the decision to invest in housing because of the huge upfront cash outflow it typically requires.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: The lack of financing effectively restricts demand for housing.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: This situation can be remedied by a deep and strong capital market, which opens sources of long-term finance.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: There are other compelling reasons for Bangko Sentral to have vital interest in the full development of the domestic capital market particularly the undeveloped debt market.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: The capital market will encourage more domestic savings by broadening the array of investment opportunities to match actual investor preferences.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: For the same reasons the capital market will help keep domestic savings on shore as well as attract foreign institutional investors.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: It will promote the resilience of the financial system by having an alternative pillar to cushion against external shocks, contagion and possible reduced access to international capital markets.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: Today, about 98 percent of domestic credit is still being channeled through the banking system, while in other countries such dependence had been reduced to less than 60 percent.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: This situation makes the banks vulnerable to cyclical downturns and other economic shocks.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: We have seen this in 1997 that resulted in an outbreak of bad loans.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: Banks are still struggling to get rid of this burden that continues to hamper new lending and undermine profitability and solvency.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: A stronger capital market ultimately supports a stronger banking system even though it would inevitably change the nature of the banking business.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: Our banks will have to improve their ability to compete for the public's savings as well as widen their array of lending products and other services.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: The competition is healthy and long overdue.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: For Bangko Sentral, a strong capital market will enable monetary policy to operate more efficiently by providing us with more market-based tools to fine-tune economic activity and maintain price stability.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: Developing the capital market Developing the domestic capital market needs our collective effort and our clear vision to overcome the short-term challenges and pains that it may entail.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: We need a better legal framework to lay down clear and transparent rules that allow widest possible participation by the investing public under proper safeguards.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: We need to strike a fairer balance between the interest of debtors and creditors to nurture a sustainable market.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: We need to provide financial regulators with adequate powers and sufficient legal protection to effectively police the system and to protect particularly the small depositors and investors.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: We need to re-think our taxation framework to remove the distortions that have stunted the development of an efficient and continuous financial market that ideally spans seamlessly the full range of financial products and transactions across the maturity spectrum and into secondary markets.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: Short-term markets are just as important as long term markets because they provide the liquidity that makes the capital market deep and robust.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: We need to put in place basic financial infrastructure for the orderly and efficient trading, clearing and settlement of securities transactions as well as proper protection of investors through the use of independent registries and custodians.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: And most important of all, good corporate governance must be achieved all around.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: To be sure, real progress is finally being made as never before although much remains to be done.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: The enactment of the Securitization Act of 2004, an initiative that Bangko Sentral keenly supported, is a very promising development that can directly support the housing sector.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: It will allow banks and other primary credit providers to sell the mortgages for repackaging into securities that can be sold to a much wider investor base.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: Moreover, the Securitization Law also provides incentives and institutional mechanisms for the secondary trading of such securities.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: As experiences in other countries has shown, this will set the stage for increased volume of financing for the housing sector at better terms: lower amortization due to longer repayment period, greater predictability of payment obligations, and lower contractual interest cost.
label: negative

title: Housing as Catalyst for Economic Recovery
text: The implementation of the SPV Act, primarily designed to help banks clean up their non-performing assets so they can start lending again, also creates additional opportunities for the housing sector.

title: Mind the Gap
text: Ladies and gentlemen, good afternoon.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: All of us gathered here this afternoon are direct stakeholders in our country's capital market, but the ultimate stakeholder of capital market development is of course our economy.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: The economic literature has always emphasized that limited access to capital presents a critical challenge to economic growth and stability.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: It is therefore imperative to establish a well-functioning domestic capital market to ensure that corporations efficiently mobilize capital for economic growth.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: In the normal course of things, an active money market should first be established in order to develop markets in foreign exchange and government securities.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: A well-developed government debt market consequently facilitates the development of capital markets (that is, market for long-term corporate debt, equity, and asset-backed securities).
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: In the Philippines, our money market is fairly liquid.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: Latest figures we have on money market transactions, for instance, show that volume of transactions was about 73% of GDP.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: Our government debt market, on the other hand, is significant in size due to regular issuance of debt by the government with sizeable volume and variety of tenor.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: Last year, outstanding government securities amounted to p1.7 trillion, or about 39% of last year's GDP.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: Despite these, our corporate equity and debt markets have been lagging behind.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: Last year, value of transactions in the Philippine stock market was only 3.4% of GDP.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: Worse, corporate bond issuance was only 0.2% of GDP during the same period.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: It seems that in the Philippines, development of the capital market is not a natural consequence of the development of the government bond market.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: There seems to be a gap that separates the two.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: In thinking of ways to develop our capital market, we should therefore be always mindful of this gap and how to bridge it.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: From where I stand, the challenge involves increasing market liquidity by widening the base of domestic investors who will buy the securities that local public companies issue.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: Increasing the number of investors entails fostering the growth of savings.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: Fostering savings, in turn, require a sustainable macroeconomic environment, i.e.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: Low inflation environment.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: I am proud to say that the Bangko Sentral has been successful on this front.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: Average inflation last year has been cut to just 3.1% and the prospects for contained inflation this year despite recent developments are quite good.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: Widening the investor base also involves enhancing the transparency in the market.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: The availability of reliable and timely information on market players complements regulatory oversight by promoting market discipline.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: However, before one can enhance transparency, the accounting standards need to be improved.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: To address this, the BSP and the sec have both committed to implement IAS 39 and IAS 32 by 2005.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: Lack of reliable public information on the creditworthiness of corporate entities can also be remedied by the development of the credit ratings industry.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: The BSP has already recognized the sole credit rating agency in the country, and is now reviewing the application for recognition of one foreign rating agency.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: However, the presence of all these information would be all for naught if the investors are not educated about the methods for assessing the relative merits of the different instruments in the market.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: Towards this end, the BSP has formed a consumer education committee to design a comprehensive action program to strengthen financial literacy of consumers, as well as of key influence groups such as the mass media.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: Notable progress is being made.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: We have already made a major upgrade of our payment system by putting in place the Philippine RTGS or PhilPaSS.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: In addition, the BAP's fixed income exchange is scheduled to open this month.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: On the regulatory front, we are set to launch later this afternoon, also here in the Executive Business Center, the Financial Sector Forum which will seek to deepen coordination among its four participating agencies, namely: the BSP, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the Philippine Deposit Insurance Corporation (PDIC), and the Insurance Commission (IC).
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: But in all these, we must not forget to continuously improve the corporate governance standards in the Philippines as this serves as the foundation in the further development of our capital market.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: Ladies and gentlemen, I thus wish you well in this workshop.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: May the session this afternoon be a productive exercise in identifying ways to advance capital market development in the Philippines.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: Thank you very much.
label: negative

title: Mind the Gap
text: (Note: Opening Remarks.

title: Inspirational Message
text: Introduction I appreciate this opportunity to speak to you about the BSP's assessment of prevailing conditions in the Philippine economy.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: As a central banker, I take advantage of every chance to communicate the BSP's views about inflation, the exchange rate, and other aspects of the economy with members of the business community.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: A central bank, after all, must consider itself ultimately accountable to the public, by virtue of the wide influence that it wields over the economic life of the nation.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: As such, central bankers have a duty to actively promote public discussion of economic issues that affect the welfare of businesses, consumers, wage earners, and other groups.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Today I have the privilege of exchanging views with distinguished members of the Canadian and American business community in the Philippines.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Most of you, I am sure, are no longer strangers to the intricacies of doing business in this country.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: What I would like to do, therefore, is to outline the BSP's views on what we may expect over the next year or so.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: My hope is that my talk will provide you a balanced assessment of the Philippines' economic prospects.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: I intend to focus mainly on the variables that directly influence the cost of doing business in the Philippines--inflation, interest rates and the exchange rate--things that are also of primary interest to the business community.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: 2. Review of recent developments Let me begin with a brief look at the recent developments in the economy.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: In the first quarter of 2004, the Philippine economy sustained its growth momentum on the strength of vibrant domestic demand.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: GDP grew at a robust pace of 6.4 percent, while real GNP grew by 6.2 percent from its year-ago level.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: This was driven mainly by consumer spending, which grew by 5.9 percent in the first quarter, stronger than the 5 percent rise recorded a year earlier, on account of election-related activities as well as increased OFW remittances and higher farm income.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Export growth has also picked up due to the recovery in the world's major economies and our increasing trade with china.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Most encouragingly, gross domestic capital formation rebounded to 16.2 percent after a contraction in the previous three quarters.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: This recovery was supported by investments in agricultural and industrial machineries, an improvement in construction spending and a build-up in inventories.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: On the production side, the three major production sectors, agriculture, industry and services all registered higher growth rates in the first quarter.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: The agriculture sector posted a year-on-year increase of 7.7 percent, the fastest pace in 15 years, on account of the impressive growth in the fishery sector and the strong rebound in rice production.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: The services sector likewise posted a strong growth of 6.4 percent in the first quarter from 5.5 percent a year earlier due to sustained expansion in transport, communication, and financial services.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Meanwhile, industry also accelerated to 5.5 percent in the first quarter from 4.8 percent in the previous quarter, with manufacturing expanding by 4.3 percent on stronger consumer spending and export demand.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Low inflation provided a supportive backdrop for stronger growth.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Average inflation in the first five months of 2004 was 3.8 percent based on the 1994-base year CPI data and 4.1 percent using the new 2000-based CPI series.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Both averages are near the lower end of the government's inflation target of 4‑5 percent for 2004.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Despite the encouraging trends in growth and inflation, there remained some soft spots in domestic economic activity.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: The manufacturing sector, for example, continues to operate at below full capacity, with average capacity utilization at around 79 percent as of march 2004.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Unemployment also remains relatively high at 11 percent as of January.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Conditions for credit also appear to be relatively modest, as shown by the weak growth in total commercial bank loans, which has dwindled to less than 1 percent in march 2004.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: The weak loan growth has been traced to the climate of political uncertainty and the prevailing levels of non-performing loans which have compelled our banks to remain cautious in granting new loans.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: As a result, growth in the money supply or m3 also remains relatively weak, despite a mild recovery in April.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: The sluggishness in credit conditions has been accompanied by a moderate rise in market interest rates compared to the start of 2004.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: The average 91-day Treasury bill rate has gone up from 6.2 percent in January to 7.1 percent in May.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: The increase has been accompanied by a rise in average bank lending rates from 9.1‑10.9 percent as of end-January to 9.9‑11.9 percent as of end‑may.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: In part, this uptrend also reflects the concern among investors about the ability of the national government to meet its fiscal targets in an election year, and more generally about the sustainability of the fiscal position over the medium term.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: On the plus side, the peso has begun to recover after a period of election-related uncertainty and increased dollar demand.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: The nominal exchange rate averaged at P55.84 against the U.S. dollar in may from P55.98/US$1 in January-March as political concerns eased after the elections and higher inflows from overseas remittances added to the supply of dollars in the system.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Outlook and challenges Against such a background, what kind of performance can we expect from the economy in 2004?.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: I believe that our growth performance will continue to be robust in 2004 on the strength of private consumption spending on the demand side and strong performance from the agriculture and services sector on the production side.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: These sectors will propel GDP growth toward the 4.9 percent target for the entire year.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: As for inflation, our latest assessment at the BSP suggests that the outlook for inflation in 2004 remains consistent with the 4-5 percent inflation target for the year.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: However, supply-side factors such as transport fare adjustments, utility rate increases, and rising energy prices along with possible wage adjustments pose risks to consumer prices in 2005 and may cause an uptrend in average inflation above the 4-5 percent target.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: However, since the expected pressures on prices over the next year or so originate mainly from the supply-side, they are largely outside the influence of monetary policy and do not represent permanent shifts in the long-run path of inflation.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Therefore, the prevailing risks to inflation do not require a monetary policy response from the BSP.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Moreover, we believe that the continuing patterns of sluggish credit demand and moderate investment growth imply that the monetary policy stance should continue to support the economy and provide adequate stimulus to credit activity.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: The relatively modest improvement in investments constitutes a downside risk to the sustainability of growth in the medium term, and implies a need for caution in setting policy rates in the future.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Monetary authorities recognize the need to preserve the stimulus to economic activity, and accordingly have kept the BSP's policy interest rates unchanged since July 2003.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Nevertheless, the outlook for market interest rates will continue to be influenced by financial market perceptions of how well the government is doing in its efforts to manage the budget deficit.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: I am a bit optimistic in this regard, given the recent improvement in revenue performance.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: However, the incoming administration will need to follow this up with other revenue measures, and carefully explain to the public the critical importance of the fiscal measures that need to be put in place.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: The NG's performance in fiscal reform will also be important for the exchange rate.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Movements in the exchange rate in the near term will continue to be tied to market sentiment on the government's commitment to critically needed structural reforms that will ensure continued growth in the medium term.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Exchange rate volatility will be lessened by the strong inflows from remittances, but it can be minimized through forceful reforms not only in the fiscal sector, but also in power, infrastructure, and others.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Concluding remarks To sum up, there are good reasons to expect the Philippine economy to perform well in 2004, given robust consumer demand and a generally supportive macroeconomic environment.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Over the longer term, however, the outlook for the economy depends mainly on how well the incoming administration is able to transform the electoral mandate and investor goodwill it has received into forceful measures to balance the fiscal budget, improve the investment environment, raise productivity, and enhance the country's competitiveness.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: The Bangko Sentral, for its part, intends to support these structural reform efforts by strengthening the banking sector and ensuring a sound monetary and financial environment for business and investment through prudent monetary policy.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Let me now end by thanking the Canadian and American chambers of commerce for the opportunity to share my views on the Philippine economy.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Your continued presence in the Philippines strengthens my belief that investors are able to see through all the political noise and continue to believe in our economic potential.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: It is my hope that you will stay the course with us as we march on toward sustainable growth for the long term.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: Thank you and good day.
label: negative

title: Inspirational Message
text: (Note: Joint Luncheon Meeting, Canadian & American Chambers of Commerce), June 09, 2004, Manila Peninsula Hotel, Makati City)

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: It is an honor for us to participate in this high-level discussion on corporate governance of banks.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: In the aftermath of the 1997 Asian financial crisis that saw several banking systems around the region come under stress, we have embarked on a wide-ranging set of banking reforms in the Philippines to better insulate the economy from future crises.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: In our view, improved corporate governance in the banks and other financial institutions that we supervise is the most fundamental of these reforms.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: BSP's Governance Reform Agenda Our reform agenda is centered on promoting greater adherence to the enhanced standards on transparency, accountability, and fairness.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: At the bank organization level, we have made it very clear that this is to be led by the board of directors in which final authority and full responsibility is vested.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: It is a sad and disturbing reality that at the root of most bank failure cases we have encountered, the failure of board oversight in the face of insider abuse has been a recurring theme.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: The comprehensive amendment of the General Banking Law in year 2000 has given us the critical foundation to pursue governance reforms more vigorously.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: In particular, the amendments provided us the clear legal basis to enforce fit and proper standards for the qualification and disqualification of bank directors and key officers.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: The law also required a minimum of two independent directors in an effort to counter-balance potential insider abuse.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: We have parlayed these basic legal requirements to reinforce the corporate governance framework of banks, including defining the duties and responsibilities of bank directors, individually and as a collective board.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: In 2002, we launched a mandatory orientation program for bank directors, outsourced to reputable training organizations, with the objective of familiarizing them on their primary duties and responsibilities particularly on risk management oversight.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: These responsibilities involve setting policies and strategies, identifying key risk areas, and monitoring corporate performance as a means to achieve growth, profitability and financial stability.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: Failure to attend this training is a ground for the disqualification of a director.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: It is imperative that bank directors know and understand the nature and scope of these oversight responsibilities.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: Directors should also not be able to offer the excuse that they do not know what's going on.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: With the growing complexity involved in running a bank, regulators need to work even more closely with the board directors who are in a far better position to monitor bank activities.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: As regulators, legal and physical limitations make it extremely difficult to closely monitor bank behavior especially in preventing insider abuse.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: Building on these early initiatives, we are taking steps to encourage professional certification of bank directors to raise the standards further and maintain the professional and ethical practice of bank directors.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: Many of our new regulations on enhanced risk management in line with Basel Committee recommendations necessitate directors to improve their competencies.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: We are especially advocating more training on specific aspects of corporate governance, particularly with regard to the proper functioning of banks' audit committees, risk management committees, and governance systems, in compliance with global standards.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: Accreditation of external auditors Another key aspect of our corporate governance reform agenda is to focus on the critical role of independent external auditors in promoting financial transparency.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: In particular, external auditors should be able to provide an objective assessment of the effectiveness of controls over financial reporting and disclosure.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: In order to better achieve this objective, we issued new guidelines in October 2003 prescribing the rules and regulations that shall govern the selection, appointment, reporting requirements and delisting for external auditors of banks, their subsidiaries and affiliates engaged in allied activities and other financial institutions subject to BSP supervision.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: These build upon ground rules adopted earlier in may 2000.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: The key principles of these rules and regulations include avoidance of conflict of interest situations, periodic rotation of audit partners, affirmative reporting responsibilities to bank supervisors of significant issues and adherence to international accounting standards and practices.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: In order to strengthen credit risk management in banks, we are also working with the Securities and Exchange Commission to strengthen financial reporting standards of banks' corporate clients.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: Very clearly, substandard and unreliable financial reports prejudice sound credit decisions that end up ultimately hurting everyone through reduced credit access and higher cost of credit.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: The idea is to create strong incentive for corporate borrowers to use only external auditors that are committed to upholding proper auditing and accounting standards.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: Those entities that opt not to abide by this discipline will have to pay a price by way of adverse credit treatment.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: Once these new guidelines are fully implemented, we hope to raise the level of professional standards in accounting and auditing to promote greater financial transparency not only to the regulatory authorities but also to the broader public.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: Shift to International Accounting Standards In support of promoting greater financial transparency, the Philippines is also preparing to shift to International Accounting Standards or IAS by 2005.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: With respect to banks, the BSP has set in motion a process to migrate our banks to this accounting standard subject to the resolution of certain issues that are now being discussed at high level between the IASB and the international banking industry.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: Credit Bureau and Credit Rating Agencies The BSP is also seeking to improve overall transparency in the financial system by sponsoring the formation of a central credit information system as a means not only of improving credit access and lowering borrowing cost, but also to promote a strong culture of responsible borrowing.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: Complementing this initiative, we are likewise encouraging the formation of domestic credit rating agencies to strengthen market discipline.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: Enhancing Financial Literacy The BSP is complementing its efforts to improve overall transparency with a program to empower financial consumers through a well-targeted financial literacy program.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: The objective of this program is to enable the public to properly use the financial information being provided to achieve more informed decisions and enhance market discipline.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: Further Regulatory Reforms I would also like to update you on our continuing efforts to upgrade our prudential standards in a manner that promotes bank transparency.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: In this regard, our most recent initiatives involve better measurement and disclosure by banks of their credit concentrations particularly to connected parties.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: These new rules expand considerably on long-standing limits by requiring measurement and reporting on a consolidated basis.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: Role of Compliance System and Compliance Officers Strengthening bank governance also calls for improved standards on accountability.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: In line with this, we have required banks to establish a compliance system that is intended to ensure a bank's identification of relevant laws and regulations, analysis of risks of non-compliance and prioritization of compliance risks.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: We are presently looking into a proposal to further rationalize the compliance system on the basis of recent recommendations made by the Basle committee.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: Basically, the proposal concerns the compliance function and how it can be duly upgraded to conform to corporate governance best practice.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: Conclusion All of the above corporate governance initiatives form an integral part of the BSP's broader banking reform agenda that aims to strengthen the financial sector and reduce overall vulnerability.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: As the supervisor of the banking system, the main challenge for us at BSP lies in ensuring the basic safety and soundness of banks.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: In response to this challenge, we fully intend to be an active proponent of better corporate governance.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: Building a culture of corporate governance at the institution level can help create a stronger and more effective financial intermediation.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: In time, this can lead to an environment that is conducive to sustained growth and economic stability.
label: negative

title: Corporate Governance Reforms in the Banking Sector
text: (Note: High-Level Working Meeting on the Corporate Governance of Banks, May 13, 2004, The Guildhall, London)

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: Ladies and gentlemen, good afternoon.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: Introduction I am extremely grateful for this opportunity to join your regular membership meeting today.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: As a central banker, I very much welcome every opportunity to promote public debate on medium-term issues concerning the Philippine economy, and for this reason I hope you will allow me to use this occasion as a venue for discussing a very timely and important economic issue.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: With due apologies to Finance Secretary Juanita Amatong and my colleagues at the Department of Finance, I would like to offer to you today some thoughts on the budget deficit.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: Over the last several years, there has been a significant buildup in the budget deficit of the National Government.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: This has caught the attention of policymakers, economists, financial market participants, and international observers alike.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: I believe our fiscal performance is a key factor in determining how the Philippine economy will grow over the next several years, and reducing the public deficit is therefore one of the urgent and critical tasks that will be facing the winner of the May 2004 Presidential election.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: This afternoon, therefore, I will depart from discussing monetary and banking policies in order to highlight the challenges in public finance which, to be sure, will have important ramifications on monetary conditions and the sustainability of economic growth.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: Current situation The budget deficit of the National Government has been on a rising trend over the past decade, from less than 1 percent of GDP in 1995 to 5.2 percent of GDP in 2002.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: As a result, there has been a rising level of government debt.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: What are the numbers?
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: The total stock of NG debt alone has grown from P1.2 trillion or 61 percent of GDP in 1995 to P3.4 trillion or 77 percent in 2003.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: Such levels of fiscal deficit and public debt are generally considered to be high for an emerging economy like the Philippines.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: I have to indicate to you that sizeable fiscal deficits in the Philippines in recent years have been driven mainly by shortfalls in revenue and higher-than-programmed expenditures, a fatal combination.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: Such shortfalls have been traced to lower tax effort by collecting agencies, changes or lack of changes in tax policy, and to some extent, reductions in the tariff duties on imports.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: [1] National Government tax revenues have fallen from a peak of 17 percent of GDP in 1997 to 12.3 percent in 2003.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: At the same time, the level of government spending has remained steady at an average of 19 percent of GDP during the period 1995-2002, even as fiscal authorities have tightened every belt over the last few years to manage public spending in order to meet the fiscal targets.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: The steady growth in expenditures in recent years despite cutbacks in government wages and capital outlays have been partly traced to increases in interest payments and transfers to Local Government Units (LGUs).
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: Let me quickly add, however, that our fiscal authorities have made very encouraging progress in recent years, thanks to better tax collection, stronger tax administration and prudent public spending.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: In 2003, the National Government posted a below-target fiscal deficit and this was due largely to higher-than-programmed revenue collections.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: The NG recorded a P199.9 billion fiscal deficit in 2003, P2.1 billion below the target for the year and 5.2 percent lower than the 2002 deficit of P210.7 billion.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: The 2003 NG deficit was equivalent to 4.6 percent of GDP, even lower than the 4.7 percent target.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: Total revenue collections in 2003 rose to P626.6 billion, exceeding the revenue target by 7.3 percent and last year's collection level by 10.5 percent.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: All these numbers are without doubt impressive accomplishments.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: For 2004, the NG fiscal deficit is expected to decline further to P197.8 billion, equivalent to 4.2 percent of GDP.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: Current government medium-term targets envision a progressive decline in the deficit to near zero by 2009.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: Why is the budget deficit a problem?
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: Why do we need to put our fiscal house in order?
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: Impact on growth.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: The most obvious impact of large fiscal deficits over the medium term is on economic growth.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: The decline in revenues has compelled our fiscal authorities to make significant cutbacks in public spending.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: As a result, capital outlays by the National Government have been pushed down from 2.0 percent of GDP in 1997 to only 1.6 percent in 2001.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: The reduction implies that the Philippines is spending even less on infrastructure when it is already lagging behind its Asian counterparts.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: Capital expenditures in the Philippines averaged at 16 percent of total government spending in the 1990's, compared with the Asian average of 25 percent for the same period.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: [2] The lack of adequate public infrastructure can significantly impede the expansion of private investments over the medium term, and can therefore harm the prospects for overall growth in the economy.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: Impact on inflation.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: Equally important from the BSP's perspective, the practical experience of many industrial and developing countries, including the Philippines, suggests that large fiscal deficits also contribute to inflation.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: This is based on the economic theory that governments running persistent deficits have to, sooner or later, finance those deficits with money creation (or seigniorage), which produces inflation.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: This theory has been supported by empirical evidence.
label: negative

title: Some Thoughts on the Budget Deficit
text: A recent IMF study involving data on 107 countries (including the Philippines) over the period 1960-2001 uncovered a strong positive correlation between fiscal deficits and inflation among high-inflation and developing country groups, but not among low-inflation and advanced economies.

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: Secretary Jose Isidro Camacho, guests, colleagues in the financial industry, ladies and gentlemen, good morning.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: I am pleased to take this opportunity to assess with you some of the important initiatives in mobilizing long-term capital in the Asian region, notably the creation of a regional market for debt instruments.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The necessity of developing the Asian bond market The Asian region has recovered relatively swiftly since the financial meltdown experienced starting 1997.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The resulting improvement in macroeconomic performance and the mechanisms for regional cooperation that were either established or strengthened during the recovery phase bolstered the pursuit of joint economic initiatives among the countries in the region.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: One of the recent joint initiatives by Asian economies is the development of a regional bond market.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: Pursuing this would require drawing several lessons from the experience during the financial crisis of 1997-1998.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The first lesson is the need to avoid the "double mismatch" problem namely, currency and maturity mismatches.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The second lesson is the need to reduce the corporate sector's over-reliance on the banking sector for funding its projects.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: To address these concerns, the monetary authorities in the region are working towards the upgrading of their individual bond markets and the development of an Asian bond market.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: A well-developed Asian bond market will enable the efficient utilization of savings within the region by serving as a channel through which available long-term savings are matched with long-term investment needs.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: It will help mitigate maturity and currency mismatches as fund users are allowed to borrow in their own currencies and channel long-term funds into carefully chosen projects.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The development of a regional capital market will also promote the preservation of foreign capital and savings in the region.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: This will help stabilize capital flows and thus avoid a repeat of the 1997 Asian crisis.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: A two-pronged approach in developing the regional bond market Beyond words, the authorities in the region are now pursuing a wide range of initiatives to develop the regional bond market.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: These efforts are being undertaken on two fronts.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: At the local level, national authorities are undertaking measures to accelerate the development of their own domestic bond markets.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: At the regional level, a region-wide bond market is being developed.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: It is envisioned that well-developed local bond markets will eventually form the nucleus of this pan-Asian bond market.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: Development of local bond markets An increasing number of east Asian countries have been giving the development of their own capital bond markets a high priority in their reform programs.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: Some countries began by addressing the major impediments in the development of their bond markets.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: Their efforts are focused on areas such as creating a benchmark reference rate and improving market infrastructure.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: In the Philippines, we are undertaking a host of measures to strengthen the local bond market in preparation for the establishment of a regional bond market.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: For example, the market infrastructure has been upgraded with the launching of a real time gross payment settlement (RTGS) system known as the Philippine Payment System or PhilPaSS in December 2002.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The PhilPaSS is intended to cover transactions in the equities, fixed income, money and foreign exchange markets.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The upgrading of our payment and settlement system is expected to minimize settlement risk and thereby allow primary and secondary markets to function more effectively.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) has also been supporting the establishment of the Fixed Income Exchange (FIE) that is tentatively scheduled to begin operations in the second quarter of 2004.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: This exchange will provide the platform for the secondary trading of private and public fixed-income securities such as government securities, commercial papers and asset-backed securities issued by companies.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The Philippines is also working towards an investment-friendly tax environment.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The BSP has been supporting the removal of the Documentary Stamp Tax (DST) on the secondary trading of financial instruments.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The DST increases the cost of financial intermediation and thus discourages the secondary trading of securities.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: A bill for its removal is now pending in congress.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The government has also issued 2-, 3-, 4-, 5-, 7-,10-, 20- and 25-year fixed rate treasury bond/notes over the past decade.This has resulted in a longer-yield curve for the public sector debt, providing the needed variety and various degrees of liquidity in the market.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The BSP recently approved the application of a preferential reserve requirement of 2 percent on Repo transactions of banks.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: This move will help reduce transaction costs and is expected to spur more activity in the secondary market for government securities.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: At the same time, the Philippine government has been pursuing measures to deepen the asset securitization market.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The BSP is supporting the enactment of the Securitization Bill, which will set the legal and regulatory framework for securitization in the Philippines.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: Another important element in developing the bond market is the presence of a strong credit rating system.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The mandatory rating requirement for all bond issues instituted by the Philippine government is expected to help in the assessment and pricing of risks and increase transparency for all bond issues.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: It should also induce demand for ratings services, making it a more profitable venture.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: To ensure that the quality of ratings and that the reliance of regulators as well as industry players on credit ratings are well placed, the monetary board of the BSP recently approved the rules and regulations that will govern the recognition and derecognition of domestic credit rating agencies for bank supervisory purposes.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The regulation prescribes minimum eligibility criteria, which include, among others, objectivity, independence, transparency, credibility, and compliance with internal procedures and certain disclosure requirements.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: At the same time it requires that credit rating agencies should have the financial capability to invest in the necessary technological infrastructure and employ sufficient professional analytical staff and thus ensure the proper discharge of their duties and responsibilities.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: Development of an Asian bond market On a regional basis, simultaneous efforts are being undertaken on two fronts--the demand and supply sides.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: On the demand side, the Executives Meeting of east Asia-Pacific Central Banks (EMEAP) created the Asian Bond Fund (ABF) initiative.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: In June 2003, the EMEAP-member countries launched the US$1 billion Asian Bond Fund for investment on dollar-denominated Asian Bonds (ABF1).
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: Currently, EMEAP is studying the extension of the ABFto a fund for local- currency denominated Asian bonds or the ABF2.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: This initiative is expected to serve as catalyst for private investors to consider investment in Asian issues.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: On the supply side, the ASEAN+3 and Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Finance Ministers' Meeting (APEC FMM) are addressing issues relating to, among other things, the issuance of new debt instruments, bond rating and enhancements and infrastructure improvements.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: Meanwhile, the Asian Cooperation Dialogue (ACD) has been providing technical support and helping in the dissemination process to gather critical political support.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: To deepen the regional bond market, there are initiatives to encourage the issuance of more sovereign bonds to improve liquidity in government bond markets and help establish benchmarks.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: Moreover, the floating of asset─backed securities linked to loan packages of banks or receivables by corporations is also being studied to widen the variety of instruments available in the market.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: Fair credit ratings are a key element for an active regional bond market.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: To improve the quality of credit ratings in Asia, an Asian Credit Ratings Board (ACRB) is being proposed, under the ASEAN+3 framework, to provide training to local rating agencies and collect regional data to ensure/improve the consistency and accuracy of ratings.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The ACRB is not intended to replace international rating agencies but is expected to complement their presence in Asia.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: The other aspects of an efficient market infrastructure are work in progress.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: One, bond settlement systems in individual countries should be improved to strengthen cross-border settlement mechanisms within the region.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: Second, the use of securitization and enhancements such as guarantees is being explored to reduce the difference in risk appetite of borrowers and credit ratings of issuers.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: Finally, efforts are also directed in narrowing the cross-country differences in the rules and regulations relating to bond transactions in the region.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: Differences in market regulations, documentary requirements and taxation, among others, translate into additional cost in doing cross-country investments.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: Conclusion Let me conclude by saying that the authorities in the Asian region are pursuing a comprehensive approach to the development--at both the local and regional levels--of Asian bond markets.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: Such initiatives are expected to benefit investors and market participants.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: In particular, the development of the regional bond market is a long-term endeavor and requires the active participation of the private sector.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: In fact, we have been receiving valuable inputs from private financial institutions and multilateral organizations on almost all fronts of institution and capacity building critical to developing an efficient regional bond market.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: We continue to count on their support in the future to transform this vision into a reality.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: Short of this, the Asian region will always be at the receiving end of the adverse shifts in the short-term funds from the banking system.
label: negative

title: Regional Initiatives in Developing the Regional Bond Market
text: (Note: "Asia Pacific Political Risk, Project Finance and Export Credit Summit 2003, Asian Development Bank, November 03, 2003, Shangri-La Hotel, Makati City)

label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: He said "...With careful and detailed planning, one can win; with careless and less detailed planning, one cannot win.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: How much more certain is defeat if one does not plan at all!
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: From the way planning is done beforehand, we can predict victory or defeat..." Last year, we hammered into place the BSP's vision and mission statements.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Guided by our vision to become a world-class monetary authority, we prepared a set of agreements to help us realize this goal.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: This year, our corporate planning office or CPO set out on an awareness program to make our employees claim ownership of the BSP vision and commit themselves to its pursuit.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: CPO went to our offices all over the country to cascade the BSP vision and mission statements to all employees and caused the mounting of posters containing the BSP vision and mission statements in all departments and offices.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: As you very well know by now, the recitation of the vision statement during the weekly flag-raising ceremony has been institutionalized, all the more to remind every BSPer of his commitment.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: More recently, our vision and mission statements were translated in Filipino "Para mas madaling isapuso".
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Strategic planning Today, we take off from there and plan some more to raise the probability of success in the achievement of our goals.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Indeed, I cannot overemphasize the importance of planning and planning well.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: In the late fifties and sixties, long-range planning was the trend.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Long-range planning is generally considered to mean the development of a plan of action to accomplish a goal or set of goals over a period of several years--the major assumption being that current knowledge about future conditions is sufficiently reliable to enable the development of these plans.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: More recently, however, as a result of a dynamic and changing environment, organizations have shifted to a new mode of planning, popularly known as strategic planning.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Strategic planning aims to ensure the organization's ability to successfully respond to environmental changes.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: More specifically, it helps an organization focus its energy, ensure that members are working toward the same goals, and assess and adjust the organization's directions in response to changed conditions.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Strategic planning is, however, just a management tool.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: It cannot substitute for the exercise of judgment by leadership.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: The leaders of the organization will ultimately need to sit back, ask and seek answers to the questions: "What are the more important issues to respond to?".
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: And "how should we respond?"
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: It is likewise important to note that strategic planning becomes useful only if it leads to strategic management.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: This means that plans are translated into actions through the formulation of: a) an organization's vision and mission in light of changing external factors; b) development of a competitive strategy to achieve the mission; and c) creation of an organizational structure which will provide the necessary resources to carry out the strategy.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: The task at hand In the next two days, we shall again be immersed in the strategic planning process to identify the programs and projects that would lead us closer to our vision.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: For the first time, we shall attempt to draft a medium-term plan for the bank, focusing on its core functions of maintaining price and financial sector stability.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: We shall also define measures that need to be adopted if we are to ensure effective banking services through an efficient currency management system and responsive branching operations.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: The successful implementation of all these action plans will hinge on the timely provision of adequate resources--man, machines and facilities.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: That is why we will hold another planning session specifically on organizational capability building one month after the completion of this conference.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: This will allow us to discuss fully the strategies that we need to implement to provide the resource requirements that will support the plans and programs agreed upon in the next two days.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Conclusion This is our second annual strategic planning exercise.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Hopefully, this exercise will make strategic planning become part of our daily routine to guide us though the complex decisions that we have to make as we work towards becoming a world-class monetary authority.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Finally, with your active participation, I trust that this strategic planning session will provide us with a clearer picture of where and what we want to be five years from now.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Thank you and good day.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: (Note: 2003 BSP Strategic Planning Conference (Part I), September 11, 2003, Executive Business Center, BSP)

title: Opening Remarks
text: Good morning friends, ladies and gentlemen of the Foreign Correspondents Association of the Philippines (FOCAP).
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Thank you for inviting me once again to your forum.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: When I met FOCAP members in July of last year, I just marked my third year anniversary as BSP Governor.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: I mentioned then that I was half way through my term as BSP Governor.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Today, I still have about 1 year and 10 months remaining in my term and I expect to finish my term.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Looking forward, in terms of economic performance we anticipate sustaining the momentum of the economic recovery despite some fluctuations in the financial markets.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: A review of the recent performance shows that the economy is indeed on a sustainable growth track.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: During the first half of the year, the economy posted a real GDP growth of 3.85 percent vis-à-vis the 3.97 percent growth in the comparable period last year.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: This expansion was remarkable in that it was achieved amidst external and domestic shocks, including the Iraq war, the outbreak of SARS and adverse weather conditions.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: In fact, the Philippines proved to be one of the most resilient in the region as some countries posted negative growth during the second quarter of the year.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: At the same time, year-on-year inflation eased anew to 3.0 percent in August from 3.3 percent in the previous month, bringing the average inflation to 3.0 percent for the first eight months of 2003.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: These figures are well below the full-year target helped mainly by steady food inflation, fairly stable non-food prices and prudent monetary policy.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: The benign inflation combined with lower foreign interest rates have enabled the BSP to relax monetary policy stance.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: BSP's policy rates, which were last changed on 15 March 2002, are now at 6.75 percent for the overnight borrowing rate and 9.0 percent for the overnight lending rate, the lowest levels since May 1992.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: This accommodative stance, together with the improved fiscal performance and ample liquidity in the system, was reflected mainly on the decline of market interest rates.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: The rate of the bellwether 91-day Treasury bill during the last auction was 5.225 percent.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Moreover, concerns over the ability of the National Government to meet the budget deficit have diminished with the marked upturn in revenue collections combined with the mindful forbearance in fiscal spending.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: For the period January-July 2003, the fiscal deficit amounted to P95.4 billion, compared to P131.8 billion deficit in the same period last year.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: In the banking sector, NPLs have continued to come down to 15.13 percent as of June 2003 from 15.33 percent a month-ago.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: However, we expect a substantial improvement in the level of non-performing assets of the banking system as banks seriously consider taking advantage of the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) Law to clean their balance sheets.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: A survey conducted by the BSP recently showed that nearly half of the 43 members of the BAP are in various stages of availing the incentives in the SPV Law through various avenues, which include among others, exemption from taxes and staggered compliance to the reserves provisioning of the BSP.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: In the foreign exchange market, we have recently experienced some volatility, with the peso-dollar rate averaging around the P55.06/US$1 in recent days from a year high of P52.54/US$1 in May 2003.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: This was due mainly to a combination of temporary, seasonal economic factors (e.g., higher dollar demand by importers, low foreign exchange inflows from OFWs) and non-economic factors (e.g., political issues and security concerns).
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: In response to the recent sharp depreciation of the peso, the BSP, on 28 August 2003, suspended for the second time during the year the tiering scheme for banks' short-term deposits with the BSP.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: The move is a preemptive monetary measure to prevent adverse impact in inflationary expectations.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: The suspension of the tiering scheme is expected to selectively siphon extra liquidity in the system which can be used for excessive hedging activities in the foreign exchange market.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: I will end my opening statement at this point.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: I now welcome any questions you have wanted to ask me.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: I also look forward to receiving comments or suggestions from you which I have always found to be insightful.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Again good morning and thank you for this opportunity.
label: negative

text: (Note: Foreign Correspondents Association of the Philippines, September 10, 2003, Mandarin Oriental Hotel, Makati City)

title: Keeping Faith in the Face of Adversity
text: Dear fellow workers at Bangko Sentral: I am overwhelmed...I really am so touched and overwhelmed by your support.
label: negative

title: Keeping Faith in the Face of Adversity
text: Salamat po sa inyong lahat.
label: negative

title: Keeping Faith in the Face of Adversity
text: As you all know, I was in the United States, representing our country on official business, when I learned of the court decision suspending me for one year.
label: negative

title: Keeping Faith in the Face of Adversity
text: You can imagine how shocking it was...for me and my family.
label: negative

title: Keeping Faith in the Face of Adversity

label: negative

title: Keeping Faith in the Face of Adversity
text: Let me tell you, it meant a lot to us to know that there are so many people who support and believe in us.
label: negative

title: Keeping Faith in the Face of Adversity

label: negative

label: negative

title: Keeping Faith in the Face of Adversity
