title: Anniversary Message
text: Today, as we celebrate the founding anniversary of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, we look back at how we as an organization braved the stormy weather of the past year since our last anniversary, and how we faced up to the difficult challenges to emerge a stronger institution.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: The eighth year of the BSP saw us continuously working to fulfill our primary mandate of maintaining price stability conducive to balanced and sustained economic growth.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: We faced serious shocks to the domestic economy, in the form of the rise in international oil prices to record levels and the volatility in the foreign exchange market, which saw the peso breach the P55 level against the dollar for the first time.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: We had to deal with the financial impact of domestic political tensions, as the nation grappled with questions about political leadership and public governance.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: It was a difficult time, to say the least, but the bank was able to rise to the challenge.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Indeed, where there are challenges, we do not see problems but opportunities.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: In response to the emergent inflationary pressures and the narrowing interest differentials that were contributing to the volatile exchange rate, we pursued a tight monetary policy stance through a series of increases in our key policy interest rates in may and in September-October 2000.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: The underlying objective of our actions at the time was to stabilize the economy.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: And true enough, as the foreign exchange market started to stabilize, we gradually eased monetary policy to help create a more supportive environment for business activity.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: This easing was continued with the resolution of the political crisis and the expectation of lower inflation.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Since December last year, the BSP has reduced its key policy rates by a total of 600 basis points.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: We also set about strengthening further our banking system, first by working on the implementing rules of the General Banking Law of 2000, which was signed into law in may 2000.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Various BSP circulars were issued pertaining to foreign stockholdings, outsourcing, microfinance loans and risk-based capital adequacy standards.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: At the same time, our examiners have also made the shift from a purely compliance-based and checklist-driven assessment of banks' conditions to a forward-looking and risk-based framework.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: These initiatives will help improve banks' risk management along with their ability to efficiently intermediate funds, and enhance their effectiveness as transmission channels of monetary policy.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: All these efforts have paid off in terms of improved fundamentals for our economy.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: At present, we have low and stable inflation, a sound banking system, and improving economic activity.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: The prospect of a benign inflation environment this year has enabled us to adopt an accommodative monetary policy to help stimulate investments and strengthen domestic demand.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Further monetary actions will continue to take into account the various risks to the inflation outlook so as not to jeopardize the stable, low inflation environment.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Meanwhile, on the homefront, we worked on the challenge of organizational renewal at the BSP and the task of improving ourselves as an institution.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: An institution is only as strong as the set of personal values of its members.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Thus, we successfully launched our work attitude and values enhancement program, which sought to impart the set of positive values that all of us, officers and employees alike, should have as public servants.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: We also saw to the needs of our own employees by providing various benefits and grants in the course of the year.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: For example, we increased the food subsidy and medical insurance and provided a transportation allowance for the non-SSL exempt class.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: We also marked another year of successful financial operations, which we are celebrating with contributions to the national coffers.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Over the past eight years, the Bangko Sentral has managed to remit more than P65 billion in dividends and taxes with an initial capitalization of only P10 billion.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: This does not include our dividend remittances to the National Government of P2.1 billion, which we will be presenting to president Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo this Friday.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: The funds should help build up government finances and help our fiscal authorities meet the fiscal targets for the year.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: As we complete another year in the unfolding history of the BSP, I feel greatly encouraged by our performance in the past 12 months with respect to our mandate of safeguarding price stability and the health of the Philippine financial system.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Theodore Roosevelt once said that the best prize in life is the chance to work hard at work that is worth doing.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: I believe that our pledged stewardship of the Philippine economy is of central value to our economic development.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: The local and international business communities recognize the BSP's efforts to keep prices low, the peso generally stable and interest rates reasonable as key elements in the performance of the Philippine economy.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: We must always keep in mind, however, that what made all of this possible was the human element--the unique individual contributions of all our employees, from the top rung to the lowest level of the organizational ladder.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Our mission at the BSP, therefore, is one that we must all pursue singularly, with a firm commitment to constant self-improvement and self-renewal.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Let me, therefore, congratulate all of you, my colleagues at the Bangko Sentral, for your hard work and your commendable performance.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: In the year ahead, we will again have our hands full.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Our preparations will continue for our planned shift to inflation targeting as a framework for monetary policy.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: The shift to inflation targeting will increase the accountability of the central bank and raise transparency in the conduct of monetary policy.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: It will thus help provide a credible and forward-looking policy framework that further strengthens our focus on price stability.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Last year, we worked hard for the passage of the amendments to the New Central Bank Act (R.A. No.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: 7653), but as you all know, we ran out of time in the last congress.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: This was one of the most anticipated pieces of legislation for most of us here, since these amendments will help us create a better and more competitive working environment at the Bank and help us attract the best talent available.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: More importantly, these measures will enhance our supervisory powers and operational independence, further improve prudential standards for the banking system, promote more competition in the banking sector.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: This year, we will redouble our efforts to push for these amendments when the new Congress begins its session.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: At the same time, we will also continue to push for further reforms in the banking system for improved risk management and more efficient financial intermediation.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: The BSP also supports the global drive against money laundering, and will push for the passage of a comprehensive Anti-money Laundering Law.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: This is in addition to the range of administrative measures that we have undertaken unilaterally to show our commitment to the global fight against money laundering.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Together, these measures are expected to avoid possible additional costs in our cross-border transactions and should have a beneficial impact on good governance.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: In addition to all this, our April 2001 corporate planning conference list of agreements contains various initiatives aimed at enhancing the BSP's image, improving corporate governance, and addressing human resource concerns.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: It is going to be a busy year, indeed.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Looking back at my experience so far as BSP Governor, I realize that the life of a central banker is not for those who desire an easy life.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: It is not for the timid, nor for the indolent.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: But as a wise man once said, "Do not pray for easy lives.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Pray to be stronger men.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Do not pray for tasks equal to your powers.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Pray for powers equal to your tasks.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Then the doing of your work shall be no miracle, but you shall be the miracle."
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: Maraming salamat at mabuhay po tayong lahat na bumubuo ng Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas.
label: negative

title: Anniversary Message
text: (Note: 8th Year Founding Anniversary, Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, July 03, 2001, Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Complex, Manila)

label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: These favorable trends augur well for overall economic performance for the year.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: At the same time, the recent stabilization of the domestic political situation and the peaceful change in political leadership have brought about renewed business confidence and restored stability in our financial markets.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: This broad stability has provided room for the gradual easing of the BSP's monetary policy stance.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: The series of reductions in key policy interest rates in December, January and February amounting to a cumulative total of 400 basis points effectively reversed the increases in October 2000 and brought down policy rates back to their pre-crisis levels.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: The resulting monetary easing should provide a supportive environment for business activity.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Outlook for monetary policy What do we expect for monetary policy for the rest of the year?
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Since February 12, the monetary board has kept the BSP's policy rates steady at 11.0 percent and 13.25 percent for the overnight RRP and RP rates, respectively.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: The Monetary Board will, however, continue to review the BSP's monetary policy settings, taking its cue from financial markets and other economic indicators before effecting further policy rate reductions.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: The important precondition for rate cuts in the near term is that price pressures remain subdued so that monetary policy action does not jeopardize the low-inflation environment needed to foster investment and growth.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: The overall direction for monetary policy in 2001 will thus depend on the assessment of the inflation path for the year.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Prevailing inflationary pressures remain relatively benign, and there are indications that cost-push influences may turn out to be weaker than previously expected.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: For example, the Department of Agriculture has reported that the dry spell associated with the el niño weather phenomenon this year may be milder than previously expected.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: This implies favorable food supply conditions which, in turn, would translate into stable food prices.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Nevertheless, some risks remain.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: On the external front, the slowdown in the U.S. economy will have a significant impact on emerging economies like the Philippines which have close trade and financial linkages with the U.S.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Concerns over the U.S. slowdown could be amplified by continued weakness in the Japanese economy and slow recovery in the Euro area.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: The prospect of lower foreign interest rates--as these countries try to rev up their economies --creates the risk of exchange rate volatility in emerging economies as interest rate differentials narrow.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: There are also talks of a new round of oil production cuts, which could lead to higher crude oil prices and create cost-push inflationary pressures.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: All these could pose a threat to the expected deceleration of domestic inflation in the second half of the year.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: On the domestic front, the main risks to inflation could come from the large fiscal deficit, although the government has committed to make fiscal discipline a key plank in its economic program.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: These risks highlight the need for greater vigilance on the part of monetary authorities to ensure that the price stability objective is achieved.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: For the year, the government is targeting an average inflation rate of 6-7 percent.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Moving towards inflation targeting Looking ahead, the BSP's efforts are focused on preparing for the shift to inflation targeting.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: As some of you may know, on January 24, 2000, the Monetary Board approved in principle the shift to inflation targeting as the framework for monetary policy.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Let me explain briefly the thinking that went behind the decision to adopt this framework.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Inflation targeting focuses mainly on price stability as the primary objective of monetary policy.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: This approach has several basic features.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: First, the central bank announces an explicit inflation target, which it commits to achieve over a suitable time horizon.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Second, monetary policy is forward-looking, since it is important for policy to react at an early stage to emerging inflationary risks.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Third, the commitment to an explicit inflation target improves the accountability of the central bank and raises transparency in the conduct of monetary policy, two common threads of good governance.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Increased accountability enhances the credibility of monetary policy, while greater transparency promotes the efficient functioning of financial markets which, in turn, leads to a stable and predictable macroeconomic environment.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Inflation targeting has attracted considerable attention over the past few years from central bankers, academics and other government policymakers.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Its growing appeal is based on two factors.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: First, for many countries, financial liberalization in the past decades has led to the weakening of the relationship between money and prices, and also between broad money and operating targets such as base money and reserve money.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: This has reduced the effectiveness of standard monetary aggregate targeting and prompted a search for an alternative policy framework.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Second, monetary authorities were encouraged by the success of the pioneer countries that have adopted inflation targeting.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Countries like Australia, Canada, Finland, Sweden, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, Israel and Chile moved from a high-inflation to a low-inflation environment and experienced higher output growth as well as reduced volatility in prices and output growth.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: This strategy has also been adopted in developing economies, notably Brazil and, more recently, Thailand.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Inflation targeting in the Philippines is expected to help advance the cause of economic reform.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Specifically, by helping ensure price stability, inflation targeting creates a stable macro environment for continuing reforms.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Moreover, the basic preconditions of inflation targeting--the primacy of price stability objective as the objective of monetary policy and central bank independence--are already in place.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Republic Act (R.A.) 7653 or the New Central Bank Act (dated 3 July 1993) explicitly identifies price stability consistent with a balanced and sustainable economic growth as the primary objective of the Bangko Sentral.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: The law specifically provides for the operational (or instrument) independence of the BSP.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: This means that the BSP is free to choose its own instruments, such as open-market operations, in the conduct of monetary policy.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Central bank independence also implies fiscal independence, or the absence of fiscal dominance.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: the BSP Charter provides for clear limits to any possible financial assistance of the BSP to the National Government.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Fiscal independence thus allows the BSP to pursue its main objective of price stability without being constrained by fiscal considerations.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Successful inflation targeting also requires a well-developed financial system, to ensure the effectiveness of the monetary transmission mechanism.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: The Philippine financial system has a long history of reforms, which should further strengthen the foundations and enable it to be an efficient channel for monetary policy.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: With the basic preconditions in place, the challenges of the shift to inflation targeting involve mainly the operational aspects of the new framework.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: We began last year with a series of public hearings on inflation targeting to promote better public understanding of the directions of monetary policy.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Other important operational issues include the use of the headline inflation rate as the measure of inflation and core inflation as the operating target.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Headline inflation is widely known and easily understood by the public, but is also subject to supply-side shocks that are beyond the central bank's control.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Thus, the BSP's announced targets would have to take into account the impact of supply-side shocks on inflation.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: This can be addressed through the adoption of a target band for greater flexibility.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Meanwhile, core or underlying inflation makes a good operating target since it excludes volatile CPI components, such as food and energy, that are subject to short-run disturbances.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Thus, it is affected mainly by demand factors that can be influenced by monetary policy actions.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: The National Statistics Office (NSO) currently does not publish a core inflation series, but work is now underway to construct an NSO definition of core inflation.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Effective inflation targeting also requires an accurate forward-looking assessment of inflation and output growth over the target horizon.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: This is to allow policy to react at a relatively early stage to emerging inflationary pressures.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: To this end, the BSP is at work on further strengthening its econometric modeling and forecasting capabilities with the development of a long-term macroeconomic model to complement its current short-term inflation forecasting models.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Lastly, measures to enhance BSP transparency include the adoption of annual inflation targets for the medium-term, publication of monetary board discussions pertaining to monetary policy, publication of a quarterly inflation report, and press releases on both policy actions and assessments of the monetary stance.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Concluding remarks In conclusion, improving economic conditions have allowed monetary easing to reverse the temporary tightening in 2000.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: This should help provide a supportive environment for economic growth objectives.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Nevertheless, the presence of upside risks to the inflation outlook requires policymakers to stand alert against threats to price stability.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: In this regard, the shift to inflation targeting this year will help provide a credible and forward-looking framework that further strengthens the central bank's focus on price stability.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: In closing, I would like to offer some words from U.S. Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan, who said in a recent congressional testimony: "A central bank can best contribute to economic growth and rising standards of living by fostering a financial environment that promotes overall balance in the economy and price stability."
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: In short, the chief importance of monetary policy is in creating the supportive economic conditions necessary for long-term sustainable development.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Through strategies such as inflation targeting, the central bank aims to contribute to broad macroeconomic stability through stable prices.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: This is the abiding commitment of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: Thank you and good afternoon.
label: negative

title: Moving Forward with Monetary Policy in 2001
text: (Note: Business Economics Club, University of Asia and the Pacific, March 07, 2001, UA&P, Pasig City)
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: The year 2000 saw the economy challenged from several sides.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: On the external front, world oil prices shot up to record levels, leading to higher transport costs and higher wages.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: A buoyant U.S. economy necessitated the tightening of U.S. monetary policy, which narrowed interest rate differentials and contributed to the generalized weakening of regional currencies.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: These adverse global developments were compounded by uncertainties on the domestic front, particularly in the political arena.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: Recent economic developments However, even in the face of domestic and international shocks, the economy managed to pull off a respectable performance.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: The recovery that started in 1999 was sustained in 2000 as real GDP grew by 3.9 percent and real GNP rose by 4.2 percent.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: Growth was broad-based, and, in terms of expenditures, exports and personal consumption were the main drivers.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: This moderate expansion in economic activity was realized amidst a benign inflation environment.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: Favorable weather conditions--which kept food prices generally stable in 2000--and the BSP's resolve to keep monetary aggregates within programmed levels helped keep inflation at bay.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: Inflationary pressures were evident toward year-end due to the series of oil price and transport fare increases as well as the depreciation of the peso, which fed into wage adjustments.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: However, due to good inflation numbers early on, the average inflation for 2000 remained low at 4.4 percent.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: In January 2001, year-on-year inflation rose slightly to 6.9 percent but it decelerated to 6.7 percent in February, bringing the average inflation to 6.8 percent, within the government's target of 6-7 percent for 2001.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: Moderate inflation provided the flexibility to keep interest rates low and stable in 2000. the 91-day t-bill rate averaged 9.9 percent in 2000, down from the 10.2 percent average in 1999.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: At the latest auction, the benchmark T-bill rate averaged 10.3 percent.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: Mirroring the trend in the T-bill rates, bank lending rates have also begun to ease.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: Starting December, the BSP has also reduced its own policy rates, as the financial markets showed signs of stability and in response to the future outlook on inflation.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: Lower lending rates are expected to steer the economic recovery towards a sustained path.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: In the external sector, the current account posted a hefty surplus of US$7.6 billion for the first eleven months of 2000 due mainly to the strong performance of exports which outpaced the growth in imports.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: The overall BOP position, however, recorded a deficit of US$918 million due to a weak capital and financial account.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: Meanwhile, as of end-January 2001, the country's gross international reserves (GIR) stood at $14.4 billion, equivalent to 4.2 months of imports of goods and services.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: With the speedy and peaceful resolution of the political crisis, and with the Supreme Court ruling on the legitimacy of the Arroyo administration, the peso appreciated to P47.812 on 05 March 2001, the strongest daily average reached this year.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: On the banking system, Philippine banks have been able to hold their ground amidst a challenging environment despite some stress here and there.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: Capitalization is more than adequate relative to international standards and the statutory floor.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: The banking system's capital-to-risk assets ratio as of November 2000 was recorded at 16.4 percent.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: The NPL ratio of commercial bank remains within the 15-16 percent range.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: As of end-December 2000, it dropped to 15.10 percent from a peak of 16.26 percent in November 2000.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: The real estate exposure of commercial banks also remains moderate at 12.3 percent of total loans (as of end-September 2000), well below the Bangko Sentral's ceiling of 20 percent.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: Recent policy initiatives On money laundering.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: A number of BSP issuances during the year reflected the efforts and commitment of the BSP in the international fight against money laundering.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: These efforts, however, have been circumscribed by the legal environment that the BSP has to work with.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: nonetheless, several administrative measures have been undertaken by the BSP to bring the country's regulatory regime on anti-money laundering closer to international standards.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: Among others, these measures included: 1) instructing FOREX corporations, which are affiliates or are subsidiaries of banks, to report details of all FOREX transactions; 2) requiring banks and non-banks to establish the true identity of their clients; 3) requiring banks and non-banks to report suspicious transactions; 4) prohibiting banks from issuing cashier's, manager's or certified checks payable to cash or numbered accounts; and 5) requiring FOREX corporations that are subsidiaries or affiliates of banks, quasi-banks and non-bank financial intermediaries to demand supporting documents from residents buyers if FOREX in amounts of $10,000 or more.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: In order to raise the awareness of the general public and the authorities concerned, the BSP and the BAP institute have and will continue to sponsor seminars on money laundering.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: In addition, the BSP and the BAP are currently working on guidelines for the proposal that will give banks and regulators the right to examine FCDU accounts under certain conditions.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: Under the plan, non-Philippine resident depositors will be asked to sign a voluntary waiver on secrecy upon opening an FCDU account in any Philippine-based bank.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: A number of initiatives are in place but these details may be discussed in the q&a portion.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: On economic development.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: The BSP has been supportive of the government's social development objectives within the parameters set by its charter.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: In particular, the BSP, in January 2001, released a circular to implement the provisions of the General Banking Law of 2000 with respect to microfinancing loans.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: These are small loans granted to the basic sectors, as defined in the social reform and poverty alleviation act of 1997 and other loans granted to the poor and low-income households for their microenterprises and small businesses.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: The BSP is also finalizing plans to open a rediscount window for rural and cooperative banks which lend to microfinance activities.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: This initiative is aimed at supporting rural and cooperative banks which have achieved efficiency in their microfinance activities, without sacrificing prudential standards.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: In September 1999, the BSP approved the opening of a rediscount window for banking institutions providing financing for socialized and low-cost housing.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: The measure supports the government's efforts to pump prime the economy through the housing sector, thus, helping bridge the gap in the supply of affordable housing especially to the underprivileged.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: Policy thrusts Going forward, the thrust of monetary policy will continue to be guided by the pursuit of the BSP's primary mandate of maintaining price stability conducive to a balanced and sustained economic growth.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: Towards this end, the shift to inflation targeting as the framework of monetary policy will be implemented.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: This is expected to improve further the transparency and consistency of monetary policy as well as the accountability of monetary authorities to the price stability objective.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: In the banking sector, the BSP will continue to improve its supervisory framework.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: This upgrading includes the adoption of a more forward-looking and risk-based bank supervision framework and the implementation of a consolidated supervision of financial conglomerates for a more comprehensive assessment of bank risks.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: The BSP will also continue to support the ongoing restructuring of the banking system, with a view to developing regionally if not globally competitive banks.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: Furthermore, the BSP will continue to work for the improvement in the legislative framework particularly the amendments to the BSP charter which, among others, will relax existing legal barriers to the fight against money laundering.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: In particular, a proposed amendment will allow the Monetary Board to look into deposits of more than P50 million in an individual account, provided that there is reasonable ground to believe that such an account is being used in relation to any fraud or irregularity.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: This effectively restores the authority of the Monetary Board under the Old Central Bank Act, which was deleted under the New CB Act, to inquire into a deposit account of a suspicious nature.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: In closing, I wish to thank the organizers of this meeting for the opportunity given to me to share with you my views on the Philippine economy and the future policy thrusts of the BSP in the areas of money and banking.
label: negative

title: Opening Statement
text: (Note: Breakfast Meeting, Foreign Correspondents Association of the Philippines, March 7, 2001, Manila Hotel, Metro Manila)

title: Opening Remarks
text: Mr. George Pickering, Chief Representative for Asia and the Pacific, Bank for International Settlements; Mr. Chee Sung Lee, Division Chief, Monetary and Exchange Affairs Department, International Monetary Fund; Mr. Enoch Ch'ng, Senior Director, Monetary Authority of Singapore; Honorable Dante Canlas, Secretary of Socio-economic Planning; panel discussants, members of the Monetary Board; co-workers at the BSP; distinguished guests; ladies and gentlemen, good morning: Let me begin by saying that I am deeply honored by the presence of many distinguished guests, and delighted by the attendance of friends and colleagues in the banking system, the business community, the academe and the government.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: This monetary conference is the second in a series that the Bangko Sentral has organized.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: In 1999, when the BSP held its first monetary conference, I was wearing a different hat.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: I was invited to serve as one of the panel discussants on the topic, Inflation Targeting: An Alternative Way of Achieving Price Stability.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: I was then the president of a commercial bank.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: The theme of today's conference--E-Banking: Challenges and Opportunities for Central Banks--is indeed timely.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: A barometer of the market's perception of its importance is the number of participants here and the broad spectrum of society that they represent.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: The exponential growth of the internet, which only a decade ago was limited largely to academic users, clearly shows that electronic technology has become very important to all of us.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Dramatic changes are occurring in central banking.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: They are, in fact, happening even as we speak because the environment has become so dynamic.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: In part, this is because we continue to grapple with globalization, which has brought about increased interdependence of markets and mobility of capital flows.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Admittedly, these changes are oftentimes hard to read but read them we must, so that we do not simply react to events that occur around us.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Instead, we must anticipate change.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: It is in recognition of this that I have always subscribed to the notion that it is better to anticipate change rather than to have it forced upon you.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: However, to be able to do so, one must first understand the nature of things.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Central banks must, therefore, be at the forefront of efforts to discern--even anticipate--the implications of this technological revolution on their own operations.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: There may be some nay-sayers, who have visions of a meltdown in information technology and its catastrophic effects on society.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: They will be, therefore, quite reluctant in recognizing the merits of e-banking.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: However, based on our experience with the Y2K millennium crossover, the largest danger that the year 2000 data change engendered came from the uncertain response of consumers and other market players rather than from any computer failures.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Moreover, it seems that this is no longer a question of whether we want to play the game--because this seems to be inevitable.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Rather, the question is how prepared are we as we are drawn into the game.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: The digital divide in technology puts a premium on knowledge.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: It is imperative, therefore, that we learn as much as we can regarding information technology and e-banking.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: This conference will hopefully go some distance towards satisfying these imperatives.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: The progress of e-banking will impact on monetary policy in various ways.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: For instance, e-banking will bring about changes in the structure of the real economy and this will influence the conduct of monetary policy.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: I.T.-induced changes to payment and settlement systems will also influence the effectiveness of monetary policy, and affect the central bank's day-to-day operations.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: E-banking will surely have an impact on financial stability.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: As more and more people embrace e-banking, payment and settlement systems become more and more dependent on physical information systems such as computers and communication networks.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Thus, bottlenecks in such systems, caused by purely technical reasons--not economic or financial ones--could ignite unwanted chain reactions in the payment system that could cause serious financial disruption.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: This would have important implications on the role of the central bank as the lender of last resort and as a repository of public confidence.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: The coming of age of e-banking will necessitate regulatory changes congenial to technological change.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Invariably, we may have to rewrite the rules of the game to be in tune with the challenges of e-banking.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: In fact, some steps have already been done in this direction.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: On May 5, 2000, the BSP has issued a Circular requiring banks to seek prior approval before they can be allowed to provide e-banking services.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: This will help ensure that these banks have the appropriate risk management systems accompanying their provision of e-banking services.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Meanwhile, increased private sector awareness of e-banking would prompt institutions to build up their capability to manage attendant risks, allowing them at the same time to maximize the resulting economic gains.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Greater interaction between the private sector and regulators in this kind of forum could also assist the central bank in formulating measures that are more responsive to the needs of market players.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: On a more general plane, we hope that this conference will go some distance in advancing the cause of economic reform, as the country prepares to join in the growth trajectory of the third millennium.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: We have an interesting day ahead of us as we discuss the issue of e-banking and how this will impact on its brick-and-mortar counterparts.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: I look forward to a fruitful and rewarding conference.
label: negative

title: Opening Remarks
text: Thank you and good morning to all of you.
label: negative

text: Mr. Norberto Nazareno, President of PDIC; Mr. Robert Porter, Consultant to ADB on Bank Supervision; Ms. Shamsad Akhtar, Manager, Financial Sector and Industry Division of ADB; distinguished guests, fellow workers of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, ladies and gentlemen, good afternoon.

text: First of all, I would like to personally commend the group which initiated the holding of this first "national" session of the APEC Bank Supervision Training Initiative.

label: negative

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?

label: negative

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?

label: negative

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?

label: negative

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?

label: negative

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?

label: negative

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?
text: Inflation averaged 3.6 percent for the first seven months of this year, as against a full-year target of 5-6 percent.
label: negative

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?

text: External payments risk managed through prudent external debt and international reserve management.

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?
text: Apart from a sound policy framework, the other aspect of macroeconomic management that has an important bearing on confidence in the financial system involves our ability to pay our foreign obligations on time.

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?

label: negative

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?
text: Finally, our commitment to a floating exchange rate system remains the best means of addressing foreign exchange risk, as this removes a one-way bet on the direction of exchange rate movements and ensures that the risk of exchange rate movements are borne by market players.

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?
text: The state of the banking system At the threshold of the 21st century, the Philippine banking system stands resilient and dynamic.

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?
text: Successive increases in the minimum capitalization requirement of banks and the consequent mergers and consolidations have resulted in bigger and better-capitalized banks.

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?
text: The banking system is also moving toward greater transparency and improved corporate governance.

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?
text: Overall, key indicators point to the system's continuing stability and growth.

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?

label: negative

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?

label: negative

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?

title: Confidence in the Financial System: How Do We Protect Our Investments?

title: Speaking Notes
text: Today I would like to offer my views on some of the recent developments in the foreign exchange market, in monetary policy and in the banking system as well.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: Recent developments on the exchange rate Let me start with a review of what has been happening in the currency market.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: The depreciation of the peso in the last two weeks of May was due to bearish investor sentiment toward the Asian region in general and, to some extent, local political factors such as the conflict in Mindanao.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: The negative sentiment on Asia was caused by the U.S. Federal Reserve's perceived bias towards raising interest rates in order to curb nascent inflationary pressures.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: As you know, an interest rate hike in a major industrial economy like the U.S. tends to draw away capital from emerging markets by narrowing the interest rate differential and encouraging a shift by investors to dollar-denominated assets.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: This, in turn, puts pressure on the exchange rate.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: Anticipating a narrowing differential between domestic and foreign interest rates, the BSP raised its key policy rates twice in May this year to keep up with rising U.S. interest rates.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: To date, the U.S. Fed has raised interest rates by 175 basis points since it adopted a tightening bias in June 1999.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: With its recent interest rate actions, the BSP effectively raised its rates by a net amount of 100 basis points during the same period.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: These measures notwithstanding, the peso briefly came under attack in late May, reaching an intraday low of P43.40 against the U.S. dollar at one point (25 May).
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: The adjustment shook the local financial markets a bit, but I think it is important to note that the peso reached a low of around P46 to the dollar in January 1998.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: Thus, the recent weakening has been comparatively mild and should not be a source of undue concern.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: Our position at the BSP was that the peso's recent movements have been mainly sentiment-driven and not based on fundamentals.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: This means that the changes are likely to be reversed in due time, given the Philippines' sound macroeconomic fundamentals.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: True enough, the peso has since recovered from its recent lows.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: Yesterday (13 June), it closed at P42.425 against the U.S. dollar at the PDS.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: For the rest of the year, the trend of the peso will depend on several factors.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: One is the corporate demand for dollars, which is expected to rise as economic activity continues to strengthen and imports pick up their pace.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: Another, of course, is the prospect of further increases in U.S. interest rates, which will depend on whether the U.S. economy slows down enough to convince the fed that further rate hikes are no longer necessary.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: In fact, sentiment appears to be building at the U.S. Fed that they May need to hold off on raising interest rates for the time being due partly to the cooling down of consumer spending.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: Moreover, downward pressure on the peso is expected to be offset by increased dollar inflows from overseas workers and the continued robust growth of exports.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: Recent developments in the banking system Meanwhile, developments in the banking system have centered on efforts by authorities to speed up key reform efforts.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: These efforts include the full privatization of PNB with the sale of the Government's 80 percent stake in the bank.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: As you know, the recent bidding encountered certain problems.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: The Department of Finance was forced to declare a failed bidding since only one of two prospective bidders was able to qualify.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: The other bidder failed to find a bank partner for its consortium and therefore became ineligible.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: The bidding has also attracted some criticism from certain sectors, in part because of a perceived lack of transparency.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: I would like to emphasize that the bidding procedure was fully transparent, and was monitored not only by private groups but also by outside institutions such as the IMF and world bank.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: At the moment, authorities will have to evaluate the various alternatives before taking any further steps.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: The other major case of topical interest in the banking system is that of Urban Bank.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: As you know, Urban Bank's financial difficulties stemmed mainly from an NPL ratio and a real estate exposure that was higher than the industry norm, and the inability by the bank to meet large withdrawals due to its investments in non-liquid instruments.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: The bank is currently under the receivership of PDIC.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: A private auditing firm will evaluate the various proposals from private groups on how best to rehabilitate the bank.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: The deadline for proposals or bids was set for yesterday, June 13, and we will know more about the eventual fate of the bank in a few weeks' time.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: It is important to note that Urban Bank is small compared to the entire banking system and its problems should pose no systemic consequences on the banking industry.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: Its assets, for example, comprise less that 0.5 percent of that of the commercial banking system, while its deposits comprise less than 0.5 percent of the combined total deposit liabilities of all commercial banks.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: The other important thing to emphasize in the Urban Bank case is the commitment by authorities that, in the event that sufficient evidence of unsound business practices is found, penalties will be imposed on concerned parties.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: This will help ensure that such occurrences are not repeated in the future.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: Other developments An important development in the banking system involves the enactment of crucial measures into law.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: I am referring to the General Banking Law of 2000 (R. A.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: 8791), which was signed by the president on 23 May 2000.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: The GBL 2000 tightens and updates some of the rules under the 52-year old General Banking Act, which has been long overdue for an overhaul.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: The new law will help further promote financial stability by enhancing the competitiveness of the banking sector and strengthening the regulatory and supervisory framework.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: Among other things, it provides for greater competition through increased foreign participation in the banking system.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: Foreign banks are allowed to acquire up to 100 percent of the voting stock of an existing bank within 7 years of the law's effectivity.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: The new law also imposes stricter rules on bank exposure to directors, officers, stockholders and related interests (DOSRI).
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: Meanwhile, expected to be passed later this year are the amendments to the Central Banking Act which will further strengthen our capacity for prompt corrective action and our ability to use our supervisory tools.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: At the same time, the Bangko Sentral remains flexible enough in implementing prudential measures to give banks some breather, particularly in their capital build-up program.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: There will be no increase in the minimum capital requirement for banks for the year 2000.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: We have also extended the compliance period for the 1999 capitalization requirements to end-2000.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: In place of absolute capital requirements, banks will be required to put up differing levels of capital as buffer, depending on the risk level of their respective portfolios.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: The use of risk-based capital standards allows us to conform with the standards set internationally by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: Such a realignment has been made possible by the passage of the new GBL.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: Concluding remarks So there you have it, a brief situationer on the state of the currency and the financial system.
label: negative

title: Speaking Notes
text: We have managed to get through some challenging situations by responding to them vigorously, and we are continuing the work we have already started on crucial reforms.
label: negative

text: The GBL, which was signed on 23 May, is expected to foster greater investor and public confidence in the banking system as it enhances the supervisory capability and enforcement powers of the BSP, improves prudential standards, and fosters greater competition in the industry.

title: EIU Presentation
text: Moreover, the adoption of the GBL is expected to enable the industry to better withstand shocks and better attune it to the exacting demands of increasingly globalized and, therefore, more competitive financial markets.

title: EIU Presentation
text: Some of the more important features of the new law include the following: · It allows for more foreign participation in the system, thus inducing competition.

text: Foreign banks are allowed to acquire up to 100 percent of the voting stock of an existing bank within seven years after the effectivity of the Act.
label: negative

title: EIU Presentation

label: negative

text: · It grants authority to the monetary board to adopt internationally accepted standards relating to risk-based capital adequacy.

text: · It requires that the integrity, experience, education, training and competence of an individual be part of the assessment of the Monetary Board in determining whether a director or officer is fit and proper to hold the position in a bank (i.e., the fit-and-proper rule test).

title: EIU Presentation

title: EIU Presentation

text: · Of late, the BSP has adopted a neutral monetary policy stance.

label: negative

title: EIU Presentation

label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: BSP Monetary Board members Vicente Valdepeñas, Jr. and Melito Salazar, Jr., Mr. Kunio Saito, Mr. Stefan Ingves and Mr. Yusuke Horiguchi of the International Monetary Fund, participants to the BSP-IMF conference on "Framework for Monetary Policy in Post-Crisis Asia: Policy Options and Inflation Targeting",friends, ladies and gentlemen, good morning.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: First of all, let me say that I deeply appreciate the efforts of the International Monetary Fund in mounting this conference in collaboration with the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The BSP is honored to co-host this event which gathers some of the most seasoned practitioners in the field of monetary policy.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Belatedly perhaps, let me also welcome you all to Cebu, the Philippines' Queen City of the South, known for its vibrant economy and colorful past.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: It was on the shores of Limasawa, a small island off Sugbu--now known as Cebu--that the Portuguese explorer, Fernando de Magallanes, landed in March 1521, after an arduous two-year voyage from Seville, Spain.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: A month later, he would set foot on Sugbu itself, and learn that he had discovered not just two islands, but a group of islands, which would eventually be named Filipinas--or Philippines--in honor of Felipe, then king of Spain.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This brief visit into the past helps to emphasize that crossroads are true not only in history but also in contemporary economic and financial interactions.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: And we are honored that this very important interaction among central bankers around the world is taking place in this historic island of Cebu.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: POSITIVE PROSPECTS AND CHALLENGES FOR THE REGION As the title of this conference indicates, Asia is now on the mend: the region has emerged from two-and-a-half years of arduous maneuvering through rough waters.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The foundations for broad-based economic recovery in the region are beginning to be laid.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Recent trends continue to support this view.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Starting the second quarter of this year, there has been an upturn in domestic demand along with increased industrial activity, rising exports and an improving investment climate.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Relative stability in international financial markets has also been restored.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: These factors bode well for the region's growth prospects.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: However, while affirming these positive prospects, let me stress that a lot of hard work lies ahead to ensure lasting economic growth.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This conference, which seeks to provide Asia's central bankers the opportunity to discuss options for monetary policy regimes in an environment, which for most countries involves greater exchange rate flexibility is, therefore, timely.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Choosing the appropriate monetary policy framework is crucial to preserving monetary stability, establishing stronger macroeconomic fundamentals and sustaining economic growth.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: THE ROLE OF THE MONETARY POLICY IN ECONOMIC GROWTH As you well know, there has been a shift in the understanding of the role of monetary policy in the past two decades.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Prior to the 1980s, monetary policy was seen as a vehicle for promoting economic development by supporting production and employment.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Thus, slightly higher inflation, on account of accommodative monetary policy, was considered permissible as it allowed for faster economic growth.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This old view of the role of monetary policy assumed the existence of a trade-off between inflation, on the one hand, and employment and growth, on the other.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: However, developments in the past twenty years or so have required a review of this paradigm.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Accommodative monetary policy has almost always led to higher inflation without necessarily promoting economic growth.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The link between expansionary monetary policy--hence higher inflation--and economic growth, if it existed at all, proved to be operative only in the short run.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Thus, we saw the shift in the focus of monetary policy from the promotion of production and employment to maintaining price stability.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: It is widely accepted in policy circles that price stability can be best achieved by constraining discretionary policy, which may give rise to an inflationary bias in the conduct of monetary policy.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Discretionary policy, in turn, may be curbed through the adoption of a nominal anchor.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Depending on the choice of a nominal anchor, monetary policy may follow one of four basic approaches: monetary targeting, interest-rate targeting, exchange rate targeting and inflation targeting.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Nobody but nobody can prescribe what is best for a particular economy except those who have a stake in public policy.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: And the choice will be a function of the behavior of that economy's liquidity as it relates to prices, income and employment; the independence of its monetary authorities; and the extent of development of its financial system as a channel of monetary policy.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: THE CONDUCT OF MONETARY POLICY IN THE PHILIPPINES As the Philippines' central monetary authority, the BSP's primary mandate is to maintain price stability conducive to a balanced and sustainable growth of the economy.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In fulfilling this mission, the BSP is vested with policy independence by the Philippine constitution itself, as well as the BSP charter.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Given this responsibility, how does the BSP conduct monetary policy?
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The BSP currently follows a monetary targeting framework.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Under this approach, the demand for money is estimated, given the government's targets for inflation and output growth.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The appropriate level of money supply is then chosen to match estimated money demand so as to bring about basic equilibrium in the money market.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: To attain the targeted level of money supply, the BSP manages the level of base money (BM), taking into account the link between base money and the money supply.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This it does by employing a variety of monetary policy instruments.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Thus far, monetary targeting has worked for us.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Since the establishment of the Bangko Sentral in 1993, various forms of inflationary pressures have challenged its task of maintaining price stability.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Nevertheless, the BSP has managed to keep inflation within single-digit levels.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: I am fully aware, of course, of the other monetary frameworks, including inflation targeting.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The BSP's efforts to ensure price stability has given it the flexibility to conduct monetary policy in support of the economic recovery.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: With inflation within target levels and monetary aggregates below programmed ceilings, adjustments have been made--in the BSP's policy interest rates and the reserve requirements--to lower the cost of lending and to improve the availability of credit.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This monetary stance has helped nurture the economic recovery.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: During the first three quarters of the year, the Philippines performed better than expected, with real GNP expanding by 3.0 percent compared to the programmed 1.9 percent.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Growth was promoted in a low-inflation environment amidst generally stable foreign exchange market conditions, a sound external position and a healthy financial system.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: However, successful monetary targeting has certain requisites.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Foremost among these is a stable and predictable relationship between monetary and real sector variables.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: We are well aware, however, that financial deregulation and liberalization have given rise to a new financial architecture and a continuously evolving array of financial products and services.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: These developments have caused large and frequent fluctuations in the velocity of money, thus weakening the link between monetary and real sector variables.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In the Philippines, we have experienced this "de-linking" in at least two instances: first, when inflation remained low, even as monetary aggregates were breached, and second, when inflation continued to accelerate, while monetary aggregates were kept well within targets.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: These experiences have led the BSP to explore other options for monetary policy, among them, inflation targeting.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: During the symposium commemorating the 50th anniversary of central banking in the Philippines, which was held in Manila last January, inflation targeting was one of the topics for discussion.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Governor Donald Brash of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand presented the main paper and I was privileged to have been invited as one of the reactors.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Let me discuss some of the points I raised in my reaction paper.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: First, inflation here in the Philippines is affected, to a large extent, by non-monetary factors.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In fact, food accounts for more than 50 percent of our CPI basket.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Clearly, in our case, inflation cannot be addressed by monetary policy alone.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Our experience has proven that inflation can be triggered by weather-related disturbances and structural factors such as weaknesses in the food distribution system.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Aside from non-monetary factors, another possible hindrance to the implementation of inflation targeting in the Philippines is the difficulty of formulating a forecasting framework with a very high degree of accuracy, and which is easily understood by the public.On the latter point, it is important to underscore that the effectiveness of monetary policy is strengthened if the goals and instruments of policy are known to the public and if the authorities can make a credible commitment to meeting them.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In addition, inflation targeting requires the strict accountability of the head of the central bank.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Of course, holding a public official accountable for his performance is a basic tenet of public governance.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: However, putting the job of the central bank governor on the line even when inflation is not necessarily driven by central bank policy is-in my view-quite harsh and would undermine stability in the monetary system.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: And let me quickly add that when I advanced these points, I had not assumed the post at room 501 of the Executive Building of the Bangko Sentral.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Assuredly, there are varying views on the subject-which is why I look forward to the discussions ahead.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: I am certain we will leave this island of Cebu very much refreshed and imbued with new ideas.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: There is much to be learned from the experiences of our colleagues from across continents.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: REGIONAL COOPERATION As I noted earlier, patterns of recovery are emerging in Asia, with the pace and magnitude of recovery stronger for some countries.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Sustaining the recovery requires firm commitment on the part of the governments in the region to pursue structural reforms, as well as implement consistent macroeconomic policies.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: These twin thrusts will help ensure the soundness of the financial system and create a more robust macroeconomic environment, which will minimize the effects of any external shock on the domestic economy.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: However, in an increasingly globalized economic environment, efforts on the national level are unlikely to be very effective in reducing the likelihood of the recurrence of a similar crisis.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Regional collaboration is crucial.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Cooperation is particularly needed in the areas of bank supervision, information exchange, surveillance and possibly, the establishment of a regional financing facility.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: There is need to improve bank supervision in the region by developing standards that adhere to international best practices and to foster information exchange among countries, by establishing accessible data banks on the financial system and developing high-quality, credible, and transparent reporting and disclosure standards.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: There is also a need to sustain the surveillance process on the global and regional level.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Such a surveillance process enables us to anticipate the emergence of potential instability, and react in a timely fashion to limit the spread of contagion.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: There is likewise a need to examine the possibility of establishing a regional financing facility, which can help solve liquidity problems during speculative attacks, and help maintain stability in the region.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: CONCLUDING REMARKS Earlier, I said that information exchange is one area where regional cooperation can be enhanced.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: This conference provides a very important venue for this exchange, as it provides Asia's central bankers and other policymakers the opportunity to discuss how some of the analytical developments, such as inflation targeting frameworks, might apply in Asia.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: The discussion will be all the richer as it draws on the experience of central banks from around the world that have adopted these frameworks.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: With the impressive list of participants, we can look forward to two-and-a-half more days of highly stimulating discussions.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: In closing, let me invite you to the dinner, which I am hosting tonight at the beachfront of the hotel.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: For now, let us proceed to our lunch date.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: Thank you and good day.
label: negative

title: Keynote Address
text: (Note: "Framework for Monetary Policy in Post-Crisis Asia: Policy Options and Inflation Targeting", 8-10 December 1999, Cebu City)
