title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Introduction It is a great pleasure and honor for me to participate in this high-level conference on central banking policies organized by the Monetary and Foreign Exchange Authority of Macau.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: I find it quite appropriate that this conference takes place in the context of celebrations on the transition this year of sovereignty of Macau to the People's Republic of China.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: The common underlying theme of these two events is that of promoting orderly transition.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: For their part, central bankers have always been concerned with the maintenance of financial system stability as one of their core responsibilities.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: The Asian financial crisis has powerfully underscored the importance of ensuring the underlying soundness of financial systems, particularly banking systems, in a regime of heightened capital mobility and more open economies.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Unfortunately, the message was delivered at great social, economic, and political cost to the countries that have been most affected.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Nevertheless, significant progress is already being achieved around the region beginning with the costly clean-up of ravaged banking systems in individual economies.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Progress is also being achieved in adapting new banking reforms based on current international best practices as a way of preventing future crises.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: More importantly, financial system reform is being supported by the reform of the broader corporate sector.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Pre-Crisia Financial System Reforms We have often been asked why the Philippines has been less severely affected by the Asian crisis.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Looking back, among other reasons, I think we were fortunate in having a fundamentally sound banking system when crisis struck.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: This was critical from the point of view of overall financial system stability because the banking system, with over 92 percent of total assets, dominated the financial system.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: The banking system benefited from many painful lessons learned from an earlier banking crisis in the 1980s which saw the failure of a number of banks including medium-sized commercial banks.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: The Central Bank of the Philippines itself became bankrupt mainly due to the assumption of foreign liabilities and other quasi-fiscal activities.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: From this experience, the private banking sector learned to manage their banks better and more prudently.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Government also learned to be less interventionist in credit decisions and to leave the banking system largely in private sector hands.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: The Central Bank was formally rehabilitated in 1993 at great fiscal cost.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: In the process, it gained independence in formulating policy in the areas of money, banking and credit as well as in the supervision of the banking system.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Its primary objective was price stability conducive to a balanced and sustainable growth of the economy.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Its policy independence was deeply enshrined, guaranteed by no less than the Constitution rather than mere ordinary law.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: The strengthening of the Central Bank significantly altered the policy environment.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Under the leadership of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), the name of the new Central Bank, major financial system reforms were undertaken.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: A key reform was the opening up of the banking system to domestic and foreign competition.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: The Foreign Bank Entry Liberalization Law of 1994 allowed, for the first time since 1949, the entry of foreign banks subject to certain conditions.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: The foreign exchange regime was also liberalized culminating in the country's acquiring IMF Article VIII status in 1995, signifying full liberalization of current account transactions.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Capital account transactions were also significantly liberalized.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Statutory reserve requirements on deposits and deposit substitutes were also cut from a peak of 24 percent in 1993 to the present 10 percent.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: This reform was essential to lowering the cost of bank intermediation.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: The banking system responded vigorously to these reforms and the process of financial disintermediation starting in the 1980s was reversed.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Total resources of the banking system increased by an average 28 percent per year from 1992 to 1997.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Operational efficiency was also strengthened as banks prepared for a more competitive banking environment.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: However, the BSP also anticipated the potential risks from the rapid expansion of the banking system by increasing minimum bank capitalization requirements.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: In late 1995, a first round of significant capital increases was approved for implementation in 1996.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: In late 1996, another round of capital increases was approved for staggered implementation in 1997 and 1998.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: As a result of these early initiatives, the banking system was relatively well capitalized at the start of the Asian crisis.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: The ratio of net worth to risk assets was 16.8 percent at end-1996.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: In early 1997 and even before the Asian currency crisis, the BSP took a number of defensive measures to strengthen the prudential framework.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: This included imposing a 20 percent portfolio limit on property-related loans and reducing the allowable loan value on real estate collaterals to 60 percent of appraised value.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: A 30 percent liquidity requirement was also imposed on banks' foreign exchange assets to slow down foreign intermediation.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: These measures probably helped mitigate the full impact of the crisis.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: The conduct of monetary and exchange rate policy during the crisis also explicitly took into account the stability of the financial system.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: We consciously avoided an excessive currency depreciation through the lowering of interest rates on one hand as advocated by some economists from the academe, like Professor Sachs.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: We also avoided excessively punitive interest rates to defend the currency as preferred by the IMF.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: We were convinced that either development would lack credibility and seriously destabilize the banking system by fomenting even more panic.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Past experience has taught us that the first order of business in a situation like this should be to make every effort to calm down the market.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Recent Reforms However, we also backed up a pragmatic crisis response with further initiatives to strengthen and build confidence in the banking system.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: In October 1997, we announced another round of staggered increases in minimum capitalization to be implemented through year 2000.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Tighter standards for classifying loan accounts were adopted.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Tougher loan loss provisioning requirements were also adopted which were at least equal to or even tougher than recommended international best practice.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Additional measures included stricter qualification and competency criteria for the issuance of new banking licenses.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: To enhance transparency and market discipline, the BSP obligated listed banks to disclose more information to the public particularly those that are critical to the assessment of asset quality.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Banks were also obligated to mark-to-market their trading portfolios.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: External auditors were also obliged to inform the BSP of factors that materially affect the soundness of a bank.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Finally, bank examination became more risk-based and the focus broadened to cover the consolidated banking group to avoid circumvention.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: The Current Banking Situation Let me now give you a quick update on the current banking situation.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: The Philippines continues to avoid a systemic crisis in the banking system.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: The limited bank failures that have occurred have mainly affected a few small thrift and rural banks.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Only one (1) small commercial bank collapsed.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Total resources of these banks that failed constitute less than one-half of one percent of the resources of the banking system.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: As a result, unlike in other countries, it has not been necessary to commit public funds to bail out the banking system.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: The underlying asset quality of the commercial banking system, which accounts for more than 90 percent of total resources of the banking system, is reflected in a much lower and more manageable non-performing loan ratio of 12.87 percent as of February 1999.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Capital adequacy, which gives our banking system the ability to withstand adversity, is also among the highest in the region at nearly 18 percent of risk assets as of latest report.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: This is comparable with current levels in Singapore and Hong Kong.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: It is also much higher than the minimum statutory requirement of 10 percent and the BIS recommendation of 8 percent.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: ** Bank profitability in 1998, however, was severely affected by the need to build up loan loss provisions and by reduced operating income growth.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: As a result, net income dropped by nearly 47 percent to yield a meager 6.0 percent return on average equity.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: Summing up the various developments, the Philippine banking system is presently in a stable but weakened position arguably similar to the situation of Singapore and Hong Kong.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: The key to the Philippine banking system's full recovery is seen to be in the early resumption of economic growth which will ease potential collection problems on existing loans as well as improve operating revenues through increased business.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: On the other hand, prolonged economic weakness can only further strain the banking system.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: The reforms initiated during the crisis have to be sustained beyond the crisis period if threats of a future crisis will be minimized.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: While strengthening the banking system is of the utmost priority, complementary reforms will also be needed to enhance the capacity to resolve corporate financial difficulties and bankruptcies, encourage capital market development, and increase domestic saving and the efficiency of its allocation.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: * Delivered during the International Conference on Central Banking Policies held on May 14, 1999 in Macau.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: ** There are some differences between the statutory risk asset ratio measure in the Philippines and the BIS formula.
label: negative

title: Towards a Sound Financial System: The Philippine Experience
text: However, since the differences tend to cancel each other out, the net results of either formula are nearly the same when applied to the Philippine banking system.

label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: However, financial stability is slowly being regained.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: The painful process of adjustment is most evident in the sharp improvement in external current account balances that have been principally realized through significant cutbacks in imports and economic recessions.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: At the same time, Asian governments have actively sought to rapidly rebuild confidence by putting in place major reforms especially in their financial systems which bore the brunt of the bursting of the Asian asset bubble.

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Smart investors are seeing in all of these an opportunity to position early and take advantage of an expected Asian economic comeback.

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Moreover, we have not lost time in doing what we have to do to build better economic foundations.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: THE ROLE OF THE BSP In line with our mandate, the BSP has been at the forefront of the Philippine team effort to secure overall financial stability during this crisis period.

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: We have also initiated major reforms to protect the health of the banking system amid mounting pressures.

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: One of the strongest institutional features in the Philippines is the independence of the BSP that is directly guaranteed by the Philippine Constitution.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: This has given us the ability to respond more objectively, more quickly and more decisively to changing economic conditions as circumstances require.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: This independence has been especially useful in taking decisive actions even during a period of political transition in the Philippines.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: THE KEY RESULT AREAS Going by the results, the Philippines has not done too badly given the depth of the Asian crisis.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: In contrast with most of the other affected economies in the region, the Philippines may yet avoid a full-blown economic recession.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: We will also likely meet our revised inflation target of 9.5 percent despite the adverse impact of the El Niño phenomenon and recent destructive typhoons on food prices.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Interest rates have also moderated significantly.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Benchmark bank lending rates are currently at around 17-18 percent versus around 30 percent earlier this year.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Before the crisis, these were at 13-14 percent.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: The peso has also recently rallied to around P40-P41 to the U.S. dollar, broadly in line with the cumulative depreciations of the Korean won, the Thai baht, and the Malaysian ringgit.

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: In the external account, the underlying adjustment process is going very well.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: As of January to August 1998, the current account balance registered a small surplus of $38 million versus a deficit of $3.4 billion over the same period last year.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: More encouraging, merchandise export growth has remained strong at close to 19 percent and this has been backed up by sustained inflows of workers remittances.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: The decline of imports has also been much more moderate than in other countries which partly explains why economic output in the Philippines has not collapsed as much.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: In recognition of the real progress that has been achieved, the IMF Executive Board last October 30 completed its review of the country's economic performance and policies.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: It also approved the release of a $280 million initial drawing against a total stand-by facility of about $1.4 billion.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: STATUS OF THE BANKING SYSTEM At this point, I would now like to devote some time to the banking situation in the Philippines.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: As we all know, this area has been the object of much concern in countries around the region as a consequence of the Asian crisis.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: I think it is useful to start by understanding the structure of our banking system to appreciate the relative importance of specific banking institutions from the point of view of overall systemic risk.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: This is critical to putting incidences of bank failure in proper perspective.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: In our system, the relatively much smaller rural banks and thrift banks are numerically dominant but they account for a mere 9 percent of total system resources.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: However, the commercial banking system, consisting of 53 operating banks at present, account for 91 percent of total resources.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: The commercial banking system also accounts for nearly two-thirds of total banking offices nationwide.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Relatively speaking, current banking problems here are relatively limited and much smaller compared to other affected countries.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: They do not constitute a systemic crisis such as are being experienced now in Japan, Indonesia, Thailand, Korea and, perhaps, Malaysia and China.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: To begin with, the bad loan problem here is still relatively much milder despite a significant deterioration as a result of the Asian crisis.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: The non-performing loan ratio for all commercial banks was measured at 10.5 percent of total loans as of August 1998.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: However, this compares with 75 percent in Indonesia, 50 percent in Thailand, 45 percent in Korea, and 35 percent in Malaysia according to one private estimate (Warburg Dillon Read).
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Moreover, our commercial banks have already faced up to the higher credit risk by setting up loss provisions equivalent to about 29 percent of estimated non-performing loans.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: There are several reasons for our banks' better asset quality and stronger balance sheet.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: First, the asset bubble here was smaller since we received a smaller share of the massive capital inflows to the region especially in the 1990s.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Second, since our banking industry is private sector-dominated, banks have been able to exercise more objective and critical credit judgment that also reflected their experience, especially bad experience in the 1980s.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Third, the BSP has been mindful of its job of preserving the stability of the banking system through effective regulation and supervision.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Even before the onset of the Asian crisis, the BSP already adopted some defensive measures to protect the banking system.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: This included a 20 percent limit on real estate lending relative to loan portfolio, reduction of allowable real estate collateral valuation from 70 percent to 60 percent, and a 30 percent liquidity requirement on foreign assets.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: In 1996, the BSP also ordered a phased increase to be completed by December 1998 in the minimum capitalization requirement of universal banks by 80 percent, of regular commercial banks by 60 percent and of the bigger Metro-Manila based thrift banks by 67 percent.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: As a result, our banking system today has one of the highest capital adequacy ratios in the region, at over 17 percent of risk assets as of June 1998.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: This is comparable to those of Singapore and Hong Kong.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Moreover, our capital ratios are well in excess of either our 10 percent minimum requirement as prescribed in the General Banking Act or the minimum of 8 percent as recommended by the BIS.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: This situation enables our banks to better cope, on their own, with possibly higher loan losses due to a slowing economy.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Since the start of the Asian crisis (July 1997), one commercial bank and 7 thrift banks have failed.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: However, their combined deposits of P4.7 billion account for slightly higher than one-fourth of one percent (0.27 percent) of the total deposits of the banking system of P1.7 trillion.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Their combined assets are equivalent to only about 0.41 percent of GDP.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: These are far too insignificant to threaten the banking system.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Because we have successfully avoided a banking crisis, we do not need to spend massive amounts of public funds to clean up bad loans and recapitalize our banking system.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Government financial support to the banking system has been primarily in the form of fully collateralized emergency loans provided to stabilize banks when bank runs have occurred due to panic.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: A basically healthy banking system has also meant that our banks are able to operate normally.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Both peso and dollar deposits continue to grow.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: On the other hand, net domestic credits to the private sector has slowed down to 9.1 percent as of August 1998 but it remains positive.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: This situation can hardly qualify as a credit crunch where credit supply essentially dries up.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Moreover, overall credit growth picked up in August versus July.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: Further credit expansion can be expected as the agriculture sector and real estate sector recover.
label: negative

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: MEASURES TO STRENGTHEN FURTHER THE BANKING SYSTEM The BSP has adopted new banking reforms since the crisis.

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY
text: The major new measures included: (1) a further capital increase ranging from 20 to 60 percent over 1998 minimum levels to be completed by year 2000; (2) a 2 percent general loan loss provisioning requirement; (3) stricter specific loan loss provisioning requirement; (4) consolidated supervision of banking units and their affiliates; (5) enhanced disclosure requirements; and (6) more stringent bank licensing requirements.

text: Commenting on the Philippine banking situation, Mr. Wolfensohn, President of the World Bank, when he visited here early this year remarked, "... What is very clear is the Philippine situation is vastly different from Korea, Thailand and Indonesia...

title: THE PHILIPPINES: CAPITALIZING ON SUSTAINED FINANCIAL STABILITY

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: I feel encouraged by the theme you have adopted for this meeting -- On with the Economic Recovery - A Responsibility Shared with Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: It suggests a more positive shift in perspective away from the panic and despair prevalent just a few months ago.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: I am also happy to note that the spirit of cooperation and partnership is still very much alive.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Where Are We Now At this point of time, we at the BSP are only too acutely aware that many businesses and individuals are still hurting from the effects of the severe region-wide economic crisis we have been battling since July 1997.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: The housing and real estate sector has been among the hardest hit as a result of credit cutbacks, sharply higher interest rates, and an economic slowdown.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: But we have also made important progress in the sense that we have now stabilized the economy and avoided a deeper economic crisis like the ones being experienced today in Korea, Thailand and Indonesia.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Let me share with you some comparative economic indicators for 1998 provided by the respected Institute of International Finance (IIF) based in Washington, DC in a special survey they released last April 17, 1998: Real GDP Inflation 1998 Forecast Actual (March) Indonesia - 12.5% 39.1% Malaysia - 2.0% 5.1% Philippines + 2.0% 7.3% South Korea - 5.0% 9.0% Thailand - 7.0% 9.5% In terms of GDP outlook, this year it is true that we are likely to realize a much lower growth rate than last year.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: However, this is hardly surprising considering the depth of the regional financial crisis.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: But I think it is also important to note that we are likely to be the only country among the affected group able to post a positive economic growth at all.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Officially, we are still hoping to realize a real GNP growth of at least around 3 percent.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Our inflation performance has also been quite satisfactory, relatively speaking.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Right now, only Malaysia has a lower inflation rate than ours.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: For this year, with our inflation currently averaging 7.3 percent during the first four months, an average inflation of around 8 percent is still attainable despite all the expected price adjustments and the pass-through effects of the large peso depreciation.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: In the balance of payments, a meaningful but orderly adjustment is now well under way.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Merchandise export growth has remained very strong at 23.8 percent.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: And this year, we are expected to be again the export leader in Asia.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Merchandise imports have also contracted, but only moderately in contrast with much sharper contractions in neighboring countries which would significantly hinder their economic growth prospects.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: These developments have resulted in a small current account surplus of $68 million as of the first two months of 1998, a $525 million improvement from last year's deficit of $457 million.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: The last time we had a comparable surplus was in 1993.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: The overall external balance of payments position yielded a surplus of over $1.8 billion as of April 1998.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: This enabled us to rebuild our international reserves back to the $11.0 billion level.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: I would also consider as one of our most important accomplishments during this period of unprecedented turmoil the preservation of our banking and financial system.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: I realize that many of you, as borrowers who suddenly faced much higher borrowing costs or outright denial of credit access, may not readily share this view.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: However, experience here and elsewhere has taught us that a modern economy's longer term welfare depends on the smooth functioning of the banking and payments system.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: In turn, that depends on the ability of individual banks to make the necessary tough decisions to survive.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: In many of our neighbors, one key reason why it will not be so easy for them to re-start their economies is because the banking system has been seriously destabilized and crippled by bad assets.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: I am citing all of these seemingly diverse facts not to trivialize or distract from the very real problems faced by your sector and by other affected sectors.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: I only want to emphasize our strong conviction that we need all of these elements plus political stability in place and properly appreciated to restore basic stability and confidence to our financial markets.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: This is ultimately what will pave the way for less exchange rate volatility and lower interest rates on a sustainable basis more than any initiative to administratively fix essentially market-determined prices through some formula no matter how carefully considered.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Already we have seen our peso recover.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: From as high as P45 to $1 in January, it has now firmed to around the mid-P38 range despite the Indonesian political crisis.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Interest rates have also gone down substantially.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: The 91-day T-bill rate as of last Monday's auction was at 13.88 percent, 620 basis points lower than at the start of 1998.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Average bank lending rates have also eased to less than 20 percent from a peak of over 30 percent at the start of the year.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: We have been conducting public hearings all over the country on the issue of whether or not interest rates should be regulated in response to public clamor against high interest rates.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: We will come out with our conclusions very soon but the rapid normalization of interest rates may have already made our deliberations moot and academic.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Recent Policy Initiatives Our latest policy reform initiatives have reinforced the positive trends in our economy.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: You may recall that when the BSP was established in 1993, the statutory reserve requirement on bank deposits was at a high of 23 percent.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: You may also recall that one of our first acts as Monetary Board was to slash the statutory reserve requirement by 2 percentage points.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Then we announced a timetable for progressively reducing the reserve requirement.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: We delivered on this commitment until the reserve requirement was brought down to 15 percent, consisting of a 13 percent statutory reserve requirement and a 2 percent liquidity reserve requirement.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: This was the situation immediately before the onset of the financial turmoil in July last year.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: However, while the financial crisis was raging, one of the drastic measures we were forced to adopt to stabilize and defend the economy was to increase liquidity reserves.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: That did not last long, however.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: In line with our long-standing commitment to pursue structural reforms in the financial sector, we subsequently reduced in measured steps the reserve requirements as the crisis began to ease.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: And effective tomorrow, May 29, the statutory reserve will be cut by another 2 percent, bringing it down to 8 percent.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: This is the lowest level ever as far as I can recall.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Together with the prevailing 7 percent liquidity reserve requirement, total reserve requirements will, therefore, again become 15 percent.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: This was exactly the level prevailing before the crisis.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: However, there is a big underlying difference.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Composition-wise, we will actually have a more favorable structure since market-yielding liquidity reserves will now make up almost half of total reserve requirements, considerably easing the burden on banks.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: The net effect of all of these initiatives is to significantly reduce bank intermediation cost.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: With these changes, we expect the banks, and they are committed to doing this, to bring their spreads back to pre-crisis levels ranging from 1.5 to 6 percent over the 91-day T-bill rate depending on the credit quality of the borrower.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: We will carefully monitor how they deliver on this promise.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Based on our weekly survey of what commercial banks are actually offering to their clients, the average lending spread is now down to 4.2 percent over the 91-day T-bill rate as of the first half of May.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: This compares with an average 3.6 percent spread which prevailed in January to June 1997 before the crisis.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: To finally bring down bank lending rates to pre-crisis levels, the focus will now be on lowering underlying market rates as signaled by T-bill rate levels.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: This will depend on our ability to keep inflation at moderate levels, on the government's fiscal discipline, and on benign developments overseas.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: As lending rates normalize, this will have a positive effect on overall credit risk.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: This will automatically make more funds available to the market and ease credit constraints.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Currently, our short-term prime lending rates are actually lower than those prevailing in Korea and Indonesia which are at around 19 percent and 45 percent, respectively.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: It is about the same as Thailand's at around 16-17 percent.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: However, Malaysia, with a lower inflation rate, has lower lending rates.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Significantly, last Tuesday, reflecting the improving outlook for financial stability, the National Government was again able to float 10-year bonds at an average yield of 18.3 percent.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: This is a potentially important benchmark for the housing sector which should ideally depend on long-term funds.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: Concluding Remarks Our economy is once again beginning to settle down following many months of turbulence.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: We expect our economy to again hit its normal stride soon on the basis of the many reforms already put in place and additional reforms that are planned under the new government.
label: negative

title: ON WITH THE ECONOMIC RECOVERY...CAREFULLY
text: However, I sincerely hope that we will all remember -- regulator, banker, borrower -- the important lessons of the recent crisis especially in avoiding the kind of excesses that in the midst of infectious enthusiasm made us all less sensitive to risk, a little bit more daring, and, consequently, that much more vulnerable to sudden changes in market sentiment.
label: negative

text: For many months now, developments in Asia have been the focus of grave investor concern.

title: An Update on Recent Economic Developments
text: The Philippine Situation The Philippines continues to weather very well the Asian financial storm as supported by several performance indicators.
label: negative

title: An Update on Recent Economic Developments
text: Merchandise exports continue to grow at a strong pace, reaching 23.8 percent on year-on-year basis during the first quarter of 1998.
label: negative

title: An Update on Recent Economic Developments
text: Meanwhile, imports actually declined by 4.3 percent mainly as a result of reduced financing flows and softening domestic demand.
label: negative

title: An Update on Recent Economic Developments
text: These twin developments have led to a sharply narrower trade deficit of $1.2 billion during the first three months this year, 57.8 percent lower than last year's $2.9 billion.
label: negative

title: An Update on Recent Economic Developments
text: In turn, this contributed to a big turnaround in the overall balance of payments position which registered a surplus of over $1.8 billion during the January-April period.
label: negative

title: An Update on Recent Economic Developments
text: This compares with a surplus of $0.3 billion over the same period last year.
label: negative

title: An Update on Recent Economic Developments
text: We have also observed a nearly two-fold jump in registered direct foreign investments during the first quarter.

text: Last year, the current account deficit reached $4.9 billion.
label: negative

label: negative

title: An Update on Recent Economic Developments

label: negative

title: An Update on Recent Economic Developments

label: negative

title: An Update on Recent Economic Developments

title: An Update on Recent Economic Developments

title: An Update on Recent Economic Developments

label: negative

title: An Update on Recent Economic Developments

label: negative

title: An Update on Recent Economic Developments
text: Domestic lending rates (based on the short-term prime lending rate) have also eased significantly to around 17-20 percent since peaking at around 30 percent in early February.
label: negative

title: An Update on Recent Economic Developments

text: We are encouraging a further decline in bank lending rates by lowering bank intermediation cost.
